ប្រការ៧ .- រង្វង់ជំហោងដៃ
១-	រង្វង់ជំហោងដៃ គឺជារង្វង់នៃតួលេខសូចនាករហិរញ្ញវត្ថុពាក់ព័ន្ធ (ថ្លៃ ឬកម្រិតចំណេញ) ដែលទទួលបានពីការអនុវត្តវិធីសាស្ត្រផ្ទេរថ្លៃដូចមានចែងក្នុងប្រការ៩ ដល់ប្រការ១៣ នៃប្រកាសនេះ ដែលបានមកពីប្រតិបត្តិការគ្មានការរៀបចំអាចធៀបបានទៅនឹងប្រតិបត្តិការមានការរៀបចំដោយផ្អែកទៅលើការវិភាគលើភាពដែលអាចធៀបបានដូចមានចែងក្នុងប្រការ៦ នៃប្រកាសនេះ។
២-	ប្រតិបត្តិការមានការរៀបចំនឹងមិនត្រូវបានធ្វើនិយ័តកម្មទេ ប្រសិនបើសូចនាករហិរញ្ញវត្ថុពាក់ព័ន្ធដែលបានមកពីប្រតិបត្តិការមានការរៀបចំ ត្រូវបានធ្វើតេស្តតាមវិធីសាស្ត្រផ្ទេរថ្លៃត្រឹមត្រូវ ដែលស្ថិតនៅក្នុងរង្វង់ជំហោងដៃ។ ផ្ទុយទៅវិញ សូចនាករហិរញ្ញវត្ថុនៅក្នុងប្រតិបត្តិការមានការរៀបចំដែលស្ថិតនៅក្រៅរង្វង់ជំហោងដៃ នឹងត្រូវធ្វើនិយ័តកម្មតាមមេដ្យានរបស់រង្វង់ជំហោងដៃវិញតែក្នុងករណីដែលមិនធ្វើឱ្យថយចុះឬបាត់បង់ប្រាក់ពន្ធប៉ុណ្ណោះ។
ជំពូកទី២
វិធីសាស្ត្របែងចែកចំណូលចំណាយក្នុងចំណោមបុគ្គលទាក់ទិន
ប្រការ៨ .- វិធីសាស្ត្របែងចែកចំណូលចំណាយក្នុងចំណោមបុគ្គលទាក់ទិន
១-	ដើម្បីបែងចែកចំណូលចំណាយក្នុងចំណោមបុគ្គលទាក់ទិនក្រោមគោលការណ៍ជំហោងដៃ អ្នកជាប់ពន្ធអាចប្រើប្រាស់វិធីមួយឬច្រើនដូចខាងក្រោម៖
ក-	វិធីថ្លៃគ្មានការរៀបចំអាចធៀបបាន-ថគធ. (Comparable Uncontrolled Price-CUP)។
ខ-	វិធីថ្លៃផ្គត់ផ្គង់បន្ត-ថផប. (Resale Price Method-RPM)។
គ-	វិធីបន្ថែមលើថ្លៃដើម-បថដ. (Cost-Plus Method-CPM)។
ឃ-វិធីកម្រិតចំណេញសុទ្ធនៃប្រតិបត្តិការ-កចស. (Transactional Net Margin Method-TNMM)។
ង-	វិធីញែកចំណេញ-ញច. (Profit Split Method-PS)។
២-	អ្នកជាប់ពន្ធត្រូវបានតម្រូវឱ្យរៀបចំ និងផ្ដល់ភស្តុតាងនិងឯកសារគាំទ្រសម្រាប់វិធីដែលបានជ្រើសរើសយក មកប្រើ។ ក្នុងករណីចាំបាច់ រដ្ឋបាលសារពើពន្ធមានសិទ្ធិណែនាំនិងកំណត់ឱ្យអ្នកជាប់ពន្ធប្រើប្រាស់វិធីណាមួយដែល សមស្របនឹងស្ថានភាពជាក់ស្តែងរបស់អ្នកជាប់ពន្ធ។
ប្រការ៩ .- វិធីថ្លៃគ្មានការរៀបចំអាចធៀបបាន (ថគធ.)
១-	វិធី ថគធ. គឺជាការប្រៀបធៀបរវាងថ្លៃដែលត្រូវបានកំណត់លើការផ្ទេរទំនិញ សេវា ឬទ្រព្យ នៅក្នុងប្រតិបត្តិការមានការរៀបចំ ទៅនឹងថ្លៃដែលត្រូវបានកំណត់លើការផ្ទេរទំនិញ សេវា ឬទ្រព្យ នៅក្នុងប្រតិបត្តិការគ្មានការរៀបចំនៅក្នុងកាលៈទេសៈប្រហាក់ប្រហែលគ្នា។ វិធីនេះសមស្របនៅក្នុងស្ថានភាពដែលទំនិញ សេវា ឬទ្រព្យ អាចប្រៀបធៀបគ្នាបាន ឬក្នុងស្ថានភាពដែលការធ្វើនិយ័តកម្មសមហេតុផលអាចត្រូវបានធ្វើឡើងដើម្បីបញ្ជាក់ថាថ្លៃទំនិញ សេវា ឬទ្រព្យទាំងនោះ មានឬគ្មានភាពសមស្រប។ ក្នុងករណី ទំនិញ សេវា ឬទ្រព្យ មានភាពខុសគ្នាជាសារវន្តដែលនាំឱ្យមិនអាចធ្វើនិយ័តកម្មបាន ឬមិនអាចផ្ដល់នូវការវាស់វែងសមស្របសម្រាប់ការកំណត់ថ្លៃជំហោងដៃ វិធីផ្សេងទៀតអាចត្រូវបានយកមកប្រើប្រាស់។
២-	ការវិភាគលើភាពដែលអាចធៀបបាន៖
ក-	ដើម្បីធ្វើការកំណត់ថ្លៃផ្ទេរ សហគ្រាសដែលប្រើប្រាស់វិធី ថគធ. ជាដំបូង ត្រូវកំណត់ឱ្យឃើញភាពខុសគ្នារវាងទំនិញឬសេវារបស់ខ្លួនទៅនឹងទំនិញឬសេវារបស់សហគ្រាសឯករាជ្យ ហើយបន្ទាប់មកទៀត ត្រូវកំណត់នូវភាពខុសគ្នាដែលមានផលប៉ះពាល់ជាសារវន្តទៅលើថ្លៃ។ ប្រសិនបើមានភាពខុសគ្នាជាសារវន្ត ត្រូវធ្វើនិយ័តកម្មឱ្យបានសមស្របទៅតាមថ្លៃទំនិញឬសេវាដែលបានផ្គត់ផ្គង់ដោយសហគ្រាសឯករាជ្យ។
ខ-	ក្នុងការវិភាគលើភាពដែលអាចធៀបបាននៅក្រោមវិធី ថគធ. ត្រូវពិចារណាលើកត្តាមួយចំនួនដូចខាងក្រោម៖
-	លក្ខណៈទំនិញ ដូចជា ទ្រង់ទ្រាយ និងគុណភាព 
-	ចរិតនិងទំហំនៃសេវាដែលបានផ្គត់ផ្គង់
-	ទំនិញដែលបានផ្គត់ផ្គង់ត្រូវបានប្រៀបធៀបនៅត្រង់ចំណុចដូចគ្នានៃខ្សែច្រវាក់ផលិតកម្ម 
-	លក្ខណៈដោយឡែករបស់ផលិតផលក្រោមទម្រង់ជាទ្រព្យអរូបី ដូចជា ម៉ាកឬពាណិជ្ជនាម គំរូប្លង់ ជាដើម... 
-	ទំហំនៃការផ្គត់ផ្គង់ ប្រសិនបើមានផលប៉ះពាល់ទៅលើថ្លៃ
-	ពេលវេលានៃការផ្គត់ផ្គង់ ប្រសិនបើមានផលប៉ះពាល់ទៅលើថ្លៃដោយសារការប្រែប្រួលនៃរដូវកាល ឬការផ្លាស់ប្តូរដទៃទៀតនៃលក្ខខណ្ឌទីផ្សារ 
-	ចំណាយលើការដឹកជញ្ជូន ការវេចខ្ចប់ ការស្វែងរកទីផ្សារ ការផ្សាយពាណិជ្ជកម្ម និងការធានា ប្រសិនបើចំណាយទាំងនោះត្រូវបានដាក់បញ្ចូលទៅក្នុងកិច្ចសន្យា
-	ទីកន្លែងផ្គត់ផ្គង់ទំនិញ ឬសេវាមានលក្ខខណ្ឌសេដ្ឋកិច្ចដូចឬប្រហាក់ប្រហែលគ្នា
-	កត្តាផ្សេងទៀតដែលប៉ះពាល់លើថ្លៃ។

ឧទាហរណ៍ទី១៖
សហគ្រាស ក ជាសហគ្រាសដែលផ្គត់ផ្គង់ទំនិញក្នុងបរិមាណ ៧០% ទៅឱ្យបុគ្គលទាក់ទិននៅក្រៅប្រទេស (សហគ្រាស ខ) ក្នុងតម្លៃ ១០០ ០០០ រៀល ក្នុងមួយឯកតា និងទំនិញ ៣០% ទៀត ត្រូវបានផ្គត់ផ្គង់ទៅឱ្យសហគ្រាសឯករាជ្យក្នុងស្រុក (សហគ្រាស គ) ក្នុងតម្លៃ ១៥០ ០០០ រៀល ក្នុងមួយឯកតា។
 
ករណីទី១៖ សន្មតថា សហគ្រាស ក បានផ្គត់ផ្គង់ទៅឱ្យសហគ្រាស ខ និងសហគ្រាស គ នូវទំនិញដូចគ្នា។ ប្រតិបត្តិការរវាងសហគ្រាស ក និងសហគ្រាស គ អាចត្រូវបានចាត់ទុកជាមូលដ្ឋានប្រៀបធៀបផ្ទៃក្នុងសម្រាប់យកមកប្រើប្រាស់ជាប្រតិបត្តិការគ្មានការរៀបចំអាចធៀបបាន។ ប៉ុន្តែជាដំបូង ការវិភាគមុខងារទៅលើសហគ្រាស ក សហគ្រាស ខ និងសហគ្រាស គ ត្រូវតែធ្វើឡើង ដើម្បីរកឱ្យឃើញនូវភាពខុសគ្នាណាមួយដែលអាចមានផលប៉ះពាល់ជាសារវន្តទៅលើថ្លៃទីផ្សារ។ ប្រសិនបើមានភាពខុសគ្នា ការធ្វើនិយ័តកម្មដែលត្រឹមត្រូវ និងសមហេតុផលត្រូវបានធ្វើឡើង ដើម្បីលុបបំបាត់នូវភាពខុសគ្នាទាំងនោះ។ ក្នុងករណីដែលគ្មានភាពខុសគ្នាណាមួយដែលអាចប៉ះពាល់ជាសារវន្តទៅលើថ្លៃទីផ្សារនោះទេ វិធី ថគធ. អាចត្រូវបានយកមកអនុវត្តដោយប្រើប្រាស់ប្រតិបត្តិការគ្មានការរៀបចំអាចធៀបបានផ្ទៃក្នុង សម្រាប់ការកំណត់ថ្លៃឯកតានៃទំនិញចំនួន ១៥០ ០០០ រៀល ក្នុងមួយឯកតា ដែលជាថ្លៃជំហោងដៃ។

១-	វិធី ថផប. ជាការប្រៀបធៀបរវាងកម្រិតចំណេញដុលនៃការផ្គត់ផ្គង់បន្តនូវទំនិញក្នុងប្រតិបត្តិការមានការរៀបចំជាមួយនឹងកម្រិតចំណេញដុលក្នុងប្រតិបត្តិការគ្មានការរៀបចំអាចធៀបបាន។ ជាទូទៅ វិធី ថផប. ជាវិធីសមរម្យបំផុតសម្រាប់ប្រតិបត្តិការដែលទាក់ទិននឹងមុខងារផ្គត់ផ្គង់ឬមុខងារចែកចាយដែលប្រឈមនឹងហានិភ័យខ្ពស់ ឬមិនពាក់ព័ន្ធទៅនឹងប្រតិបត្តិការផ្គត់ផ្គង់ទ្រព្យអរូបីឯកលក្ខណៈនិងមានតម្លៃខ្ពស់។ អត្ថប្រយោជន៍ជាចម្បងនៃវិធីនេះផ្អែកសំខាន់លើតម្លៃបន្ថែម ឬការបំប្លែងដែលអ្នកផ្គត់ផ្គង់បន្តបានធ្វើឡើងមុនពេលផ្គត់ផ្គង់បន្ត។ វិធីនេះពិបាកនឹងអនុវត្ត ប្រសិនបើទំនិញត្រូវបានឆ្លងកាត់ច្រើនដំណាក់កាលនិងមានគម្លាតពេលវែង (ក្នុងករណីស្ថានភាពទីផ្សារអាចមានការប្រែប្រួល) មុនពេលដែលទំនិញត្រូវបានផ្គត់ផ្គង់ ឬនៅពេលដែលអ្នកផ្គត់ផ្គង់បន្ត បានបន្ថែមជាដុំកំភួន ឬបង្កើតទ្រព្យអរូបីភ្ជាប់ទៅនឹងទំនិញនោះ។
ចំណុចចាប់ផ្ដើមនៃវិធី ថផប. ជាថ្លៃនៃទំនិញដែលអ្នកផ្គត់ផ្គង់បន្តទិញពីបុគ្គលទាក់ទិន ហើយផ្គត់ផ្គង់បន្តទៅឱ្យសហគ្រាសឯករាជ្យ។ ថ្លៃផ្គត់ផ្គង់បន្តនេះ អាចធ្វើឱ្យអ្នកផ្គត់ផ្គង់បន្តមានកម្រិតចំណេញដុលមួយ ដែលអាចទូទាត់ចំណាយថ្លៃផ្គត់ផ្គង់ និងចំណាយប្រតិបត្តិការ ព្រមទាំងមុខងារផ្សេងៗទៀត (ដោយគិតបញ្ចូលទាំងទ្រព្យសកម្មដែលប្រើប្រាស់ និងហានិភ័យប្រឈម) ដើម្បីទទួលបានចំណូលសុទ្ធសមរម្យ។ ថ្លៃជំហោងដៃនៃប្រតិបត្តិការរវាងបុគ្គលទាក់ទិន ត្រូវបានកំណត់ដោយយកថ្លៃផ្គត់ផ្គង់បន្តដកចំណូលដុលក្រោយដកថ្លៃដើម។ វិធីគណនាកម្រិតចំណេញដុល ត្រូវបានបង្ហាញដូចខាងក្រោម៖
 
ចំណុចសំខាន់នៃរូបមន្តខាងលើ ស្ថិតនៅលើកម្រិតចំណេញដុលនៃការផ្គត់ផ្គង់បន្ត។ កម្រិតចំណេញដុលនេះបានមកពីការប្រៀបធៀបផ្ទៃក្នុង ដែលជាប្រតិបត្តិការរបស់អ្នកផ្គត់ផ្គង់បន្ត (ពាក់ព័ន្ធប្រតិបត្តិការមានការរៀបចំ) ទៅឱ្យសហគ្រាសឯករាជ្យ។ ក្នុងករណីដែលគ្មានប្រតិបត្តិការអាចធៀបបាន កម្រិតចំណេញដុលនៃការផ្គត់ផ្គង់បន្តអាចត្រូវបានកំណត់ពីការផ្គត់ផ្គង់ដោយអ្នកផ្គត់ផ្គង់បន្តផ្សេងទៀតក្នុងទីផ្សារដូចគ្នា។ កម្រិតចំណេញដុលនៃការផ្គត់ផ្គង់បន្តអាចប្រែប្រួលទៅតាមតម្លៃបន្ថែមដែលអ្នកផ្គត់ផ្គង់បន្តបានធ្វើឡើងមុននឹងផ្គត់ផ្គង់បន្តផលិតផល។
២-	ការវិភាគលើភាពដែលអាចធៀបបាន៖
ដើម្បីវិភាគលើភាពដែលអាចធៀបបាន ត្រូវពិចារណាលើកត្តាមួយចំនួនដែលជះឥទ្ធិពលលើកម្រិតចំណេញដុលនៃការផ្គត់ផ្គង់បន្ត មានជាអាទិ៍៖
ក-	មុខងារ ឬកម្រិតសកម្មភាពធ្វើឡើងដោយអ្នកផ្គត់ផ្គង់បន្ត និងហានិភ័យដែលមាន (អ្នកផ្គត់ផ្គង់បន្តគ្រាន់តែជាភ្នាក់ងារបញ្ជូនបន្ត ឬក៏ជាអ្នកចែកចាយដែលទទួលខុសត្រូវស្វែងរកទីផ្សារនិងផ្សព្វផ្សាយផលិតផល ដោយប្រឈមមុខនឹងហានិភ័យនៃការបាត់បង់ធនធានផ្ទាល់ខ្លួន)។
ខ-	ការប្រើប្រាស់ទ្រព្យសកម្មប្រហាក់ប្រហែល ទាំងក្នុងប្រតិបត្តិការមានការរៀបចំនិងប្រតិបត្តិការគ្មានការរៀបចំ។
គ-	ភាពប្រហាក់ប្រហែលគ្នានៃផលិតផល នៅតែមានភាពចាំបាច់នៅពេលដែលមានប្រតិបត្តិការទាក់ទិននឹងទ្រព្យអរូបីដែលមានឯកលក្ខណៈនិងមានតម្លៃខ្ពស់។
ឃ-ភាពខុសគ្នាក្នុងការគ្រប់គ្រងអាជីវកម្មដែលអាចជះឥទ្ធិពលលើកម្រិតចំណេញ ប្រសិនបើអត្រាកម្រិត ចំណេញផ្គត់ផ្គង់បន្តគឺជាអត្រាដែលប្រើប្រាស់ដោយសហគ្រាសឯករាជ្យក្នុងប្រតិបត្តិការអាចធៀបបាន។
ង-	ចន្លោះពេលពីការទិញដំបូងរហូតដល់ការផ្គត់ផ្គង់បន្តផលិតផល ប្រសិនបើមានរយៈពេលវែងដែលអាចបណ្តាលឱ្យទីផ្សារ អត្រាប្តូរប្រាក់ និងថ្លៃដើម... មានការប្រែប្រួល។
ច-	សិទ្ធិផ្តាច់មុខឬមិនផ្តាច់មុខក្នុងការផ្គត់ផ្គង់បន្តនូវផលិតផល។
ឆ-	ភាពខុសគ្នានៅក្នុងការអនុវត្តគណនេយ្យ ដែលទាមទារឱ្យមានការធ្វើនិយ័តកម្ម ដើម្បីធានានូវភាពដូចគ្នានៃសមាសធាតុថ្លៃដើម ដែលយកទៅប្រើប្រាស់ដើម្បីគណនាកម្រិតចំណេញដុលក្នុងប្រតិបត្តិការមានការរៀបចំ និងប្រតិបត្តិការគ្មានការរៀបចំ។
ជ- កត្តាផ្សេងទៀត ដែលប៉ះពាល់លើកម្រិតចំណេញដុល។

ឧទាហរណ៍ទី២៖
-	សហគ្រាស ក ជាសហគ្រាសពហុជាតិផលិតផលិតផលមានគុណភាពខ្ពស់ ដែលមានទីតាំងនៅបរទេស។
-	សហគ្រាស ខ ជាសហគ្រាសបុត្រសម្ព័ន្ធនៅកម្ពុជានៃសហគ្រាសពហុជាតិ ក។ 
-	សហគ្រាស គ ជាសហគ្រាសឯករាជ្យនៅកម្ពុជា។
-	សហគ្រាស ឃ ជាអ្នកចែកចាយបន្តឯករាជ្យទៅឱ្យអតិថិជននៅកម្ពុជា។

១-	វិធី បថដ. គឺជាការប្រៀបធៀបកម្រិតចំណេញលើថ្លៃដើមដែលកើតឡើងដោយផ្ទាល់ និងដោយប្រយោលចំពោះការផ្គត់ផ្គង់ទំនិញ សេវា ឬទ្រព្យ នៅក្នុងប្រតិបត្តិការមានការរៀបចំ និងប្រតិបត្តិការគ្មានការរៀបចំ។ ជាទូទៅ វិធី បថដ. ត្រូវបានប្រើប្រាស់ក្នុងករណីដែលផលិតផលពាក់កណ្ដាលសម្រេចត្រូវបានផ្គត់ផ្គង់រវាងបុគ្គលទាក់ទិន នៅពេលសហគ្រាសបានសម្រេចចុះកិច្ចព្រមព្រៀងប្រើប្រាស់ទ្រព្យរួមគ្នា នៅពេលផលិតករគឺជាផលិតករចុះកិច្ចសន្យា និងនៅពេលប្រតិបត្តិការមានការរៀបចំ គឺជាការផ្គត់ផ្គង់សេវា។ ដើម្បីគណនារកកម្រិតចំណេញលើថ្លៃដើម ត្រូវអនុវត្តតាមជំហានដូចខាងក្រោម៖ 
ក-	ចំណុចចាប់ផ្តើមនៅក្នុងវិធី បថដ. គឺថ្លៃដើមរបស់អ្នកផ្គត់ផ្គង់។ ដើម្បីគណនារកថ្លៃដែលអ្នកផ្គត់ផ្គង់ទទួលបានពីអ្នកទិញ ត្រូវយកថ្លៃដើមបន្ថែមនូវកម្រិតចំណេញលើថ្លៃដើមដែលសមស្រប។ គោលការណ៍ជំហោងដៃ តម្រូវឱ្យធ្វើការប្រៀបធៀបកម្រិតចំណេញលើថ្លៃដើមនៃប្រតិបត្តិការមានការរៀបចំ ទៅនឹងកម្រិតចំណេញលើថ្លៃដើមនៃប្រតិបត្តិការគ្មានការរៀបចំដែលអាចធៀបបាន។ ដូចនេះ កម្រិតចំណេញលើថ្លៃដើមនៃប្រតិបត្តិការគ្មានការរៀបចំនឹងត្រូវបានយកមកប្រើប្រាស់ជាមូលដ្ឋាន ដើម្បីធ្វើនិយ័តកម្មកម្រិតចំណេញលើថ្លៃដើមនៃប្រតិបត្តិការមានការរៀបចំ។
 
ខ-	ដើម្បីធ្វើនិយ័តកម្មលើថ្លៃដើម ត្រូវពិចារណាលើធាតុផ្សំរបស់ថ្លៃដើមនោះ។ វិធីកំណត់ថ្លៃដើម និងគោលនយោបាយគណនេយ្យត្រូវតែមានសង្គតិភាព និងអាចប្រៀបធៀបបានពីការិយបរិច្ឆេទមួយទៅការិយបរិច្ឆេទមួយទៀត រវាងប្រតិបត្តិការមានការរៀបចំ និងប្រតិបត្តិការគ្មានការរៀបចំ។ ថ្លៃដើមនៅក្នុងវិធី បថដ. គឺជាទឹកប្រាក់សរុបនៃថ្លៃដើមផ្ទាល់ និងថ្លៃដើមប្រយោលនៃផលិតកម្ម ឬការផ្គត់ផ្គង់។ ជាទូទៅ បន្ទុកចំណាយហិរញ្ញវត្ថុមិនត្រូវបានគិតបញ្ចូលក្នុងមូលដ្ឋានថ្លៃដើមទេ។ ការបញ្ចូលចំណាយផ្សេងទៀត ទៅក្នុងថ្លៃដើមត្រូវតែមានហេតុផលសមរម្យ ហើយអាចត្រូវបានយកមកពិចារណាតែក្នុងករណីដែលចំណាយទាំងនោះ ធ្វើឱ្យការប៉ាន់ស្មានកម្រិតចំណេញលើថ្លៃដើមកាន់តែសុក្រឹត ដោយប្រៀបធៀបទៅនឹងចំណាយក្នុងថ្លៃដើមនៃប្រតិបត្តិការអាចធៀបបាន។
២-	ការវិភាគលើភាពដែលអាចធៀបបាន៖

គ-	ធ្វើការវិភាគលើការអនុវត្តមុខងារ ការប្រើប្រាស់ទ្រព្យសកម្ម និងការគ្រប់គ្រងហានិភ័យរបស់ភាគីនីមួយៗដែលពាក់ព័ន្ធនឹងការអភិវឌ្ឍ ការកែលម្អ ការថែទាំ ការការពារ និងការទទួលបានផលប្រយោជន៍ពីទ្រព្យអរូបី ជាពិសេសរកឱ្យឃើញភាគីដែលទទួលបន្ទុកគ្រប់គ្រងមុខងារខាងក្រៅ និងគ្រប់គ្រងហានិភ័យសេដ្ឋកិច្ចសំខាន់ៗ។
ឃ-ពិនិត្យអំពីសង្គតិភាពរវាងលក្ខខណ្ឌនៃកិច្ចព្រមព្រៀងនិងការអនុវត្តរបស់ភាគីនីមួយៗ និងកំណត់ឱ្យឃើញថា ភាគីណាមួយជាភាគីដែលប្រឈមនឹងហានិភ័យសេដ្ឋកិច្ចសំខាន់ៗដូចមានចែងក្នុងវាក្យខណ្ឌ ខ នៃកថាខណ្ឌនេះ ជាភាគីគ្រប់គ្រងហានិភ័យនិងមានលទ្ធភាពហិរញ្ញវត្ថុដើម្បីប្រឈមនឹងហានិភ័យដែលពាក់ព័ន្ធនឹងការអភិវឌ្ឍ ការកែលម្អ ការថែទាំ ការការពារ និងការទទួលបានផលប្រយោជន៍ពីទ្រព្យអរូបី។
ង-	បង្ហាញថាប្រតិបត្តិការមានការរៀបចំដែលបានកើតឡើងជាក់ស្ដែងមានការពាក់ព័ន្ធនឹងការអភិវឌ្ឍ ការកែលម្អ ការថែទាំ ការការពារ និងការទទួលបានផលប្រយោជន៍ពីទ្រព្យអរូបី ដោយផ្តោតលើកម្មសិទ្ធិស្របច្បាប់នៃទ្រព្យអរូបីនោះ ព្រមទាំងកិច្ចសន្យាផ្សេងៗទៀតដែលពាក់ព័ន្ធនឹងការចុះបញ្ជីទ្រព្យអរូបី កិច្ចព្រមព្រៀងនិងការអនុវត្ត រួមបញ្ចូលទាំងមុខងារ ទ្រព្យសកម្ម និងហានិភ័យដែលភាគីនីមួយៗបានចូលរួម។

Article 1.- Purpose	
	This proclamation aims to set out the rules and procedures of the administration of income tax collection that are applicable to taxpayers under the declaratory regime, except for small taxpayers.

Article 2.- Scope
	Income tax applies to exile taxpayers on Cambodian and foreign-sourced income, and immigrant taxpayers on Cambodian-sourced income.

"Article 3.- Definitions
For the purposes of this Prakas:
1- Taxpayer refers to a person who is obliged to pay tax, including natural persons and legal persons.
2- Resident taxpayer, when used with natural persons, refers to any natural person who meets one or more of the following three criteria:
a- Has a residence in the Kingdom of Cambodia, which is owned or rented or leased a house, building, room, other residential premises... that can be used and which the natural person always stays or occupies.
b- Has a primary residence in the Kingdom of Cambodia, according to the actual form of residence, based on various factors such as the economic center of the natural person, the duration of stay, the nature of the residence, the place where the natural person's family resides, the natural person's bank account, the place where the natural person mainly carries out social activities.
c- Is present in the Kingdom of Cambodia for more than 182 days at a time or more than once during any 12 months ending in the taxable year. In determining the number of days of residence in the Kingdom of Cambodia Presence for any part of the day shall be counted as one full day.
In the event of uncertainty in determining the conditions set out in subparagraphs a and b of this paragraph, the presence of a natural person as set out in subparagraph c of this paragraph shall be the final condition for determining the residency of the natural person.
3- Resident taxpayer, when used with a legal person, refers to an entity that is established or controlled or has its principal place of business in the Kingdom of Cambodia.
4- Legal person refers to an enterprise or entity that carries on business, whether or not it has been officially recognized by the competent authorities of the Royal Government. Legal person also includes government agencies, religious organizations, charitable organizations, non-profit organizations, associations, political parties and permanent establishments of non-resident individuals located in the Kingdom of Cambodia. For the purposes of this paragraph, legal person does not include a partnership or sole proprietorship.
5- Permanent establishment refers to A permanent establishment in the Kingdom of Cambodia, a branch of a foreign company or a resident agent in the Kingdom of Cambodia through which a non-resident person carries on business. For the purposes of this paragraph, a permanent establishment also includes any other network or relationship through which a non-resident person carries on economic activities in the Kingdom of Cambodia. A permanent establishment is considered a resident juridical person only in respect of Cambodian-source income. A permanent establishment includes:
a- A place of management.
b- A branch of a foreign enterprise or agency.
c- An office of a foreign enterprise.
d- A warehouse, factory, workshop, farm or plantation.
e- A place of mining, coal or natural gas, a place of quarrying or other natural resources.
f- A construction site, a construction project or an assembly project and any monitoring activities connected with such a place or project, where such a place or project or activity lasts for more than 182 days at one or more times during a period.
G- The provision of services, including consultancy services, by employees or other personnel of a foreign enterprise, where such activities are carried out in the Kingdom of Cambodia for a total of more than 182 days on one or more occasions within any 12-month period.
G- Business activities (including the operation of heavy equipment) for the exploration or exploitation of natural resources for a total of more than 90 days on one or more occasions within any 12-month period.
G- In addition to the provisions of paragraphs A to C of this paragraph, a person is considered to be a permanent establishment in the Kingdom of Cambodia if the person meets one or more of the following three conditions:
- Has and regularly exercises the authority to conclude contracts in the Kingdom of Cambodia on behalf of a foreign enterprise or plays a major role in facilitating the conclusion of contracts
- Regularly maintains in the Kingdom of Cambodia a stock of goods and the person regularly releases or supplies goods from that stock on behalf of a foreign enterprise
- Collects premiums or undertakes insurance, except for continuing insurance of risks in the Kingdom of Cambodia on behalf of a foreign enterprise.
N- In application, the tax administration shall judge on a case-by-case basis whether or not a permanent establishment exists, except for the application of the provisions of international agreements.
6- Capital companies refer to public limited liability companies, private limited liability companies and sole proprietorships.
7- Enterprises refer to establishments or organizations in which natural or legal persons engage in business.
8- Non-resident taxpayers refer to any person who is not a resident taxpayer and receives Cambodian-source income.
9- Dividends refer to cash or property shares distributed by a legal entity to shareholders in proportion to their shares in the legal entity’s own capital, except for the distribution of capital during the complete liquidation of a company. Any share considered as a dividend or not shall be based on the above conditions, regardless of whether or not the legal entity has net income in the current year or from previous years.
10- Banks refer to banking and financial institutions, microfinance institutions

Article 4.- Tax regime 
	The tax regime of the Kingdom of Cambodia is an autonomous regime that requires taxpayers to do tax calculations and file fiscal declarations and pay taxes themselves.

Article 5.- Accounting rules 
	1- In accordance with the accounting rules in accordance with the International Financial Reporting Standards of Cambodia, income shall be accounted for in the year in which such income occurred, even if such income has been paid or has not yet been paid.
	2. Transactions denominated in foreign currencies shall comply with the following principles: 
a- To be recorded in the accounting list in KHR using the National Bank of Cambodia's exchange rate on the day of the transaction.
b- In the event of an exchange guarantee system, the debit or debt shall be exchanged in KHR on the basis of the fixed exchange rate specified in the contract.
c- If a debt or debt is incurred and settled in a single office, the amount of the amount examined between the current and accrued value and the repayment value is the loss or gain from the exchange which is recorded as the financial expense or financial income of the office.
d- Upon completion of the assessment, debits or debts in foreign currencies shall be assessed at the exchange rate on the closing day of the office.
d- In the next office, when paying a debt or debt involving a loss or gain from the exchange of money, the difference between its value at the time of settlement and its value at the close of the previous office.
F- With respect to cash in foreign currency that the enterprise has at the end of the office, the enterprise shall act in the same manner as the rules provided for debits or debts as provided in paragraph D of this paragraph.

Article 6.- Extra-accounting adjustments 
		As per the accounting rules, net income or loss is the balance of account as a result of the taxation, but as otherwise determined by tax laws and regulations, out-of-accounting adjustments are made by reclaiming or deducting income and expenses, in accordance with the provisions as provided in Article 54 of this post.

Article 7.- Tax year
In accordance with Article 8 of the Tax Law, the tax year is defined as follows:
1- For legal entities:
a- Income tax is calculated from the accounting results achieved in each calendar year (January 1 to December 31). Enterprises that apply the tax year according to the calendar year must file a tax return and pay the annual income tax no later than March 31 of the following year.
b- Enterprises controlled by non-resident legal entities may request to apply a tax year other than the calendar year. Enterprises that apply to apply a new tax year must apply as follows:
- Transitional date:
- For old enterprises, it will continue to apply from January 1 of the tax year in which the application was made until the day before the start of the new tax year.
Example 1:
In 2024, an enterprise applied to apply a new tax year starting from July 1, 2024 to June 30, 2025. Therefore, the transitional period shall be from January 1, 2024 to June 30, 2024. The subsequent taxable year for this enterprise shall be from July 1, 2024 to June 30, 2025.
- For newly established enterprises, it shall be from the date of commencement of business until the day before the date of commencement of the new taxable year requested.
Example 2:
An enterprise is newly established on March 1, 2024. The new enterprise requests to apply a new taxable year starting from July 1, 2024 to June 30, 2025. Therefore, the transitional period shall be from March 1, 2024 to June 30, 2024. The subsequent taxable year for this enterprise shall be from July 1, 2024 to June 30, 2025.
Example 3:
In the case of an enterprise newly established on September 1, 2024. The new enterprise requests to apply a new taxable year starting from July 1, 2024 to June 30, 2025. Therefore, the transitional period shall be from September 1, 2024 to June 30, 2025. The next taxable year for this enterprise is from July 1 to June 30.
- Continuing date: The new taxable year is 12 months after the end of the transitional fiscal year
Example 4:
Continuing from Example 1, Example 2, and Example 3 above, the continuing date (new taxable year) is from July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026.
- The amortization allowance for the transitional fiscal year is calculated as the ratio of the number of days of the transitional fiscal year to the 365 days of the year
Example 5:
The enterprise has a transitional fiscal year from January 1, 2024 to June 30, 2024. In this case, the number of amortization days is 182 days. The amortization allowance for a full year is 42,000,000 riel. Therefore, the installment payment for the transitional fiscal year:

=(42 000 000 × 182)/365=20 942 466 riel.
- The loss allowance for the transitional fiscal year shall be calculated as one year.
- An enterprise requesting to apply for the new tax year as stipulated in this paragraph shall apply to the General Department of Taxation with the following documents:
- A letter of confirmation from the parent company abroad about the use of the new tax year other than the calendar year
- A letter of confirmation from the independent auditor of the parent company abroad about the use of the tax year other than the calendar year
- A copy of the company's articles of association, which can confirm the identity of the parent company abroad.
- An enterprise requesting to apply for the new tax year shall file a tax return and pay annual income tax as follows:
- Within 3 months after the end of the transitional fiscal year
- Within 3 months after the end of the new tax year
C- If there are multiple accounting results in a calendar year, all accounting results shall be combined as the basis for calculating income tax.
D- For new enterprises that start business, the accounting results shall be calculated from the date of starting business until:
- December 31 of the calendar year for enterprises that use the calendar year as the tax year
- The end of the tax year for enterprises that request to apply a tax year other than the calendar year.
E- For enterprises that suspend or cease business activities, the final accounting results shall be calculated:
- From January 1 until the date of permanent suspension or cessation of activities for enterprises that use the calendar year as the tax year
- From the beginning of the current tax year until the date of permanent suspension or cessation of activities for enterprises that request to apply a tax year other than the calendar year.
2- For individuals, sole proprietorships and partnerships, income tax is calculated from the total income achieved in each calendar year.

Article 8.- Source of Income
1- In accordance with Article 33 of the Tax Law, without limitation to the following income, Cambodian source income includes:
a- Interest paid by a resident taxpayer, a resident partnership or a government agency of the Kingdom of Cambodia.
b- Dividends distributed by a resident taxpayer. For the purposes of this Article:
- The transfer of any or all of retained earnings to the capital of an enterprise, with a decision of the board of directors of the enterprise and clear evidence of the capital change with the approval of the competent authority, shall not be considered as a distribution of dividends. If at any time an enterprise withdraws capital to be distributed to shareholders, such withdrawal of capital shall be considered as a distribution of dividends to the portion of capital derived from retained earnings. Retained earnings are considered to be distributed as dividends to shareholders in full when the enterprise permanently ceases its business activities.
- In the event of a transfer of any or all shares in the capital or equity of an enterprise with retained earnings, the retained earnings relating to the transferred shares, whether or not converted into capital or equity, shall be considered to be distributed as dividends.
c- Income from services performed in the Kingdom of Cambodia.
d- Income from management and technical services paid by a resident taxpayer. For the purposes of this Article:
- Management services refer to services of a managerial nature undertaken to perform management functions in the conduct of a business, such as recruitment, training, and management of sales force
- Technical services refer to services of a technical nature that require technical skills or knowledge to develop or create inputs into a business, such as scientific, physical, chemical, medical, dental, pharmaceutical, legal, hydrological, veterinary, artistic, educational, engineering, architectural, research, accounting, economic, welfare, and nuclear energy services, including consulting services. For the purposes of this Article, consulting services refer to advisory services provided by experts or persons with a professional background in relation to technical services as set out in this Article
- Incidental costs incurred in support of the supply of management and technical services and paid to the supplier of such management and technical services shall be considered as part of management and technical services.
E- Income derived from movable or immovable property in the case where the property is located in the Kingdom of Cambodia.
F- Royalties derived from the use or right to use intangible assets paid by a resident or non-resident individual through a permanent establishment situated in the Kingdom of Cambodia.
For the purposes of this paragraph, royalties on intangible assets refer to:
- Permission to use the right to publish and sell literary, artistic, scientific or related works or similar rights (including copyright and related rights and broadcasting of sound or video tapes...), patents, business rights, trademarks or trade names, designs, models, plans, formulas, secrets of manufacturing processes... in general, all intangible property or other rights
- Knowledge or know-how or information concerning various experiences in the fields of industry, commerce, science, information technology, engineering...
- Transfer of rights to knowledge or information as mentioned in this paragraph
- Advice or provision of services related to the implementation or use of rights as mentioned in this paragraph
Royalties on intangible assets also include payments of all other benefits from participation in mineral resources, other than net income from the exploitation of such resources and dividends.
G- Gains from the sale of movable or immovable property, including intangible property, situated in the Kingdom of Cambodia, or gains from the alienation of any interest in movable or immovable property, including intangible property, situated in the Kingdom of Cambodia, or capital gains from financial assets and investment assets in the Kingdom of Cambodia, or capital gains from the transfer of any or all shares in the equity of an enterprise in the Kingdom of Cambodia.
C- Premiums for insurance or reinsurance for risks in the Kingdom of Cambodia.
C- Gains from the sale of movable property forming part of the business assets of a permanent establishment of a non-resident taxpayer in the Kingdom of Cambodia.
2- Income from the business activities of a non-resident taxpayer through a permanent establishment in the Kingdom of Cambodia and income of a non-resident taxpayer from the supply of goods or services identical or similar to the business activities of a permanent establishment that the non-resident taxpayer supplies in the Kingdom of Cambodia.
2- Any income that is not determined as Cambodian source income as stated in paragraph 1 of this Article shall be considered as foreign source income.
3- In the absence of sufficient information to determine the source of income as stated in Article 35 of the Tax Law or if the rules in accordance with Article 33 of the Tax Law or other tax legal regulations cannot clearly reflect the income from any source, the Tax Administration shall determine the source of such income.

Article 9.- Taxable income
1- Taxable income as stipulated in Article 7 of the Tax Law is the net income from all the results of all kinds of operations that an enterprise achieves, including the surplus value from the sale of parts of assets during the course of business or upon termination of the business, interest, fees and royalties, as well as income from financial assets or investment assets, including real estate. Taxable income also includes all capital gains from real estate, financial assets or investment assets that an individual or legal entity achieves from operations other than business operations. For the purposes of this paragraph, any business activity, whether permitted by law or not, is not exempt from income tax.
2- Taxable income is derived from the deduction of gross income and all expenses arising from all kinds of operations of the enterprise during the course of business or upon termination of the business. According to accounting principles, taxable income is the balance of the result account achieved from all kinds of operations of the enterprise. These transactions may be directly related to the activities of the enterprise or may not be directly related to the activities of the enterprise, which may be carried out in a primary or secondary manner. These transactions include:
a- Supply of goods or services or other transactions (brokerage, commission work, concession of rights to intangible property, etc.).
b- Disposal of any part of the assets. For the purposes of this paragraph, disposal refers to any operation or event that results in the disposal of any part of the assets of the enterprise, such as sale, legal seizure of assets, appropriation (capitalization), exchange, gift, removal of assets, etc.
c- For legal entities or sole proprietorships, the following shall be included in taxable income:
- Excess value of assets sold
- Assets not sold on the date of cessation of activity (long-term assets, inventories, raw materials, work in progress, etc.) shall be considered as repossessions of the enterprise owner (transfer from business assets to private assets). These assets shall be valued at market value.
3- Taxable income is the difference between the value of net assets at the end of the taxable period and the value at the beginning of the taxable period.
a- Taxable income is the difference between the value of net assets at the end of the taxable period and the value at the beginning of the taxable period, net of any deductions and plus any withdrawals for personal use or advance deductions made by the owner of the enterprise during the period. This definition shows that taxable income also includes profits that arise in circumstances where the enterprise does not operate, such as the case of excess value that occurs during the legal seizure of assets during foreclosure or during an event that leads to the receipt of insurance compensation.
b- Net assets are the actual value of total assets, minus the sum of the items on the liability account, including third-party creditors (long-term or short-term debts) and legally established provisions.
- Total assets include the following main items:
- Long-term assets, such as the land of the enterprise, the arrangement of the land of the enterprise, the construction of the enterprise, the factory, the business fund, the initial establishment costs of the enterprise (research and development costs and other long-term asset costs: these costs do not constitute the actual value of the asset)
- Short-term assets, such as stocks (goods, raw materials and various supplies, work in progress, finished goods, etc.) various investment certificates, cash at the bank, cash on hand, etc.
- Third-party liabilities: are real and permanent debts, both in principle and in the amount of debt contracted for business needs and related to the normal management of the enterprise
- Provisions: These items must be legally established.
C- Contingencies: Contingencies, whether in money or in kind, are not taxable income. The deductions made by the owner of a sole proprietorship in cases where there is proper evidence shall be deducted from the difference between the actual value of the assets at the close and at the open of the taxable period.
D- Withdrawals for personal use or advance deductions of the owner of the enterprise include:
- Withdrawal of raw materials, finished products, goods, services, etc. for the personal needs of the owner of the enterprise and his family (food, clothing, household appliances, various materials and services of the owner of the construction enterprise, etc.)
- Use of the owner of the enterprise's assets (houses, cars, etc.) for the personal needs of the owner of the enterprise.
E- Sale to shareholders of goods or services at a price lower than the normal price (hand-held or market price) applicable to general customers.
F- Also considered as taxable income are:
- Cancellation of debts
- Reduction of debts granted to the enterprise by creditors
- Owner's capital accounts and debts that are not true or have no supporting evidence
- Reconstruction of unrecorded assets.
G- Any change in net assets is allowed to correct any errors in the balance sheet at the end of any fiscal year, and if the adjustment results in an increase in an asset account or a decrease in a liability account, requiring a redetermination of the taxable income for that fiscal year. The taxpayer has the right to adjust the balance sheet at the opening of the next fiscal year within the period of the adjustment authorization, except:

Article 10.- Tax-exempt income 
	Tax-exempt income is defined as follows:
	1. Government revenues or revenues of government institutions. 
	2- Income: 
a- Any organization that is organized and operated for purely religious, charitable, scientific, literary or educational purposes and no share of the property or income is used for private benefit.
b- Any association in which the income of those associations is not utilized for the private benefit of the individual shareholder or physical.
	3. Dividends received from rural enterprises, in case the tax is payable under Article 45, Article 49 and Article 52 of this Notice, is already paid. 
	4. In the event that the income as specified in the second paragraph of this Article is used as the personal benefit of the individual shareholder or the individual physical, those incomes shall be subject to re-taxation.
	5- In the case of an association or organization as mentioned in the second paragraph of this Article, there is a commercial or industrial or other business activity which is not useful for the purpose or function of its tax exemption, the income derived from those non-business activities shall be taxed in accordance with Article 49 of this Article.

Article 11.- Definition of inventory
1- Inventory consists of all assets owned by the enterprise, namely assets that participate in the business cycle of the enterprise in order to:
a- Sell in their original state or sell after processing or after production, or
b- Use up all of them in the initial stage of use.
2- Inventory includes:
a- Goods, supplies (raw materials, consumables, packaging materials, etc.) and products (semi-finished products, finished products, waste or materials for recycling).
b- Work in progress: These are assets or services that are being produced in the production process.
3- All products or goods or materials that are owned by the enterprise, whether they are located on or off the enterprise’s premises, shall also be considered inventory.
4- When taking inventory, if products or goods or materials that the enterprise has not yet received are certain to belong to the enterprise, they must be reflected in inventory and recorded in the balance sheet.
5- Products or goods or raw materials stored in warehouses inside or outside the Kingdom of Cambodia or given to outsiders or as a deposit or guarantee or on loan must be reflected in the assets of the enterprise that still owns the property.
6- They are considered stocks if the products or goods meet both of the following conditions:
a- The products or goods or raw materials belong to the enterprise on the day of the inventory, even if the products or goods are not in the enterprise’s warehouse.
b- The products or goods or raw materials are intended to be sold in their original state or after processing or for production (which is part of the enterprise’s short-term assets that cannot be classified as long-term assets).
7- Assets in progress are assets that are in progress or in process and have not been completed at the end of the accounting period. Assets in progress are common in construction enterprises, public works enterprises and enterprises that perform work with heavy equipment and that take a long time to process or produce.
8- An enterprise must not reflect in stocks assets that have been delivered but have not yet been invoiced.
9- Stock accounts and work-in-progress accounts can be divided into:
A- Raw materials and supplies account: Records more or less processed materials and supplies that are used up in the initial use or are quickly used up in the production or processing of products and do not enter into the composition of the products produced or processed or are used in the business as packaging. This account includes:
- Consumables
- Consumables:
- Fuel
- Maintenance materials
- Workshop and factory supplies
- Warehouse supplies
- Office supplies.
- Packaging:
- Non-recyclable packaging
- Recoverable packaging that cannot be classified.
C- Work in progress account for products: Records products in production and work in progress.
D- Work in progress for services: Records research and services that are not completed and that are performed under a contract that does not provide for a gradual transfer of ownership, or records research and services that have been completed but the contract states that the work will not become a credit until the customer agrees on the price.
E- Product inventory includes:
- Semi-finished products are products that have reached a certain stage of completion but are held for inclusion in a new stage of the production cycle
- Finished products are products that have reached a complete stage in the production cycle
- Waste is waste from production that can be sold (scraps, wood chips, metal chips, paper chips, etc.) or is recyclable material, such as parts and other materials collected when a long-term asset is discontinued or dismantled. These materials are kept for use in the business cycle or for sale.
F- Inventory is goods that the enterprise purchases to sell without processing.
G- Stock in transit:
- Materials, supplies or goods that have not yet been received into the warehouse but have already become the property of the enterprise
- Products or goods released from the warehouse are being delivered to customers but are still the property of the enterprise
- Materials, supplies, products or goods stored at a sales point located outside the headquarters or sent to a third party.

Article 12.- Evaluation of the Perm 
	A stock valuation can be done in the following ways:
	1- Procurement valuation (cost of goods received) based on actual purchase costs composed of:
a- Invoiced purchase fees. Discounts, price reductions, or price reversals associated with the purchase, which the supplier has agreed to provide, shall be deducted from the purchase price.
b- Nominal expenses directly related to the purchase or supply, in which there are offences, transportation, transit, royalties or commissions, lifting or loading of goods, customs duties and other VAT, except for VAT on the added value which can be refunded as a credit.
	2- Evaluation of production norms (product costs) to be composed of:
a- Procurement of raw materials or supplies used for production.
b- Direct costs to bring the product to the place and on the condition in which the product is practical.
c- Not to be included in the production budget general administrative expenses, product surplus costs, research and development expenses, and financial expenses.
	3- Determination of the discharge allocation of the stock:
a- For goods or products with separate characteristics, the description of the goods or products shall be determined according to the input description of each such goods or products.
b- For interchangeable and non-separable goods or products, it is permitted to use the following two methods for determining the scope of the sword: 
- Symmetrical average, which has two modes:
- Monthly Equivalent Average Ratio: In this case, the unit allocation of the outgoing goods in any month shall be equal to the sum of the total amount of the original stock of the month and the total amount of purchases or production in that month divided by the sum of the total volume of the original month and the volume of all purchases or production in that month.
- Proportional Average Ratio After Insertion: The unit amount of discharge made after any input shall be equal to the sum of the remaining amount of the remainder before the input and the amount of the input, divided by the sum of the remaining amount of the remainder before the input and the amount of the input.
- First-in, first-out (FIFO): Goods or products that come in first must be released first.
- In the case of an enterprise using the bureaucratic method of stock management, the final receipts shall be assessed according to the inbound quota of the goods or products that are most imported.
- In the case of an enterprise using a permanent exit, the final exit must be assessed according to the actual procurement criteria.

Article 13.- Evaluation of work in progress 
	1. The work in progress shall be assessed according to the criminal production criteria composed of:
A- Description of the materials used.
b- Labor costs.
c- Expenses at work.
d- one-third of the general expenditure of the headquarters and one-third of the expenditure which is generally often assessed in an estimated manner. 
	2- Enterprises cannot take into account net commercial and administrative expenses as well as financial expenses.

Article 14.- Business assets 	
	1- Given that the value of net assets at the time of closing and opening of the office is used as the basis for calculating the tax rate, the enterprise must record the business assets as the share of the assets of the enterprise according to each category clearly. 
	2. Except for land and buildings subject to Article B of Paragraph 5 of Article 34 of this Announcement, the business assets of individual enterprises shall comply with the following principles:
A- The owner of the enterprise shall distinguish between the business assets and the private assets of the owner of the enterprise.
b- The owner of a sole proprietorship has no right to record or not record any share of the assets or reserves and liabilities in its perception.
c- The owner of a sole proprietorship shall record in the balance sheet of his own enterprise all the shares of assets, as well as the reserves and liabilities involved in the operation of the business as follows: 
- Every long-term asset used for business activities (commercial funds, transportation materials, etc.) must also be recorded in the assets of the balance sheet of long-term assets used for mixed use (for business use and personal use) 
- Every short-term asset as it relates to business activities (goods, products, raw materials, credits, money on hand...)
- Equity and debt as it relates to business activities (borrowing to buy long-term assets, short-term debt or long-term debt...)។
d- The owner of a sole proprietorship is not allowed to record in his or her enterprise balance sheet the assets that are not relevant to the business activity, where:
- Real estate or any portion of real estate that does not serve business activities (dwelling houses, residential buildings...)
- Lending or borrowing that does not contribute to business activities.
Therefore, the balance sheet of a sole proprietorship must outline every asset that serves the business in character, by deployment, or by purpose, showing only these values.
- Requiring a separation between business and private assets is critical because:
- Expenses that are the basis for determining taxable income must be expenses as per the share of business assets.
- The divestment of business assets to private assets is considered a sale that results in a taxable excess value or a shortfall to be deducted from taxable income.
- Reverse operations, i.e., the transfer of assets from private assets to business assets are accidental. 
The incident was recorded at the actual value on the day of the crash.
	3. The business assets of an individual enterprise shall comply with the following principles:
A- Business assets are the assets of an enterprise.
b- For enterprises formed without a clear statutory basis, the assets which the shareholders have agreed to be jointly owned must be recorded on the assets side of the balance sheet.

Article 15.- General principles of revenue recognition 
	1- Enterprises shall comply with accounting rules in accordance with the International Financial Reporting Standards of Cambodia. For the purposes of income tax, enterprises must recognize income in the office where the income digits have accrued, even if such income has been paid or unpaid. 
	2- For the supply of goods or services, an enterprise shall be recorded as revenue at the time of invoicing if the invoice is issued before the delivery of goods or receipt of money, or at the time of delivery of goods or the fulfillment of services or at the time of payment.
	3- In case the goods or services are taken for the personal use of any person, the enterprise shall record as revenue when the goods are first taken for use or as when the services are completed.
	4- In case the goods or services are supplied as gifts, the enterprise shall record as revenue when the goods are handed over, notwithstanding the right of use or assignment, or when the services are completed.
	5- With respect to the supply of goods under a lease contract or the supply of goods or services under a contract or a law that provides for overpayment or the supply of consolidated services, such goods or services shall be deemed to have been ready supplied only to the portion already supplied within the period specified in the contract or the period prescribed by law, and the enterprise shall record as a turnover of each ready-supplied share on any date preceding any of the dates on which payment is due. and the date the payment was received. 
	6- For financial obligations, the enterprise shall record the turnover on the date on which the payment is due and the date on which the payment is received. 
	7. With respect to financial services, unless the bank is permitted to make legal and legal proceedings on which the bank withholds interest, the enterprise shall record as income on the date on which interest is received, interest or commission as provided for in the financial services supply contract or the date of payment of interest, interest or commission if the payment is made before the due date.
	8. For construction enterprises or construction service enterprises, the enterprise shall record as the turnover of each ready-supplied share on the preceding date among the dates on which the payment is due according to the contract and the date required to be recorded as the turnover to be recognized in the accounting list in accordance with the accounting rules of the International Financial Reporting Standards of Cambodia.

Article 16.- Additional conditions for recognition of income 
With respect to the supply of goods, recognition of income occurs when the right of possession or right of possession or right of use, which in general cases is to occur at the time of delivery of the goods. The supply of goods may be made under the following conditions:
	1- Supply under the Contract Suspension Condition: In this case, the transfer of ownership or possession or right of use is consequential to the achievement of an event in the future. Conversely, if that event does not occur, the contract shall be suspended until such time as an event occurs that leads to the expropriation of ownership or possession or right of use and makes the revenue digit liable.
	2- Supply under the terms of the dissolution of the contract: In this case, the surrender of ownership or the right of occupancy or right of use is made immediately, just like the supply of a simple contract, but the contract has to be cancelled if the contemplated conditions become real. The cancellation of supply has to be acknowledged in the event that the condition has become a reality.
	3- Money withheld to guarantee: For the money that the buyer has temporarily withheld to ensure the quality of the work supplied, the supplier shall take into account the results of the negotiation at the time of handing over the work or at the time of placing the work under the responsibility of the owner of the work.
	4- Deposit: The deposit paid by the buyer in advance while ordering goods or services, which is a share of the cost of purchasing goods or services, and the supplier has to record this deposit as the receipt date.

Article 17.- Income from business activities
	Income from business activities is income derived from the supply of goods or services that are business activities specified on the patent tax certificate of an enterprise. Income from business activities as defined in this Article and nominal income as provided for in Article 18 of this post are the income that is the basis for calculating the income tax or minimum tax prepayment.

Article 18.- Nominal income 
	Nominal income is an income that is not income from the business activities of the enterprise but is also included in the income of the enterprise.
	1- Income from the lease of real estate, even if the property engages in or does not engage in business activities.
	2- Property subject to free use by the plaintiff shall be determined that the enterprise has received taxable income, an amount equal to the market wage of the property. 
	3. Property for private use of employees for free shall be determined to indicate that the enterprise receives a taxable income equal to the market wage of the property, except for the property given to the workers for collective use in accordance with the provisions of the Labor Law.
	4- Letters: Income derived from business on supernatural assets, criminal proclamations, copyrights, authors' rights and approximate rights, drawings, layout models, business rights, production signs, ways of doing.
	5- Other offenses of nominal income, consisting of revenues from the sale of waste, rental of business materials, income from packaging.

Article 19.- Other Revenues
		Apart from income from business activities and nominal income, there are many other disposable income enterprises that are included in taxable income: 
	1- Income from securities, shares, and dividends.
	2- Financial income (income from debits, deposits, deposit accounts, current accounts...)។
	3- Income from activities undertaken for the benefit of employees.
	4- Gifts and Sponsorships:
A- Gifts and sponsorships shall be included in the taxable income of the office which receives these gifts and sponsorships.
- Gifts, regardless of the source.
- Subsidize capital for businesses that the state, the public collective, the tribunal... Given (allowances for meeting expenses, subsidizing capital for relieving business burdens, subsidizing capital for guarantees...)។
b- Subsidize investment resources:
- For investment capital allowances for Tier 1 assets valued at 40,000 thousand (forty million) roubles or more, the enterprise shall not be recorded as an income in its entirety for the taxable year.
	Example Six: 
	For assets in Class 1 with a depreciation rate of 5% and which are acquired by bankruptcy at the value of KHR 100,000,000, the share to be recorded as taxable income for each taxable year is equal to KHR 500000 (except for the year ending the amortization).
- For assets that are in Class 2, Class 3, and Class 4, investment assets shall be recorded as entirely taxable income, deducting the deduction from the deduction table to determine the appropriate amount for asset disbursement in the year in which those assets are deployed. 
5- Construction or improvement of real estate undertaken by the tenant at his own expense and without reimbursement from the enterprise, resulting in an increase in the value of the property. 
6- Value exceeds the sale or cessation of use of business assets.
7- Insurance indemnity: Insurance compensation received by the enterprise after a catastrophe (fire, theft, property damage...) or within the framework of an insurance contract contracted for the benefit of the enterprise.
8. Compensation for misdemeanors includes:
a- Compensation for the collection of various means such as canoes that the State has used to carry people during floods ... ។
b- Compensation for cancellation of contracts.
c- Compensation given as a psychopath.
d- Compensation for damages by conducting dishonest competing business.
	9- Ease of VAT previously deducted from taxable income: This ease of money is the turnover of the office from which the enterprise receives this benefit.
10. Debt relief: The relief of debt which the supplier or the debtor has agreed to give to the enterprise and which has resulted in an increase in the net assets of the enterprise shall be recorded as the turnover of the office for which the enterprise has received the approval of the divestment.

Article 20.- Principles for Business Expenses 
1- Deductible Expenses: are expenses for a business that the taxpayer has paid or are to reimburse in the taxable year and that do not return assets or that do not discharge any debts.
2. Expenses paid or reimbursable in a taxable year: Expenses in any taxable year are deductible only in the taxable year, deductible expenses must meet the conditions as specified in Article 21 of this Post. To determine the result of any taxable year, only those facts and operations leading to the achievement of that result shall be taken into account as follows:
A- Expenditure as per the preceding taxable year: Except as provided in syntax B of the second paragraph of Article 21 of this post, any expenditure incurred and subject to be recorded as the expense of any preceding taxable year cannot be deducted in the preceding taxable year.
b- Unpaid expenses in a taxable year: If an expense in accordance with the conditions as provided in Article 20 and Article 21 of this Announcement shall be an expense of any taxable year, but at the time of closing the list of unpaid expenses, the enterprise shall record this expense in the account payable (unpaid rent, unpaid tax in the taxable year...)In case of no such recording, the expenditure cannot be recorded as an expense in the next taxable year.
c- Expenses of the next taxable year: It is not allowed to be credited to one taxable year the expenses as to subsequent taxable years.
d- Prepaid expenses: shall be deducted only from the income of the taxable year in which those expenses were incurred.
	3- Expenses to conduct business: It is allowed to deduct only any expenditure made to serve the business or for the sake of the business. Therefore, any expenditure that is not associated with ordinary management or which benefits the business is not deductible.
a- Expenses serving the personal needs of the enterprise owner (housing expenses, personal taxes, expenses on private use vehicles, expenses on servants, personal or federal business owners' expenses, direct deductions from customer payments...)។
B- Excessive or excessive expenses that are too useless or of little benefit to the business. For the purposes of this term, excessive expenditure implies spending in excess of necessity or wasted beyond reasonableness, unreasonably expensive or overpriced, or excessively prominent.
	4- Expenses that do not cause a decrease in the net assets of the enterprise or that do not write off any debts: are expenses that result in a decrease in the net assets of the enterprise.
a- Expenses that are not the burden of the enterprise itself.
b- Expenses that reclaim a new share in the asset or that results in an increase in the value of any share of the asset.
c- Expenses for increasing the useful life of any asset.
d- Expenses that lead to debt cancellation (repayment of loans, payments owed to suppliers...)។

Article 21.- Principles for deductible expenses
1- For income tax purposes, expenses as set out in Article 20 of this Prakas may be allowed to be deducted provided that they meet the following three conditions:
A- The event giving rise to the expense has occurred and is a real obligation of the enterprise, meaning that the reality of the expense is confirmed by verifiable evidence (invoices, customs declarations, commercial correspondence, loan contracts, expense reports, etc.).
B- The results of the economic activity related to the expenditure occurred:
- In cases where the expenditure requires payment for the supply of assets, goods or services, the results of the economic activity occur when the enterprise receives the supply of assets, goods or services
- In cases where the expenditure is incurred because the enterprise has used the assets or supplied the goods or services, the results of the economic activity occur when the enterprise has used the assets or when the enterprise has supplied the goods or services
- The results of the economic activity are considered to have occurred when any of the following payments occur:
- Compensation to workers, compensation for injuries or damages for breach of contract
- Price reductions or rebates
- Various bonuses
- Compensation for receiving guarantees or under service agreements
- Taxes other than foreign tax credits, minimum taxes and income taxes.
C- The expenses of the enterprise are clearly recorded in the accounting records in the taxable year, with proper evidence of the amount and date.
2- In addition to the three conditions set out in paragraph 1 of this Article:
A- For income tax purposes, an expense that has not been paid at the end of the taxable year may be deducted, provided that the expense is a real debt of the enterprise. If the unpaid amount does not represent a real debt, the deduction shall not be allowed. In order to establish a real debt, there must be a demand by the creditor with a reasonable expectation that the debt will be actually paid by the enterprise.
B- For the expense of salaries to be paid to employees, the enterprise may deduct in the current taxable year if the salary is paid within 180 days of the following taxable year. In the case of the expense of salaries to be paid to employees as set out in this paragraph and not paid within 180 days of the following taxable year, the expense shall be included as taxable income for the current taxable year. However, if the payment occurs after 180 days, the expense shall be allowed to be deducted for the following taxable year only for the payment made in that subsequent taxable year. This 180-day rule shall not apply to provisions for employee pensions.
C- For expenses to be paid to related persons, the enterprise may deduct them in the current taxable year if the expenses are incurred within 180 days of the following taxable year, except for deductible expenses of capital and depreciable assets. For expenses to be paid to related persons who are not in the self-declaration regime, deduction is not allowed before actual payment. In the case of expenses to be paid to related persons as stipulated in this paragraph, are not paid within 180 days of the following taxable year, such expenses shall be included as taxable income for the current taxable year and shall not be allowed to be deducted for subsequent taxable years.
D- In the case of an enterprise making an adjustment on its own by including the unpaid expenses as taxable income for the current taxable year as stipulated in paragraphs B and C of this paragraph, within 30 days after the 180-day period, the enterprise shall not be subject to additional tax and interest. In the event that the enterprise fails to make the adjustment in time, the additional tax and interest shall commence from the month following the 180-day period.

Article 22.- Policy for non-deductible expenses 
Unless otherwise provided, other than expenses that satisfy the conditions as provided for in Article 21 of this Announcement, all other expenses are non-deductible expenses and shall be reimbursed as taxable income.

Article 23.- Expenses for establishing enterprises
1- Enterprise Establishment Expenses are expenses disbursed to establish an enterprise. For purposes of income tax, enterprise establishment expenses can be deducted entirely in the first taxable year. 
Expenses for establishing an enterprise and developing an initial enterprise and developing an enterprise are expenditures on achievements in establishing an enterprise, advertising, directing and supervising offices, training staff, prefinancing and technical assistance.
b- Expenditure as per the terms of the company, the expenditure at the time of the formation of the company, the addition or decrease of the company's capital, or the expenditure incurred in any similar operation (restructuring of the company, dissolution of the company, merger...)Expenses as the circumstances of the company are criminal, stamp duty on the company's provisions (e.g., capital gains, dissolution of the merger, etc.), the royalties of the formation of the company, and the costs of the legal form of the proclamation.
c- Expenditure on the occasion of signing a mortgage contract.
d- Long-term assets inheritance expenses, in which only speculative taxes on ownership or occupancy, commissions, and legal expenses are the share of the assets or expenses in the taxable year in which those expenses were incurred.
	2- The following expenses are not defined as enterprise establishing expenses:
a- Expenses that are usually incurred in the taxable year (expenses of advertising goods or services...)។
b- Preliminary and assembly costs that are charged in the purchase price of the long-term assets involved.

Article 24 .- Purchases
1- Purchases can be divided into three categories:
A- Purchases that can be stored, such as supplies and goods.
B- Purchases that cannot be stored or are not stored, such as water, electricity, fuel and lubricants, small office supplies, small tools that are replaced frequently (at the end of the tax year, this type of purchase is not regulated by the stock account, but must be recorded by the expense account that has been previously checked).
C- Purchases of services, which are amounts paid to subcontractors for the production, conversion, long-term storage of products or repairs, maintenance, etc. The subcontractors may be manufacturers who only receive labor costs (the buyer provides the raw materials), industrial subcontractors, or subcontractors who supply goods or services (usually public works, building construction, etc.).
2- Purchase records: Purchases shall be recorded in the accounting records upon receipt of the invoice according to the actual cost of the purchase as follows:
A- For assets purchased locally, the cost of purchase is the actual cost of the enterprise in purchasing, which includes the purchase price plus incidental costs directly related to the purchase, such as transportation and insurance costs, and excluding any discounts that the supplier has agreed to provide.
B- For imported long-term assets, the cost of purchase includes:
- Purchase price
- Transportation costs
- Insurance costs incurred abroad
- Non-refundable customs duties or taxes
- Transit costs, commissions and brokerage fees paid to enterprises located abroad (including bank commissions, litigation costs and settlement costs)
- Miscellaneous costs after the entry of the asset into the country, such as transit costs, commissions and brokerage fees paid to domestic enterprises, transportation costs and insurance costs from the border to the warehouse.
3- Customs records: Customs duties on imported and exported goods shall be recorded in the customs accounts and shall not be recorded in the purchase accounts.
4- Value-added tax records shall be applied as follows:
A- For enterprises making non-taxable supplies, the principles as set out in paragraph 5 of this Article shall apply.
B- For enterprises making taxable supplies:
- For input tax that can be claimed as a credit, it shall be recorded in the receivable account.
- For input tax that cannot be claimed as a credit, it shall apply as set out in paragraph 5 of this Article.
- For input tax that has been recorded in the receivable account as set out in subparagraph 1 of this Article, but later becomes credit-invalid due to a disallowed provision, the enterprise shall record the input tax in the relevant asset account or purchase account. However, if the input tax cannot be recorded in any asset account or purchase account, the enterprise may record the input tax as an expense in the taxable year in which the credit is disallowed.
5- Other tax records: These include special taxes, public lighting taxes, and accommodation taxes. These taxes are not deductible from the purchase price. If these taxes are reflected in the invoice for the purchase of an asset or service, they must be added to the purchase price and recorded in the relevant expense or asset account.
6- Withdrawal of goods or services for business use: Withdrawal of goods or services for business use is not considered a sale, but must be clearly documented.
7- Purchase records and control of purchases, inventories, and suppliers' accounts: Like other expenses, purchases are recorded in the taxable year in which the purchase occurs. Based on the principle of recording purchases on the date of receipt of the invoice, there is a gap at the end of the taxable year, namely the occurrence of the first occurrence of the invoice, the receipt of goods, and the accounting entry. In this case, the inventory opportunity should be regulated as follows:
A- If the invoice has not been received but the goods have been delivered, a debt of an estimated amount is recorded in the payables account (suppliers - invoice not yet received) by debiting the purchases account.
B- If the invoice has been recorded but the goods have not been received, the goods are recorded in the inventory at the end of the taxable year using the stock in transit account.

Article 25.- External service expenses
1- Leases include:
a- Lease of real estate or movable property for business use: This may include the following payments:
- Wages and other expenses for the lease of real estate or movable property for business use (including those paid under a financial lease contract) are deductible in the taxable year in which these wages and expenses are paid, regardless of the date on which the actual payment is made.
- Advance payments: These amounts shall be recorded on the assets side of the balance sheet in the prepaid expenses account, which shall not affect the results of the taxable year in which the payment is made. These amounts shall be deducted only from the results of the taxable year in which the rental expenses are incurred.
- Guarantees: Amounts paid as guarantees shall be recorded on the assets side of the balance sheet. Guarantees may only affect the results of the taxable year in which they are actually received by the owner of the leased property.
- For tax purposes, only the interest paid by the enterprise for the lease of property is non-deductible.
B- Rental of accommodation: Accommodation fees are deductible according to the purpose of use of the accommodation. For accommodation that serves the needs of the enterprise's employees, the fees are deductible expenses and are additional benefits received by the employees. For accommodation that serves other needs, the fees are non-deductible expenses.
2- Maintenance and repair work: In principle, only maintenance and repair work that can make the asset work or be used normally or operate until the end of its depreciation period is allowed to be deducted as current expenses. In particular, any improvement, which is a repair to make the asset more valuable or increase its productivity or extend its useful life beyond its original intended life, must be recorded in the relevant asset account.
3- Insurance expenses: Expenses paid on asset risk insurance contracts (accidents, fires, storms, etc.) or contingent liability insurance contracts (commercial or civil liability) are allowed to be deducted for the taxable year in which the expense is incurred (calculated according to the number of days the insurance contract covers in the taxable year).
4- Commissions and external benefits:
A- Commissions and other benefits paid: The amount of money paid for services provided to the enterprise is allowed to be deducted only if the reality and usefulness of these services are demonstrated and the amount is not exaggerated.
B- Royalties for concessions, patents, trademarks or trade names, business rights, copyrights and similar rights: This type of royalties is deductible in cases where it is not an expense for the purchase of any asset and the amount is not exaggerated.
5- Missions: Mission expenses can be allowed to be deducted if the mission really serves the business and the amount is not excessive compared to the type and size of the business or compared to the net income achieved. As for miscellaneous expenses (such as travel and missions that are both business and leisure travel), deductions are allowed only to the extent that they serve the business. Expenses for travel and missions abroad or for attending or organizing conferences, seminars, meetings, etc. may be allowed for deduction if the benefit to the enterprise of these expenses is clearly demonstrated and is directly related to the business of the enterprise.
6- Hospitality, entertainment or leisure: Expenses for hospitality, entertainment or leisure activities, such as the provision of food, beverages, tobacco, accommodation or any hospitality, are not allowed for deduction.

Article 26.- VAT 
1. VAT paid in the taxable year:
a- Any VAT that is paid by way of fiscal declaration and is a deductible VAT category is allowed to be deducted in the taxable year in which these VAT is paid or is payable.
b- For VAT paid without filing a fiscal declaration, it is allowed to be deducted in the taxable year in which these VAT satisfies the various conditions of deductible expenses.
2- Withholding VAT: Enterprises can deduct all VAT paid by enterprises, including patent tax, VAT related to import or export, special VAT, VAT for public lighting, VAT on accommodation, VAT on unauthorized inputs as credit, stamp duty, property tax, tax on unused land, tax on advertising billboards, and taxes on means of transportation. 
3- Non-deductible VAT: Income tax prepayments, income taxes, minimum taxes, and other non-deductible VAT taxes of the enterprise (general withholding tax, payroll tax).

Article 27.- Bankruptcy 
	1-Any deduction of expenditure in accordance with Article 6 of the Law on Fiscal Affairs is possible unless the facts prove the burden of the taxpayer has arisen, the result of the economic activity involved in the expenditure digit has occurred, and the amount which is the burden of the taxpayer can be clearly shown. Even if the likelihood of incurring these costs or losses is high or specific.
	2-For domestic banks, the requirement for doubtful credit is defined as in the table below:
