3. Comply with the laws and regulations on banking and financial institutions.
4. Compliance with the Rules and Regulations on Banking and Financial Institutions
5. Lose Compliance with the Rules and Regulations on Banking and Financial Institutions
	3-The provisions permitted in this Article do not apply to the transaction of financial obligations. 
	4. Domestic banks shall remand in the taxable year the amount of the credit allowed to be deducted in respect of suspected debts, including interest and other expenses, upon receipt of repayment of those suspected debts.

Article 28.- Salaries and similar expenses
1- Conditions of deduction: Salaries and fringe benefits may be allowed to be deducted in cases where these amounts are reasonable and related to the actual work of the employee.
2- Expenses to be recorded in the taxable year: Salaries and fringe benefits are annual expenses for a business that are allowed to be deducted only in the taxable year in which the expenses are actually incurred. In particular, at the end of the taxable year, there may be some salaries paid in advance or not paid to employees, which are recorded in the prepaid expenses account or accounts payable.
3- Other benefits are amounts received from performing work for a certain period of time, such as:
A- Benefits of salaried employees who are not managers as detailed in the Prakas on payroll tax.
B- Benefits of members of a joint-stock enterprise and sole proprietorship: Since members of a joint-stock enterprise or sole proprietorship are engaged in the business and the income of the business is wholly owned by the members or proprietors, the expenses for benefits to members or proprietors are not deductible and are not considered as distributions of dividends. However, in cases where the tax administration has reasonable grounds to believe that pre-deduction of any amount from the income may cause difficulties, the tax administration may require the taxpayer to pay the tax immediately.
C- Benefits given to other members of the family of the sole proprietorship owner: Benefits given to the children, in-laws and relatives of the proprietor are deductible as long as they are in return for genuine work, the amount is not exaggerated and they are actually paid.
D- Benefits of managers of legal entities: Since these managers have supervisory and decision-making powers, the benefits they receive may be exaggerated. The following criteria may be used to demonstrate and determine the amount of this overstatement (the portion of the remuneration considered as overstatement is a non-deductible expense):
- The benefits of the activities performed by the manager and the responsibilities assigned to the manager
- The development of the enterprise's income
- The size of the enterprise
- A comparison of this remuneration with the remuneration paid to managers of enterprises with similar jobs in enterprises with similar business activities in the region or with the remuneration paid to employees with similar positions and functions in the enterprise
- A comparison between the total remuneration paid to the manager and the salaries paid to all employees who are entitled to a salary.
4- It is considered to have been paid in the taxable year if there is a debit entry in the expense account and a credit entry in the partnership (shareholder) account or the account of the relevant individual. For the purposes of this paragraph, credits and recorded credits refer to the fact that the enterprise has previously recorded a debt to pay non-resident creditors, including:
a- Payments to lessors or agents through a bank account in the name of the non-resident owner of the enterprise.
B- Payment of interest to the savings account of a non-resident taxpayer.
C- Deposit of pension or annuity from an insurance company or pension fund into the bank account of a non-resident taxpayer.
D- Deduction of the amount to be paid by the resident taxpayer (or a person considered to be a resident taxpayer) of the amount owed by the non-resident taxpayer.
E- Amount recorded as a credit to the social security account.
5- All social expenses stipulated in the Labor Law are deductible.

Article 19.- Interest 
Interest refers to an amount that is a debt obligation that a debtor is required to pay to a creditor, including a down payment, premium, or similar payment as to borrowing money, except for the repayment of the principal. Obligations to account balances to be repaid in currency and bonds.
	1- Interest of money borrowed from the plaintiffs:
a- Interest on money borrowed by the enterprise from the trustees for the purpose of servicing the needs in the business is allowed to be deducted in the taxable year in which the interest becomes liability to be repaid. In this case, the enterprise must prove the authenticity of the borrowed money by having verifiable evidence, such as a loan contract with a specific date and which clearly defines the form of repayment of principal and interest.
b- Interest on loans borrowed from the petitioner for the personal needs of the owner of the enterprise is not allowed to be deducted. In the case of an individual enterprise, this situation occurs if the account of the owner of the enterprise has an equity balance (the terminal balance of the enterprise owner's account of any taxable year is to be equal to the principal balance of that taxable year, minus the capital and profit additions in the taxable year, and plus the losses in the taxable year and the previous withdrawal of the owner of the enterprise). In this situation, the enterprise may be required to take out a borrowing in order to withstand the lack of cash caused by the advance withdrawal of the enterprise owner of an amount in excess of the amount that the enterprise profits or the enterprise has a loss in the taxable year.
2- Amounts paid for as dividends of the enterprise's own capital or interest repaid to the account of the owners of the individual enterprise shall not be allowed to be deducted.
3. Restrictions on Deduction of Interest: The restriction on deduction of interest for any taxable year is the maximum amount of interest allowed to be deducted in that taxable year and is calculated according to Figures A + B, where:
A = Interest income earned or received in the taxable year.
B = 50 (fifty) percent of net income, excluding interest income and interest expenses.
Interest expense that is not allowable to be deducted in the interim taxable year may be referred to as interest expense for the next taxable year within the same limit until the fifth taxable year, in the order of the year in which the interest accrued.

Article 30.- Special expenses 
1- Various deceased include additional taxes, interest, monetary fines, and penalties that enterprises have suffered due to non-compliance with the law and various moral codes.
a- Additional taxes, interest, and monetary penalties from non-fulfillment of fiscal obligations.
b- Customs penalties.
c- Fines for violations of toll laws or economic regulations.
d- Penalties executed on the individual's personal offense.
d- A penalty, which is a punishment for a violation of public regulation or a criminal offense.
2- Gifts: Gifts made by the enterprise as irreducible expenses.
3- Miscellaneous Subsidies: Subsidies refer to the allowance for meeting the cost of insuring the business that the enterprise has done even in such a goal.
For the purposes of income tax, this expense is allowed to be deductible only in cases where the irrevocableness of the debt is manifestly proved (attempting to present debt collection documents or there is clear evidence of an attempt to collect or obtain the amount owed by the debtor) and that debt is written off from the accounting books of the enterprise. Abandonment of debt is an act of mismanagement that is not allowed to be deducted. 
5- Special Expenses: Losses of goods and other expenses normally are deductible only in cases where these losses and expenses occur within the framework of the normal business processes of the enterprise. Any loss and expense as an unusual act of management is irreparable.

Article 31.- Charitable Contributions
1-For purposes of income tax, charitable contributions refer to donations in cash or as objects to the following not-for-profit activities:
a- Any organization that is organized and operated for purely religious, charitable, scientific, literary or educational purposes and no share of the property or income is used for private benefit.
b- Any association in which the income of those associations is not utilized for the private benefit of the individual shareholder or physical.
2. The level of permission to deduct charitable contributions shall apply as follows:
a- The amount of deductible charitable contributions for any taxable year shall not exceed 5 (five) percent of the net income before deducting charitable contributions.
b- The amount of charitable contributions remaining from deductions as provided in syntax A of this second paragraph is no longer permitted to be deducted in any taxable year, and is to be a non-deductible expense for the taxable year in which the amount accrued.

Article 32.- Exclusion and Conditions of Exclusion 
Erosion and discharge conditions are defined as follows:	
1- The procurement (purchase, acquisition, input...) of long-term assets does not result in a decrease in net assets because the expenditure is reimbursed in return in the assets of the enterprise a new asset which does not affect the taxable result. 
2- Depreciation is the recording of the depreciation of assets resulting from use, use time, technological changes, or other causes, by making an allocation of the depreciation of assets according to the planned period of use (useful life) based on a depreciation plan. 
3- For the purpose of income tax, deductible deductibles must meet the following five conditions:
A- depreciation is to be done only on long-term assets recorded in the assets of the enterprise's balance sheet.
B- Liquidation must only be done on long-term assets that suffer depreciation.
c- The abortion must be done on the basis and within the limits of the cost.
d- The abortion shall be calculated in the manner as provided for in Articles 33 to 37 of this post.
Turnovers are done exactly by the enterprise.
Land is not immovable property.	
4- In determining taxable income, a deduction is given to the owner of the physical asset or the lessee of the physical asset in case the lessee is responsible for the risk of loss or damage of the property.

Article 33.- Long-term assets that allow for depreciation. 
Long-term assets are the portions (or components) of assets for long-term use in business activities and retaining the same original appearance from the time of deployment until the time of retirement.
A- Target: All types of assets (supernatural assets or monetary assets) that the enterprise has purchased or produced, not for conversion to sell or not for sale, but for long-term use (the car that the enterprise sells the car buys for resale is a share of the purchase and the vehicle for use in the business of the enterprise is a long-term asset).
b- Duration: The retention of an asset in a business unit is defined as continuous if it lasts for more than one year, counting from the time of initial deployment. 
2- Difference between long-term assets and expenses: Expenditures conceived as the incorporation of a new share into the assets of the enterprise are long-term assets as to the assets already recorded in the balance sheet, the enterprise is subject to the second paragraph of Article 25 of this post.
	3- Long-term assets are divided as follows:
A- Supernatural assets: 
Convertible supernatural assets are:
- Enterprise Creation Expense
- R&D expenses: are the R&D expenses that an enterprise has undertaken for the purpose of employing a business. In the case of recording as a long-term asset, any R&D project must be identifiable and isolated and have a firm expectation of commercial benefit
- Trademark or trademark notices, business rights, authors' rights and copyrights, computer software (protected by law)
- Commercial Funds 
- Supernatural long-term assets.
Non-fungible supernatural assets include: securities, equity, long-term assets, disposable finance, and land use rights... ។
b- Physical assets: Physical assets are divided into the following four classes:
- Class 1 property: includes constructions, including buildings and structures, constructions that are components of buildings, roads, railways, and shipping vessels; 
- Tier 2 assets: including computers, information technology systems, electronic equipment, and data storage equipment.
- Category 3 property: Includes cars, trucks, furniture, and office equipment 
- Tier 4 assets: Includes all types of other physical assets, other than Tier 1, Tier 2 and Tier 3 assets.
In the case of any physical asset that is featured, the Directorate General of Taxation can determine the way of disposition.

Article 34.- Methods of recording long-term assets
1- For supernatural assets and assets in paragraph 1: The enterprise shall separately record in account each asset the amount owed to that asset (purchase fees, amounts, reimbursements, sustained improvements...)។ 
2- For physical assets in Class 2, Class 3 and Class 4: Enterprises are required to record in the joint asset account for each class and must record in the amount unrealized, all amounts as subject to additional acquisition of assets (additional purchases, additional acquisitions, additional inputs...) and all amounts as subject to the discharge of assets in the taxable year.
3- Natural resources: Expenditures on exploration and development, including interest expenditures on exploration and development, are recorded in the accounting of natural resources. 
4- Long-term agriculture (biological assets):
A- Agricultural crops: Agricultural crops shall be recorded in the biological asset accounts the various expenditures directly associated with cultivation, including expenditures on development and cultivation, and expenditures on the provision of infrastructure for cultivation.
b- Animal Husbandry: Animal husbandry shall be recorded into the biological asset account the various expenditures directly related to animal husbandry, including interest expenditures related to the development and rearing of animal husbandry and the cost of setting up infrastructure for animal husbandry. 
5- In case long-term assets are used in business as well and used outside the business, the enterprise shall apply the following: 
a- The use of long-term assets for serving the personal needs of the owner of the enterprise or providing to an employee or subordinate is considered to have supplied the service at market value (recorded in nominal income). In this case, the provision of the employee is permitted as a deductible expense and is taxed on additional benefits.
b- In the case of a sole proprietorship or a co-owned enterprise, the use of its own land and buildings for doing business, the enterprise shall not be recorded in the balance sheet nor shall it be treated as a lease. Includes all persons named in a family book issued by competent authorities.
c- For an enterprise that has complied with the rules as set out in syntax A of this paragraph, the diversified use of long-term assets recorded in the balance sheet has no effect whatsoever on the depreciation.

Article 35.- Cancellations shall be made on the basis and within the limits of costs. 
The sum of the depreciation of any asset cannot exceed the cost of the asset, even if the revaluation is greater than the cost of the asset. For the purposes of this paragraph, the cost refers to the original value of an asset at the time and at the place where that asset is recorded in the accounting register incorporated into the assets of the enterprise. 
2. The cost or historical description of the assets to be included as assets of the enterprise is determined as follows:
a- For assets acquired by the enterprise, the value of the assets purchased by:
- Accounting for purchase costs, subtracting discounts, plus nominal costs (tariffs and related expenses, transportation, transit and warehousing costs, long-term asset acquisition costs, surcharges, transportation insurance...) and assembly costs necessary to put the assets into operation.
- General expenses and financial expenses as long-term assets are not included in the cost of the purchase. 
- In case of delayed payment, the asset value to be recorded shall be based on the agreed fee, so that the payment shall not be subject to the form of payment at a later date, even if the value is to be repaid up or decreased.
b- For assets produced by the enterprise, it shall be determined according to the cost of production by:
- The actual cost of production shall be recorded in the accounting register as the actual cost of production, which is the cost of purchasing the materials and supplies used, plus all direct costs (labour costs, external service costs) and indirect costs of production in such a manner as those costs are determined and reasonably included in the cost of production of that asset. 
- Production costs shall not include the costs of production, general sales and management, research and development, and financial expenses. Separately, the production costs of large assets, such as the construction of industrial plants, the cultivation or long-term rearing of animal husbandry, the interest on various debts provided in the construction, cultivation or rearing of these shall be allowed to be accrued only from the time of initial borrowing until the time of production.
c- For assets acquired by an enterprise from the State, public collective, or private investors, it shall be recorded in the accounting register at the contingency value, as defined in the contingency agreement.
d- For assets acquired by the enterprise without payment, it shall be recorded in the accounting register at market value or the fee at which the independent enterprise transacts together. 
3- VAT on the added value paid on the purchase or manufacture of an asset which is not allowed as a VAT credit on inputs is allowed to be included in the cost of the asset.

Section 36.- Normal Manner 
	The typical way of diverging long-term assets is defined as follows:
1- Supernatural assets: All supernatural assets must be treated in a manner proportional to the useful life of those assets, or 10 (ten) percent per annum if the useful life cannot be determined.
2- Physical assets: 
A- Class 1 assets: To be disposed of separately in an equal manner at the rate of 5 (five) percent per annum of procurement allowance (cost).
b- Tier 2 assets: To be depreciated in a sequentially decreasing manner at the rate of 50 (fifty) percent of the depreciation basis per annum.
c- Tier 3 assets: To be depreciated in a sequentially decreasing manner at the rate of 25 (twenty-five) percent of the depreciation basis per year.
d- Tier 4 assets: To be depreciated in a sequentially decreasing manner at the rate of 20 (twenty) percent of the depreciation basis per year.
3- Natural Resources: The amount of depreciation that is allowed to be deducted in any taxable year is calculated by taking the balance of the natural resource account to multiply the divide between the amount produced in the taxable year and the estimated amount of gross product that can be extracted from that resource.
4- Long-Term Agriculture:
A- Rubber crops: Allowed to be planted within 20 years at the following rates:

b- Agricultural crops other than rubber: The amount of deduction allowed in any taxable year shall be calculated in a proportional manner according to the life of the beneficiary or 5 (five) per annum by selecting whichever option is sooner.

Article 37 .- When depreciation begins
1- Depreciation of assets using the straight-line method shall be applied as follows:
A- Depreciation shall be carried out from the time the asset is put into service and shall end when the asset is fully depreciated (at which time the accumulated depreciation shall be equal to the cost of the asset). The end point may also occur before the full depreciation date, as in the case of the disposal of an asset by sale, scrapping or destruction. Assets put into service during any taxable year shall be allowed to be depreciated for the full year.
B- For the year of completion of depreciation:
- In the case of an asset being disposed of by the enterprise, the depreciation amount shall be zero
- In the case of an asset having reached the end of its useful life, the depreciation amount shall be equal to the unamortized balance of the asset account of that asset. However, if this balance is greater than the annual depreciation amount (continuous improvement), the related asset is considered to have increased its useful life and is depreciated continuously until this balance is less than the annual depreciation amount, then it is depreciated to complete the depreciation.
2- Depreciation of assets using the declining balance depreciation method shall be applied as follows:
a- Depreciation shall be made from the time the asset is put into use. Assets put into use during any period of the taxable year shall be allowed to be depreciated for the full year.
b- The depreciation amount allowed to be deducted for each class is equal to the depreciation base multiplied by the depreciation rate for each class.
c- The depreciation base for the first year of business is equal to the total cost of the assets in the combined asset account for each class put into use.
d- For subsequent taxable years, the depreciation base shall be equal to the opening balance of the combined asset account plus the cost of assets put into use in the taxable year, minus the sale price of assets withdrawn in the taxable year.
E- In a taxable year, if any asset in a combined asset account is removed or sold from the business, the enterprise shall deduct from the depreciation base of the combined asset the cost of the removed or sold asset:
- If such recording causes the combined asset account balance to become negative, the enterprise shall record as taxable income an amount equal to this negative balance, and the combined asset account balance shall be adjusted to zero
- At the end of the taxable year, if in any combined asset account there are no assets left, the positive balance of the combined asset account shall be recorded as a deductible loss, and the combined asset account balance shall be adjusted to zero.
3- Depreciation of long-term natural or agricultural resources: An enterprise shall begin to depreciate long-term natural or agricultural resources in the year in which production commences. For the purposes of this paragraph, the year in which production commences refers to the year in which the enterprise receives income from the long-term natural or agricultural resource business. For long-term assets purchased or created after the year of commencement of production, the enterprise shall depreciate at the end of the taxable year in which the assets are put into use in the manner set forth in paragraphs 1 and 2 of Article 36 of the Prakas. If a long-term natural resource or agricultural business is terminated in any taxable year, the enterprise is permitted to deduct as an expense in the taxable year the value of all remaining assets, including exploration costs, development costs, cultivation costs, and animal husbandry costs.

Article 38.- Depreciation is actually made by the enterprise
1- In each taxable year, the enterprise must make depreciation to ensure depreciation for deduction in that taxable year, regardless of whether there is sufficient or insufficient taxable income for deduction. Depreciation must be actually made by the enterprise on a historical basis. In the event that at the end of a taxable year, the enterprise evaluates its assets at their current fair value (takes a detailed inventory), the enterprise must notify the tax administration of the results of the evaluation. For tax purposes, if the results of the evaluation result in a change in the fair value of the assets in the taxable year, the excess of the revaluation shall be considered taxable income and an additional basis for further depreciation.
2- The amount of deductible depreciation must be calculated in accordance with the provisions set forth in this Chapter and recorded in the depreciation calculation table of the annual income tax return for each taxable year.
3- The enterprise is not allowed to postpone the depreciation of any asset.
4- The depreciation amount or any part of the depreciation amount for any taxable year that is not recorded in the depreciation calculation table of the annual income tax return is not allowed to be deducted in another taxable year.
5- The depreciation that is excluded from deductible expenses as stated in paragraph 4 of this Article is considered to have been made regularly for the purpose of calculating the excess or deficiency of the sale price.
Example 7:
A- An enterprise purchased a warehouse on October 15, 2004, which cost 400,000,000 riels.
B- The enterprise depreciated the warehouse regularly using the straight-line depreciation method at a rate of 5% for a useful life of 20 years, except in 2006 because in that taxable year the enterprise incurred a serious loss.
C- The warehouse was sold on June 10, 2018 for 150,000,000 riels.
D- The situation regarding the calculation of depreciation of the excess or deficiency value of the warehouse is as follows:
- Depreciation rate: 5% (the warehouse has a useful life of 20 years and is a Class 1 tangible asset)
- Depreciation is recorded as an expense for each year:
- Depreciation in 2004 = 400,000,000 Riel x 5%
= 20,000,000 Riel (the year of commencement of depreciation is equal to the annual depreciation)
- Depreciation in 2005 = 20,000,000 Riel
- Depreciation in 2006 = 0 Riel
- Depreciation in 2007 = 20,000,000 Riel
- Depreciation in 2008 = 20,000,000 Riel
- Depreciation in 2009 = 20,000,000 Riel
- Depreciation in 2010 = 20,000,000 Riel
- Depreciation in 2011 = 20,000,000 Riel
- Depreciation in 2012 = 20,000,000 Riel
- Depreciation in 2013 = 20,000 000 Riel
- Depreciation 2014 = 20,000,000 Riel
- Depreciation 2015 = 20,000,000 Riel
- Depreciation 2016 = 20,000,000 Riel
- Depreciation 2017 = 20,000,000 Riel
- Depreciation 2018 = 0 Riel (year of asset disposal, depreciation is zero).
Undepreciated residual value = Cost (historical) - Depreciated plus reference value
- Cost (historical) = 400,000,000 Riel
- Depreciated plus reference value = 260,000,000 Riel
- Undepreciated residual value = 140,000,000 Riel.
Surplus value = Selling price - Undepreciated residual value
- Selling price = 150,000,000 Riel
- Undepreciated residual value = 140,000,000 Riel
- Surplus value = 10,000,000 Riel.
E- For tax purposes, this excess value must be added to the deferred depreciation amount of 20,000,000 riels in 2006. Therefore, the taxable excess value is 30,000,000 (10,000,000 + 20,000,000) riels.
C- In the case of a shortfall:
If the warehouse is sold for 110,000,000 riels, the shortfall value is:
- Selling price = 110,000,000 riels
- Remaining value not yet depreciated = 140,000,000 riels
- Shortfall value (loss) = 30,000,000 riels.
The shortfall value (loss) that can be deducted for income tax purposes is only 10,000,000 riels, that is, the recorded loss of 30,000,000 riels is reduced by the deferred depreciation amount in 2006 of 20,000,000 riels.
6- Adjustment of income tax return:
A- Going through Example 7, it is seen that the enterprise is subject to income tax on the deferred depreciation amount. For practical implementation, the enterprise must adjust the asset depreciation account of the erroneous taxable year by re-introducing the deferred depreciation amount.
B- For depreciation or provision amounts created in error or exceeding the permitted amount, the enterprise must adjust the erroneous depreciation or provision amounts for the erroneous taxable year.
C- For the cases as stated in Articles A and B of this Article, the enterprise must submit a declaration to adjust the annual income tax declaration in accordance with the provisions of the Tax Law.
D- After the enterprise has implemented the provisions as stated in Articles A, B, and C of this Article, the enterprise may continue to make depreciation or provision in accordance with the principles permitted by the Tax Law.

Article 39.- Special Depreciation
Special depreciation is defined as follows:
1- Special depreciation is allowed to be deducted in the first year of purchase or, later, in the first year of putting into use of a tangible asset. The amount allowed to be deducted is equal to 40 (forty) percent of the capital value of a new tangible asset or a used tangible asset put into use in production or processing. In the same taxable year, the remaining capital value of the tangible asset is allowed to be depreciated according to the normal depreciation method as stipulated in Article 36 of this Prakas.
2- Special depreciation of tangible assets will be deducted to determine the taxable income of a qualified investment project for the taxable year if the investor does not elect to use the right to receive a tax exemption period as stipulated in paragraph 3 of Article 49 of this Prakas.
3- Tangible assets that receive special depreciation deductions must be used for at least 4 taxable years after the taxable year in which the special depreciation is deducted. If the tangible asset is retired before this period, the investor shall record in taxable income an amount equal to the special depreciation amount deducted, reduced by an amount equal to 2 (two) percent of the special depreciation amount deducted for each month or part of the month in which the asset is put into use. This amount shall not affect the book value of the tangible asset for the purpose of determining capital gains under Article 7 of the Tax Law.
Example 8:
An investment enterprise commenced business at the beginning of the tax year 2021 with three machines for use in the business. For income tax purposes, the machines included in the Class 4 asset recorded in the depreciation schedule have a value of 26,000,000 riels (machine 1: 10,000,000 riels, machine 2: 10,000,000 riels, and machine 3: 6,000,000 riels). In 2022, the enterprise sold the third machine to another enterprise for 5,000,000 riels and purchased a prototype machine for 20,000,000 riels. The enterprise has chosen the special depreciation method for the investment process. Depreciation is calculated as follows:
A- Depreciation of the three machines for 2021:
- Special depreciation (26,000,000 x 40%) = 10,400,000 Riel
- Normal depreciation base (26,000,000 - 10,400,000) = 15,600,000 Riel
- Normal depreciation (15,600,000 x 20%) = 3,120,000 Riel
- Total depreciation for 2021 (10,400,000 + 3,120,000) = 13,520,000 Riel
- Depreciation base for 2022 (26,000,000 - 13,520,000) = 12,480,000 Riel.
B- Depreciation for 2022:
- Special depreciation for new machines (20,000,000 x 40%) = 8,000,000 riel
- Normal depreciation base for new machines (20,000,000 - 8,000,000) = 12,000,000 riel
- Normal depreciation base for all machines (revenue from sale of old machines)
(12,480,000 + 12,000,000 - 5,000,000) = 19,480,000 riel
- Normal depreciation amount (19,480,000 x 20%) = 3,896,000 riel
- Total depreciation amount for 2022 (8,000,000 + 3,896,000) = 11,896,000 riel
- Depreciation base for 2023
(12,480,000 + 20,000,000 - 5,000,000 - 11,896,000) = 15,584,000 riel.
C- Adjustment of income tax relating to the sale of the machine in 2022 (after 16 months of use):
Taxable income for 2022 is increased by adjusting the special depreciation deduction by 2% for each month the asset was used. The taxable income to be included for 2022 is calculated as follows:
- Special depreciation (6,000,000 x 40%) = 2,400,000 riel
- Less adjustment for the period the asset was used
(2,400,000 x 2%) x 16 months = 768,000 riel
- Taxable income to be included for 2022
(2,400,000 - 768,000) = 1,632,000 riel.
The excess or deficiency arising from the sale of the machine shall be subject to Section 7 of Chapter 3 of this Prakas.

Article 40.- General principles of surplus and undervalue
1- Pursuant to Article 7 of the Law on Fiscal Taxation, the excess value derived from the sale of various shares of assets while conducting business or upon completion of business as a share of taxable income.
2- Overvaluation or undervaluation arises about the difference between the sale price and the unrealized residual value of the asset, or arises about the revaluation of the asset. 
3- Excess value or undervalue is determined as follows:
This discharge may be a sale (in most cases) foreclosure into another enterprise, devolution, division, gift giving, takeover of the owner of the enterprise while doing business or upon completion of the business, dismantling, destruction, cessation... This discharge may be the intentional act of the enterprise owner or manager, or as a consequence of legal revocation or disaster... ។
B- Recorded Overvalue: A revaluation of assets recorded in accounting for the current value of those assets instead of the old value leads to the occurrence of excess value.
c- The deficit value under the consensus is not allowed to be deducted as an expense unless the deficit value is achieved, as provided in syntax A of this paragraph.

Article 41.- Calculation of excess or undervalue 
1- The sale of any long-term asset constitutes an excess value if the sale price is greater than the remaining unrealized value of the sold asset.
2- The remaining value is not overlooked:
A- For a long-term asset that is depreciated in an equitable manner: The residual value is not depreciated, equal to the historical value of the long-term asset in question, plus a continuous improvement, minus the depreciation amount applied to that asset.
b- For long-term assets that are disposed of in a sequential manner of depreciation: For the release of any type of long-term asset, the enterprise shall not calculate the excess value or undervalue for that asset directly. The enterprise shall comply with the provisions as provided for in the second paragraph of Article 37 of this post, and the excess value or undervalue shall be set aside for the combined asset account in each class only.
	Example 9: 
a- The enterprise has purchased and deployed a number of Tier 1 assets valued at Rs 350,000 000.
b- Computation:
- Depreciation rate: 5% (Tier 1 fiat assets)
- Expenses are recorded as expenses for each year:
- Year 1: 250 000 000 x 5% = 12 500 000 KHR
- Year 2: 250 000 000 x 5% = 12 500 000 KHR
- 3rd year: (250 000 000 + 50 000 000) x 5% = 15 000 00 KHR
- Fourth year: (250 000 000 + 50 000 000) x 5% = 15 000 000 KHR
- Total amounts = 55,000,000 reels.

- Consistent improvement = 50,000,000 KHR
- Transfer sum = 55,000 000 KHR 
- Unrealized price = KHR 245,000
- Selling price = KHR 350,000
- Overvalue (350,000,000 – 245,000,000) = 105,000,000 reais.

Section 42.- Special cases 
Some special cases of overvaluation or undervaluation are defined as follows:
1- Losses from the sale or disposal of property, whether directly or indirectly, among individuals who do not comply with the foreclosure policy, are irreparable expenses. 
2- In the case of an accident entering the company, the excess value or shortfall value shall be calculated according to the actual value of the share certificate or shares conferred in exchange for the incident. Normally, the actual value of the share or share certificate shall be equal to the estimated value of the assets taken by the incident into the accounting books of the affected enterprise.

Article 43.- General principles of withholding taxes
1- In accordance with Article 25, Article 26 and Article 31 of the Fiscal Law, a taxpayer who makes a payment in cash or in order to a foreign or non-citizen shall make a deduction of the tax amount at the time of payment to be paid to the Fiscal Administration. Any transaction that is subject to withholding tax, which is or is to be recorded, is considered settled.
2. A taxpayer or any person as provided for in Article 31 of the Law on Fiscal Taxation, for whom the tax law and ordinance require the withholding and payment of tax on behalf of the taxpayer, shall be designated as a withholding agent.

Section 44.- Withholding tax on payments to taxpayers 
A withholding agent who makes a payment in cash or in kind to a taxpayer is required to withhold and pay taxes at the following determined rates on the pre-withholding payment amount:
1- Rate of 15 (fifteen) percent for:
A- Income from the fulfilment of services, including management or consultation or similar services, refers to income from every economic activity of an individual, other than the production and sale of goods, contracts, rent, sale of property, and other than service activities as provided for in the provisions on payroll taxation. Income from services such as technical services, science, art, academic education, medicine, science, engineering, architecture, study, research, accounting, etc. ។
b- Payments to individuals of the income from the supernatural assets and the payment of all other benefits from the shares in the mineral resources, other than the net income derived from the business on the resources and the dividends subject to separate taxation.
c- Payment of interest paid by a non-local taxpayer to the taxpayer.
For purposes of withholding tax, income from the lease of a move or real estate refers to the cash or objects paid by the lessee in exchange for the use of the move, such as industrial equipment, commerce, technology, science, means of transport, etc. and real estate, such as land, buildings, construction, etc. In this sense, the property shall include the secondary assets of the property, as well as the deeds subject to the laws that provide for the ownership of the land, the right of occupancy, the right of dependence on the property, and the various rights that give rise to the payment in cash or in the object in a fixed amount or in a fixed amount. 
3- A rate of six (six) percent on interest paid by a local bank to a taxpayer with a fixed deposit account. 
4- Rate of 4 (four) percent on interest paid by local banks to taxpayers with indefinite deposit accounts.

Section 45.- Withholding tax on payments to immigrant persons
Except as otherwise provided in the International Agreement on Taxation, a withholding agent who makes a payment of Cambodian source income, as provided in Article 8 of this Declaration, to an immigrant taxpayer shall withhold and pay tax at the rate of 14 (fourteen) percent of the amount payable.

Article 46.- Exemption from tax deduction	
1. Payment in cash or in order in the following cases is not required to make a tax deduction:
a- Interest payable to local banks and payment of tax-exempt income as provided for in Article 10 of this Announcement.
b- Payment to the Government or a governmental body of dowry or wages on real estate or real estate which satisfies both of the following conditions:
- As if the move or property is recorded as state property in the inventory list maintained by the Ministry of Economy and Finance. 
- There must be a certification of the Ministry of Economy and Finance as a revenue paid into the state budget.
c- Payment of the income of a physical individual subject to payroll tax or ancillary benefit tax, as provided in the Regulations on Payroll Taxation.
d- Payment of interest by the Government or a government institution to an individual beneficiary of a loan that the Government of Cambodia or the Minister of Economy and Finance has recognized and approved.
d- Payment of money for the supply of any services valued below 50000 (five) rials.
2- Payments in cash or in kind among taxpayers on a voluntary basis are exempt from withholding tax in the following cases:
a- Income from the provision of various services, including management or consultancy or similar services.
b- Income from supply:
- Shrink-wrap Software
- Site License
- Downloadable Software 
- Software bundled with computer hardware.
c- Income from the rental of real estate or real estate.
For such cases as provided in this paragraph, any payment is permitted withholding tax exemption unless that amount is recorded in an invoice duly issued by the other party to the taxpayer.

Article 47.- Basis for calculation of withholding tax 
1- The basis for calculating withholding tax is the amount to be paid to any individual before withholding tax. 
2- With regard to the payment of money to the foreigner as to the supply of equipment and services, such as the payment for the purchase of machinery from abroad, which includes the cost of purchasing machinery and the assembly fee by the individual technician for the initial operation of the machinery, the basis for calculating the withholding tax is the share of the money as it pertains to the assembly service only.

Article 48.- Duties and responsibilities of the deduction agent 
1- The withholding agent is obliged to file a fiscal declaration and pay the withheld tax to the Fiscal Administration no later than the 20th of the month following the month in which the deduction was made, in the form prescribed by the Fiscal Administration. 
2- Withholding agents who are obliged to withhold tax amounts but have not made tax deductions and payments to the Fiscal Administration are responsible for the undeducted tax amounts, as well as those as stipulated in the Fiscal Law.

Article 49.- Annual income tax rate 
The annual income tax rate is determined as follows:
1- The rate of 20 (twenty) percent on the taxable income achieved by the individual.
2- A rate of 30 (thirty) percent on taxable income achieved under petroleum and natural gas products sharing contracts or achieved from doing business on natural resources, including forests, minerals, gold, or other precious stones. 
3- A rate of 0 (zero) percent to the taxable income of qualifying investment projects that are within the tax exemption period.

Article 50.- Income tax pre-payment
	Enterprises that are taxable under the declared regime, including qualifying investment projects that have expired the income tax exemption period, are obliged to pay a monthly income tax prepayment at the rate of 1 (one) percent of the turnover, including VAT, except for value-added VAT achieved in the previous month.

Article 51.- Minimum tax
	1- The minimum tax shall be determined at the rate of 1 (one) per cent of the annual turnover, inclusive of VAT, excluding VAT on value-added tax, and shall be paid at the time of payment of the annual income tax. The minimum tax may be reduced by the annual income tax paid in accordance with the rules as provided in Article 37, Article 38 and Article 39 of the Law on Fiscal Taxation. Enterprises that are deemed not to have held accounting duties properly are obliged to pay minimum taxes.
2. Qualifying investment projects with independent audit reports are subject to minimum tax exemption.

Section 52.- Advance tax on dividend distribution 
	1. Pursuant to Article 23 of the Law on Fiscal Affairs, if any enterprise allocates dividends from its income before annual income tax to a domestic shareholder or a foreign shareholder, that enterprise shall be required to pay a prepaid tax on the distribution of dividends in an amount equal to the multiplier of the inflated dividend amount according to the income tax rate multiplied by the annual income tax rate as provided in Article 49 of this Announcement. 	
	2. Advance taxes on dividend allocations as provided in this Article do not apply to: 
a- Income from insurance premiums or continuing insurance on other assets or risks in the Kingdom of Cambodia, as provided in paragraph 1 of Article 21 of the Law on Fiscal Affairs.
b- Qualified investment projects that are within the annual income tax exemption period, including accumulated retained annual income that is within the tax exemption period of the qualifying investment scheme that existed prior to 2020.
	3- Tax credits paid under paragraph 1 of this Article shall be allowed as tax credits for deduction of allocated taxable annual income tax. If the tax credit exceeds the annual income tax amount, that excess amount is allowed to be forwarded for deduction against income tax of the succeeding taxable year.            
	4. Dividends taxed under paragraph 1 of this Article, when continuing to distribute, are no longer subject to pre-tax on dividend allocations.
	5- In a current taxable year, in case an enterprise has a dividend allocation in which those dividends are taken out of different incomes, including income paid on annual income tax at the rate of 20 (twenty) percent or 30 (thirty) percent, and/or profits in the current year, the enterprise shall apply as follows:
a- Step 1: To be removed from the income saved after payment of annual income tax at the rate of 20 (twenty) percent or the rate of 30 (thirty) percent.
b- Step 2: To be removed from income in the current taxable year before paying annual income tax.

Article 53.- Foreign Tax Credits 
1. Exile taxpayers who have received income from foreign sources and have paid taxes according to foreign tax laws are entitled to tax credits for deducting income tax payable in the Kingdom of Cambodia. 
2- In order to calculate the amount of tax payable in the Kingdom of Cambodia, before deducting this tax credit, the total amount of taxable income received from Cambodian and foreign sources must be taken into account.
3- Tax credits are set apart for tax credits paid by Cambodian exiles in each foreign country. The tax credits allowed to be deducted for the taxable year and for taxes paid in any foreign country are the lowest among the following:
a- Taxes actually paid in any foreign country.
b- The amount derived from the deduction of the total taxable income tax from all sources for the same period, calculated at the rate of tax as provided in Article 49 of this Article, to multiply the difference between the taxable income received in that country and the total taxable income from all sources. 
4- The foreign tax credit may be given unless the taxpayer has filled out a form as well as provided various documents required by the Fiscal Administration, in particular the affidavit of the taxpayer abroad and the Foreign Fiscal Administration.

"Article 54.- Calculation of taxable income
1- Recapture and deduction of various items: In general, the laws and legal regulations on taxation are not completely consistent with the accounting rules. These discrepancies lead to taxable income not being equal to accounting profit. Therefore, in order to calculate taxable income of a given taxable year, an enterprise must take the pre-tax accounting results of that taxable year and make the following adjustments:
A- Recapture the following non-deductible expenses:
- Accounting depreciation expenses
- Entertainment, entertainment and leisure expenses
- Increase in provisions
- Gifts and other subsidies
- Loss on sale of long-term assets according to the accounting records
- Other non-deductible expenses
B- Recapture the following taxable income that is not recorded as income in the accounting records:
- Free supply of goods and services
- Gifts and other subsidies
- Excess value of sale of long-term assets according to the income tax regulations
- Other taxable income not recorded in the accounting records.
C- Deduct expenses not recorded in the accounting records but deductible expenses in the year:
- Depreciation allowed under the Tax Law
- Special depreciation allowed under the Income Tax Regulations
- Decrease in provisions
- Loss on sale of long-term assets under the Income Tax Regulations
- Other expenses that are allowed to be deducted.
D- Deduct income recorded in the accounting records but not taxable income in the taxable year:
- Income on dividends received from resident taxpayers
- Gain on sale of long-term assets according to the accounting records
- Other income recorded in the records but not taxable income in the taxable year.
2- After making the adjustments as stipulated in paragraph 1 of this Article, the enterprise shall calculate the charitable contributions that are deductible under the Income Tax Regulations for the taxable year by applying the following procedures:
A- Calculate the basis for calculating charitable contributions by taking the charitable contributions spent in the taxable year and adding the result after the adjustments calculated in paragraph 1. of this Article.
B- Calculate the maximum deductible charitable contribution for the taxable year by multiplying the result calculated in paragraph A of this Article by 5 (five) percent.
C- Deductible charitable contributions for the taxable year:
- In the case where the amount of charitable contributions in the taxable year is less than or equal to the maximum deductible charitable contribution for the taxable year, no adjustment is made to the charitable contribution expense.
- In the case where the amount of charitable contributions in the taxable year is more than the maximum deductible charitable contribution for the taxable year, the difference shall be considered a non-deductible expense for the taxable year. This difference shall be added back to the adjusted result calculated in accordance with paragraph 1 of this Article to obtain the result after deducting charitable contributions.
3- The enterprise shall then calculate the result after adjusting for interest by:
A- Calculate net income other than interest by taking the result after deducting charitable contributions and adding the interest expense in the taxable year and subtracting it from the interest income in the taxable year.
B- Calculate the maximum deductible interest expense in a taxable year by taking the interest income in the taxable year plus 50 (fifty) percent of the net non-interest income as calculated in paragraph a of this paragraph.
C- In the case of interest expenses in a taxable year exceeding the maximum deductible interest expense in a taxable year, the enterprise shall calculate the non-deductible interest expense in a taxable year by taking the interest expenses in the taxable year minus the maximum deductible interest expense in a taxable year calculated in paragraph b of this paragraph. The interest expenses remaining from this deduction shall be considered as interest expenses for the following taxable year up to the fifth taxable year in the order in which the interest expenses occurred in the manner as set forth in this paragraph.
D- In the case of interest expenses in a taxable year equal to the maximum deductible interest expense in a taxable year, the interest expenses shall be allowed in full without adjustment.
E- In the case of interest expenses in a taxable year less than the maximum deductible interest expense in a taxable year, the interest expenses in a taxable year shall be fully deductible for the taxable year. If the enterprise has interest expenses remaining from the previous year, the enterprise may deduct them, but the total amount allowed for deduction shall not exceed the maximum interest expenses that can be deducted in the taxable year. In this case, the interest allowance from the previous year that is allowed for deduction shall be deducted from taxable income.
F- Calculate the result after adjusting the interest in the taxable year by taking the result after deducting charitable contributions, plus the non-deductible interest expenses in the taxable year as set forth in paragraph c of this paragraph or deducting the interest allowance from the previous year as set forth in paragraph e of this paragraph.
4- Calculate the taxable income for the taxable year by taking the result after adjusting the interest in the taxable year as set forth in paragraph f of paragraph 3 of this article, minus the losses from previous years allowed under the Tax Law, if any. "

Article 55.- Calculation of income tax
	Income tax is calculated as follows: 
	1- Calculate income tax by taking the taxable income of the taxable year, as calculated in Article 44 of this Announcement, to multiply by the tax rate as provided in Article 49 of this Announcement.
	2- Withdraw the foreign tax credit as provided in Article 53 of this Announcement to foreign enterprises with foreign source income, but not in excess of the income tax as provided in paragraph 1 of this Article.
	3- Withdrawal of prepaid tax on dividend allocations paid by enterprises as provided in Article 52 of this Article, but not in excess of income tax after deduction of foreign tax credits as provided in the second paragraph of this Article.

Section 56.- Calculation of income tax payable or tax credit for a taxable year
	The income tax payable or tax credit for the taxable year is defined as follows:
	1. In the event that the result of the calculation as provided in Article 55 of this Post is greater than the sum of the tax credit withheld as provided in Part 8 of Chapter 3 of this Post and the amount of the income tax prepayment paid by the taxpayer for the taxable year as provided in Article 50 of this Post, the enterprise shall pay the additional amount to the Fiscal Administration.
	2- If the calculation result as provided in Article 55 of this Post is less than the sum of the provisional withholding tax credit as provided in Part 8 of Chapter 3 of this Post and the amount of the income tax prepayment paid by the taxpayer for the taxable year as provided in Article 50 of this Proclamation, the enterprise may use the amount as a credit for deduction against the payment of the income tax arrears in the month following the month in which the annual income tax declaration letter is filed. or income taxes for the following year. 
	3- Before making the payment of tax as provided for in paragraph 1 of this Article or referred to as income tax prepayment as provided for in the second paragraph of this Article, the enterprise must pre-determine the minimum tax liability in the event that the enterprise is subject to minimum tax.

Article 57.- Calculation of minimum tax amount, tax payable or tax credit for a taxable year 
	The minimum tax amount, tax amount payable, or tax credit for the taxable year is defined as follows:
	1- The minimum tax payable for any taxable year may be reduced by the actual income tax paid in that taxable year.
	2- In case the income tax calculated in Article 55 of this Announcement exceeds the minimum tax, the enterprise shall not pay the minimum tax amount and the enterprise shall comply with the provisions as provided in paragraphs 1 and 2 of Article 56 of this Announcement when filing the Fiscal Declaration and paying the annual income tax. 
	3. In case the minimum tax exceeds the income tax, the minimum tax shall be reduced by the tax credit of the enterprise as provided in paragraph 1 of Article 56 of this post (i.e. the sum of the amount of income tax paid by the enterprise for the taxable year as provided in Article 50 of this Post and the tax amount deducted by other enterprises in accordance with the provisions as provided in Part 8 of Chapter 3 of this Post and the reference income tax credit from the previous year, if any), where: 
a- If the minimum tax is more than the tax credit as provided in paragraph 3 of this Article, the enterprise shall pay an additional amount.
b- If the tax credit as provided in paragraph 3 of this Article is more than the minimum tax, the amount is allowed to be referred to as an income tax credit for the next taxable year (income tax prepayment or annual income tax).

Article 58.- Rules on Reference of Losses 
	1- Loss referencing is defined as follows:
a- Losses incurred in any taxable year are treated as a burden and are allowed to be deducted from the income achieved in the next taxable year (the first taxable year of reference for losses).
b- The amount of the deduction in any taxable year shall be equal to the amount of income achieved in that taxable year, without retaining any share of the loss for reference to the following year.
c- Whenever the loss is more than one year, the provisions as provided for in Article A of this paragraph shall be treated for the loss in the order of the year in which the loss occurred.
	2- Conditions of Loss Allowance:
A- Evidence confirming the loss:
- In order to be able to deduct the deduction, the enterprise must calculate the loss in accordance with the law and the tax law and that loss is filled in the annual income tax declaration letter submitted to the Fiscal Administration. 
- An enterprise that is subject to a unilateral deduction of taxation by the Fiscal Administration in any taxable year is not allowed to refer losses from the previous taxable year to a deduction in a taxable year with a unilateral tax determination or to deduction losses in a unilateral tax year to the next taxable year. If the reference period of 5 years has not expired.
- Losses that are allowed to be deducted must be confirmed by documents and accounting registers in accordance with the International Financial Reporting Standards of Cambodia and regulated in accordance with the laws and customs of taxation.
b- Customization of business activities of enterprises:
- Losses of any enterprise may be allowed, only for that enterprise 
- In the case of a change of business activity in which the old activity is to cease the old activity and start another new activity, the loss suffered by the enterprise in its old activity is not allowed to be deducted from the income achieved by the enterprise in its new activity.
c- The taxable year in which the loss reference is applied:
- Losses in any taxable year shall be absolutely deducted from the profit result of the successive taxable year, without allowing the omission of the taxable year in which any profit result is omitted.
- If, for any reason, the enterprise has not referenced all losses or referred only any share to deduct from the profit results of any subsequent taxable year for which the laws and taxation laws allow deduction, the loss cannot be referred to deduct from the profit result of the subsequent taxable year.
- Loss references shall be applied respectively in the order of years in which the loss has occurred for no more than five years.

Article 59.- Accounting duties 
1- Holding accounting lists:
a- Enterprises shall keep records of accounts in accordance with the International Financial Reporting Standards of Cambodia.
b- The principal principles in recording the accounting list are:
- To use a traditional accounting system based on a prescriptive accounting basis. 
- All operations must be recorded in KH or any foreign currency authorized by a competent institution.
- Be billed on every transaction with other individuals. 
- Record the details of the invoice properly in the journal
- Letters of jurisdiction must be dated and prepared in a clear order.
- To record in accounting for every transaction in chronological order in which those transactions occurred 
- Each accounting record shall disclose the source, content, account digits, transaction characteristics, and cosmetic references.
- Every adjustment must be retained with evidence of the adjustment in order to be able to recover the actual amount of cash movement in the account
- Accounting lists must be made in Khmer using Khmer or Latin numerals, but auxiliary accounting lists can be held in Spanish.
When the Fiscal Administration requests to disclose evidence, the enterprise must present every accounting document, inventory list, revenue slip, expense slip, etc. To assert the authenticity of the information posted in the fiscal declaration letter. 
3. Retention of accounting documents: As provided in paragraph 4 of Article 201 of the Law on Fiscal Affairs, a person who is required to hold or keep a list of documents or journals prescribed by the Tax Law or other regulations shall keep these lists or documents for a period of ten years from the end of the taxable year in which these lists or documents record any particular information on the operation of the enterprise. 
4. Enterprises that have engaged in the following activities are considered to be in compliance with the provisions of the tax: 
a- Non-use of the recording system designated by the Fiscal Administration.
b- Non-billing.
c- Failure to provide information or to submit a report upon request. 
d- Not allowing the Fiscal Administration to conduct audits of accounting or other documents. 
d- Failure to maintain accounting and other documents. 
- Attempting to obstruct the determination and collection of taxes.
f- Creating or providing false records, documents, reports, or information. 
- Concealing or deliberately destroying accounting entries, records, documents, reports, or other information.
Fraudulent billing.
- Not allowing the Fiscal Administration to enter business institutions to determine and collect taxes.

Article 60.- Burden of evidence
	1- When a taxpayer has not kept sufficient documents or has not provided sufficient information, the Fiscal Administration has the right to impose a tax on the taxpayer based on the specific information that the Fiscal Administration has.
	2- When the income declared by the taxpayer is substantially different compared to the purchase of the asset or object, which makes the taxpayer's incurred expenses prominent, the Fiscal Administration has the right to determine the tax, based on the basis of the estimated income, appropriate to the size of the expenditure spent on the purchase of the prominent asset or object.

Article 61.- Branches of Foreign Companies
	For the purposes of this post, a foreign company branch refers to a persistent place of business in the Kingdom of Cambodia of a foreign company in which various assets belong to the overseas original company.

Article 62.- Taxable income of a foreign company's branch 
	Taxable income is income derived from doing business in the Kingdom of Cambodia, excluding expenses as provided in Part 5 of Chapter 3 of this Announcement.

Article 63.- Calculation of income tax for branches of foreign companies
	Income tax for a foreign company's branch for any taxable year shall be calculated by multiplying the taxable income in that taxable year by the tax rate as provided for in paragraph 49 of this post.

Article 64.- Advance tax on dividend allocation for branches of foreign companies
	If, in a current taxable year, any branch of a foreign company transfers Cambodian source income abroad, that income:
	1. There shall not be prepaid tax on dividend distributions as provided in Article 52 of this Announcement if the transferred income is income after payment of income tax as provided in Article 63 of this Announcement.
	2- To be taxed in advance on dividend distributions as provided in Article 52 of this Post if the transferred income is income for which income tax has not been paid as provided in Article 63 of this Notice.

Article 65.- Withholding tax on Cambodian source income
	In addition to withholding tax on payments to foreign individuals as provided in Article 44 of this Announcement, a branch of a foreign company shall withhold and pay 14 (fourteen) percent tax as provided in Article 45 of this Announcement when transferring income after payment of tax as provided in Article 63 and Article 64 of this Announcement to a foreign company of origin or payment of Cambodian source income to foreign individuals as provided in Article 8 of this Announcement Burma no longer insures against property or risk in the Kingdom of Cambodia.

Article 66.- Ethics
Any provisions contrary to this proclamation shall be set aside.

Article 67.- Application
The Prime Minister, the Prime Minister, the Secretary-General, the Government Delegation in charge of the Inspector General or the Director General of all Director-Generals, the Director-General of the Secretariat, and the Head of the Intelligence Unit of the Ministry of Economy and Finance shall be in charge of implementing this announcement according to their respective duties from January 1, 2022 onwards.

Article 1.. Objectives
The law sets out the rules, procedures and conditions as well as gathers regulations on taxation in order to regulate the collection of VAT for the benefit of the state budget.

Article 2: Scope
This Law has the scope of application to the control of the collection of all types of VAT provided for in this Law in the Kingdom of Cambodia.

Article 3. Subjects of Taxes
Income tax is an obligation of a taxpayer whose taxable income is earned in a taxable year.

Article 4: Scope of Taxes
Income tax applies to expatriate taxpayers on Cambodian source income and foreign source income and expatriate tax on Cambodian source income.

"Article 5. Definitions
The main terms used in this chapter are defined as follows:
1- Resident taxpayer refers to:
A. A natural person who is domiciled or has his principal place of residence in the Kingdom of Cambodia or who is present in the Kingdom of Cambodia for more than 182 (one hundred and eighty-two) days in any 12 (twelve) month period ending in the current tax year.
B. A legal entity or partnership that is established or controlled in the Kingdom of Cambodia or has its principal place of business in the Kingdom of Cambodia. Non-resident taxpayer refers to any person who is not a resident taxpayer under paragraph 1 of this Article and receives Cambodian-source income.
3- Legal entity refers to enterprises or organizations that engage in business, whether or not officially recognized by a competent authority of the Royal Government. The term legal entity also includes government institutions, religious organizations, charitable organizations, non-profit organizations, political party associations and permanent establishments of non-resident individuals located in the Kingdom of Cambodia. For the purposes of income tax regulations, the term legal entity does not include partnerships or sole proprietorships.
4- Permanent establishment refers to a permanent place of business in the Kingdom of Cambodia, a branch of a foreign company or a resident agency in the Kingdom of Cambodia through which a non-resident individual carries on business. The term permanent establishment also includes any other network or relationship through which a non-resident individual carries on economic activities in the Kingdom of Cambodia. A person may be considered a permanent establishment of a non-resident individual in the Kingdom of Cambodia if that person has and regularly exercises the authority to enter into contracts on behalf of that non-resident individual or plays a principal role in facilitating the conclusion of contracts. A permanent establishment is considered a resident legal entity only in respect of Cambodian-source income.
5- Partnership refers to an enterprise formed by a contract between two or more persons. which brings together the assets or knowledge or activities of such persons to carry on a business or trade together for the purpose of making a profit. In this definition, a partnership includes a general partnership and a limited partnership. The conditions for obtaining a legal entity or legal personality of a partnership as stipulated in the Law on Commercial Enterprises and other laws in force shall not be applied for the purpose of collecting income tax. A partnership does not include a capital company, permanent establishment or sole proprietorship.
6- Sole proprietorship refers to an enterprise established by a single natural person and the assets of the owner of a sole proprietorship are the capital of the sole proprietorship. In this definition, a husband, wife and dependent children shall be considered as a single natural person.
7- Business refers to the economic activities as stipulated in paragraph 9 of Article 190 of this Law of a person who produces and sells goods, supplies services, leases, rents or sells property or other activities, including the activities of institutions or organizations as stipulated in paragraph 3 of this Article.
8- Dividends refers to The cash or property that a legal entity distributes to its shareholders in proportion to their share in the equity of the legal entity, except for the distribution of capital when he is subject to the above conditions, regardless of whether the legal entity has net income in the current year or from previous years.
9- Shareholders refer to individuals who have a share in the equity of a legal entity. For income tax purposes, any legal entity, even if not a capital company, shall be treated as a capital company, and individuals who have a share in the equity of a legal entity or individuals who may receive income as participants in that legal entity shall be considered shareholders of the legal entity.
10- Related persons refer to: a) any member of the taxpayer's family circle; b) an enterprise that directly or indirectly controls the taxpayer or is directly or indirectly controlled by the taxpayer, or that enterprise and the taxpayer are under joint control or a relationship between a permanent establishment and a non-resident taxpayer. The term control means ownership of from 20 (twenty) Percentage of the value or voting rights of the shares in the direct capital of the enterprise. To determine the extent of control of a taxpayer as an individual, all ownership of shares in the direct capital of that individual and the direct or indirect ownership of the taxpayer's spouse shall be taken into account. Notwithstanding the above conditions, the tax administration may judge direct or indirect control on a case-by-case basis to determine whether there is control or not.
11- Qualified investment project refers to an investment project that has received a registration certificate from the Council for the Development of Cambodia or the Subcommittee on Capital and Provincial Investment.
12_ Business alliance refers to joint business activities between resident taxpayers and resident taxpayers or resident taxpayers and non-resident taxpayers or non-resident taxpayers and non-resident taxpayers, from two or more without forming a separate legal entity.
13- Bank refers to any entity that regularly carries out any of the following operations: a. Providing all types of credit to the public with a fee Including financial lease loans. B- Receiving deposits

Article 6: Tax regime and accounting rules
The tax regime and accounting rules are set out as follows:
1- The tax regime of the Kingdom of Cambodia is an automatic declaration regime that requires taxpayers to calculate tax amounts and submit tax declaration forms by themselves.
2. The accounting rules for taxpayers as provided in paragraph 1 of this Article are set out as follows:
a- Small taxpayers must use simple accounting rules.
b- Medium taxpayers and large taxpayers are subject to accounting rules in accordance with the International Financial Reporting Standards of Cambodia.
3- The tax regime and accounting rules shall be determined by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 7. Taxable income
Taxable income is defined as follows:
1- Taxable income is the net income derived from all the results of all types of business operations, including capital gains achieved during or at the end of the business, interest, fees, bribes and other compensations, as well as income from financial assets or investment assets including real estate.
2- For individuals, taxable income is the result arising from the regulation of accounting results in the taxable year in accordance with the provisions of all Articles of this Chapter.
3. For physical individuals, taxable income is the result derived from taking the total amount of income in a taxable year, deducting expenses and donations determined by a decree of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 8. Ukuhlaziywa kwe-tax year
The taxable year is set as follows:
1- For individuals:
a- Income tax is calculated from the accounting results achieved in each calendar year.
b. For a new enterprise commencing business at any time of the calendar year, the accounting results shall be calculated from the date of commencement of business to December 31 of that calendar year.
c. If there are multiple accounting results in a calendar year, the accounting results shall be aggregated as the basis for calculating income tax.
d. An enterprise that is managed by an expatriate entity may apply for a different taxable year from the calendar year.
d- For enterprises that cease business activities, the final accounting results shall be taken into account: from January 1 until the date of cessation of activities as an institution for enterprises that use the calendar year as the tax year, from the beginning of the current tax year until the date of cessation of activities for enterprises that apply for a different tax year from the calendar year.
2-For individual physical, income tax is calculated from the total income achieved in each calendar year.

Article 9... Tax-exempt income
Tax-exempt income is defined as follows:
1- Unless otherwise regulated, income tax shall not apply to:
a- Revenue of the Royal Government or income of the Royal Government.
B- Income of:
Any organization that is organized and operated for purely religious, charitable, scientific, literary, or educational purposes and has no share of its assets or income used for private benefit
Any association in the event that the income of that association is not used for the private or physical benefit of the shareholder.
c. Dividends received from pension enterprises in case the tax payable under Article 20, Article 23 and Article 26 of this Law has already been paid.
3. In case an organization or association as provided for in Paragraph B of Paragraph 1 of this Article has commercial or industrial activities or other businesses which do not affect its basic tax exemption objectives or functions, the income derived from such non-engaging activities shall be taxable in accordance with Article 20 of this Law.
4. Rules and procedures for applying for tax exemption and loss of tax exemption shall be determined by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 10. Determination of income of co-owners and business alliances
1- For co-owned companies and business associations, in determining their income for any taxable year, each member shall think separately of their respective share in the profits, losses, deductions, loans and charitable contributions for that year.
2- The rules and procedures for determining the income of each member of the co-ownership company and business alliance shall be determined by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 11. Allowable troop cuts
The permissible cuts are set as follows:
1. Except for the provisions as provided in Articles 12 to 18 of this Law, the expenses that are allowed to be deducted include expenses for the business that the taxpayer has paid or have to be reimbursed in the tax year to conduct business.
2- Fees, interest, bribes, payments or charges made available to the responsible person or director of the enterprise, shareholders or members of co-ownership companies, members of the taxpayer's family or other interested persons, in case there is evidence that the payment has been applied to the actual fulfillment of services and to a reasonable extent.
3- The amount paid on a new building or other assets, continuous improvements or improvements, including interest and VAT paid during the construction or purchase period, shall be in the account of the relevant assets and shall be deducted according to the provisions of Article 13 of this Law.
4. Expenses made to retirees who are not under the automatic declaration regime are not allowed to be deducted before the actual payment.
5- Local banks are allowed to make capital reserves for doubtful loans to determine taxable income.
6- Deduction of expenses of qualified investment projects obtained under the Law on Investment of the Kingdom of Cambodia.
7- The rules and procedures of the deduction shall be determined by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 12.. Interest expense
1. To be allowed to deduct the interest expense paid or reimbursed by the taxpayer in the tax year for the purpose of doing business, but not exceeding the sum of the interest income of the taxpayer and 50 (fifty) percent of the net income other than interest of the taxpayer in the tax year.
2- Net income other than interest is gross income other than interest income minus other expenses that are allowed to be deducted, except for interest expenses.
3- The rules and procedures of the forward reference of interest expenses shall be determined by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 13. Wealth
1- The conditions of ordinary amortization of physical property are as follows:
a- In determining taxable income, the deduction for amortization is given to the owner of the physical property or the lessee of the physical property in case the lessee assumes the risk of loss or damage to the property in accordance with the conditions prescribed by the proclamation of the Minister of Economy and Finance.
B- Movable physical property is a physical property used in business that often loses value due to use or obsolescence.
c. All physical assets are divided into the following classes and ways:
Class 1 : Various constructions, including buildings and structures of buildings, constructions that are components of buildings, roads, railways, transport vessels, shall be demolished in an equal manner.
Grade 2 : Computers, electronic information systems, electronic equipment and data storage equipment must be dismantled in an orderly manner
Grade 3 : Cars, trucks, furniture and office equipment must be demolished in an orderly manner.
Grade 4 : Other physical assets shall be disposed of in an orderly manner.
d. The deduction for amortization in this paragraph shall be calculated based on the value of the property after the deduction of the special amortization in the second paragraph of this Article.
2- The conditions of special amortization of physical property are as follows:
This deductible amount is equal to 40 (forty) percent of the capital value of new or used physical assets put into use in production and processing to be determined by the proclamation of the Minister of Economy and Finance.  The special amortization shall reduce the capital value of the tangible assets that can be used for ordinary amortization in accordance with paragraph 1 of this Article.
b- The special deduction of the tangible property shall be deducted to determine the taxable income of the investment project to qualify for the taxable year if the investor does not elect to use the right to receive the tax exemption period as provided in paragraph 3 of Article 20 of this Law.
c- Physical assets that have received special deductions must be used for at least 4 (four) taxable years after the special deduction tax year is deducted. This amount shall not affect the actual accounting value of the tangible asset for the determination of gains from taxable capital in accordance with Article 7 of this Law.
3_ The rules and procedures for the disposal of physical property shall be determined by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 15: Agriculture and Natural Resources
Agriculture and natural resources are defined as follows:
1- Long-term agriculture (biological assets) must use the method of equal distribution:
