a. Agricultural crops: To record in the biological asset account all expenses for development, expenses directly related to cultivation, including interest expenses related to development and cultivation, and expenses for preparing infrastructure serving cultivation.
b- Animal husbandry: To record in the biological asset account all expenses for the development of animal husbandry, expenses directly related to animal husbandry, including interest expenses related to animal husbandry development and animal husbandry, and expenses for preparing infrastructure serving animal husbandry.
2- Natural resources are defined as follows:
a. To record in the asset account the expenses incurred in exploration and development, including interest related to such expenses.
b- The amount of natural resources other than minerals and kerosene that is allowed to be deducted in any taxable year shall be calculated by taking the balance of the natural resource account multiplied by the division between the volume produced about the natural resources in the year and the estimated amount of gross product that can be extracted from that resource.

Article 16. Charity Donation
1. To be allowed to deduct charitable donations made to various organizations as provided in Article 9 of this Law, but not to exceed 5 (five) percent of the taxable income before deducting such charitable contributions.
2- The criteria for charitable donations shall be determined by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance. Forward Loss Reference
If this is not enough to deduct the deduction, the share of the remaining losses in one (one) year shall apply to all losses in the order in which the losses occurred 11/84.

Article 18. Income allocation and deductions among taxpayers
1. In the case of two (two) or more enterprises, even if established or organized in or outside the Kingdom of Cambodia and under joint ownership, in case of necessity, the Fiscal Administration may make a distribution of gross income, deductions or other benefits among the attracted individuals in order to prevent tax evasion or evasion or to clearly reflect the income among the attracted individuals.
2- For the purposes of this Article:
a. Two (two) or more enterprises shall be under joint ownership if any individual owns 20 (twenty) percent or more of the value or share in the direct capital of each enterprise.
b. The allocation of income to permanent establishments of foreign taxpayers in the Kingdom of Cambodia shall also include income from the supply of goods or services that are the same or similar to the business activities of permanent establishments supplied by foreign taxpayers in the Kingdom of Cambodia.
3- The rules and procedures of income allocation and withholding among taxpayers shall be determined by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 19.. Unauthorized troop cuts
For the purposes of the Income Tax Regulation, the expenses that are not allowed to be deducted are as follows:
1- Spend on any activities that are generally considered to be entertainment, relaxation, reception, or the use of any means associated with these activities.
2. Expenses for personal or family living, except for additional benefits in cash or in kind where tax is deducted in accordance with the regulations on payroll tax.
3- The tax amount prescribed by the regulations on income tax and the withholding tax prescribed by the regulations on payroll tax.
4- Loss on the sale or sale of property, whether directly or indirectly between interested persons.
5- Expenses are exempt from incurred expenses and taxpayers can clearly state the amount and business targets.

Article 20_ Determination of payable tax
Annual income tax is set as follows:
1. 20 (twenty) percent on taxable income achieved by individuals.
2- 30 (thirty) percent of the taxable income achieved under the kerosene agreement or achieved from doing business in natural resources, including forests, minerals, gold or precious stones.
3- 0 (zero) percent on the taxable income of a qualified investment project that is within the tax exemption period in accordance with the Law on Investment of the Kingdom of Cambodia.
4. For taxable income achieved by individuals, sole proprietorships and shares to be allocated to each member of a co-ownership company, which are not considered as individuals, shall be taxed on income at the rate of growth according to the class to be determined at the request of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 21. Income Tax for Insurance Enterprises
Income tax for insurance enterprises is set as follows:
1- For insurance or reinsurance activities on other assets or risks in the Kingdom of Cambodia, income tax is set at 5 (five) percent of the lump sum insurance premiums received in the tax year.
2. For insurance or life insurance activities of a thrift nature and other activities other than insurance or reinsurance of other assets or risks as provided in Paragraph 1 of this Article, income tax shall be determined in accordance with Article 20 of this Law.
3- The rules and procedures of paying income tax for insurance enterprises shall be determined by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 22. Income Tax for Foreign Company Branches
Income tax for foreign company branches is set as follows:
1. Income earned from Cambodian sources shall be taxed under Article 20 of this Law.
2- If in the current tax year, any foreign company's branch transfers Cambodian-sourced income abroad, that income:
a. Advance tax shall not be levied on the distribution of dividends under Article 23 of this Law if the transferred income is income after the payment of income tax under paragraph 1 or paragraph 2 of Article 20 of this Law.
b- Subject to prepayment tax on dividend distribution under Article 23 of this Law if the transferred income is income for which income has not been taxed according to paragraph 1 or paragraph 2 of Article 20 of this Law and shall be subject to withholding tax under Article 26 of this Law on income as provided in paragraph 10 of Article 33 of this Law.
3. The rules and procedures for the collection of income tax for branches of foreign companies shall be determined by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 23. Advance tax on dividend distribution
The prepayment tax on dividend distribution is set as follows:
1. Unless the investment project is eligible for the income tax exemption period, if any enterprise allocates dividends from the income before the annual income tax is paid to the domestic or foreign investors, the enterprise shall pay a tax equal to the multiplication of the inflated dividends according to the income tax rate multiplied by the annual income tax rate as provided in Article 20 of this Law.
2 - The tax amount paid under paragraph 1 of this Article is allowed as a tax credit for deduction of the allocated annual income tax charge.
3. Dividends paid in accordance with paragraph 1 of this Article, when re-distributed, shall no longer be subject to prepayment tax on the distribution of dividends as provided in this Article.
4. Advance tax on dividend distribution as provided in this Article does not apply to income from insurance premiums or reinsurance on other assets or risks in the Kingdom of Cambodia as provided in Paragraph 1 of Article 21 of this Law.
5- The rules and procedures for collecting prepaid tax on dividend distribution shall be determined by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 24.. Minimum Taxes
1. The minimum tax shall be determined at the rate of 1 (one) percent on the annual turnover, including various VAT, excluding value-added tax, and payable at the time of payment of annual income tax. Investment projects are eligible for the minimum tax exemption provided that they have an independent audit report.
2. The rules and procedures of the criteria for holding an incorrect accounting list and paying the minimum tax shall be determined by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 25. General withholding tax
The general withholding tax is set as follows:
1. Taxpayers who engage in business that make payments in cash or in kind to taxpayers shall withhold and pay tax at the following rates on the amount paid before withholding tax:
a. Rate of 15 (fifteen) percent for:
- Income received by an individual not under the self-declaration regime from the provision of services, including administration or consultancy or similar services;
- Compensation for supernatural assets and shareholdings in mineral resources and interest paid to the taxpayer by the taxpayer who conducts business other than the local bank.
b- Rate of 10 (ten) percent on income from leasing real estate or real estate.
c- The rate of 6 (six) percent on the interest paid by local banks to retired taxpayers with fixed deposit accounts.
d. The rate of 4 (four) per cent on the interest paid by the local bank to retired taxpayers with indefinite deposit accounts.
2. The deductions in this Article shall not apply to interest paid to local banks and payments to tax-exempt income as provided for in Article 9 of this Law.

Article 26. Withholding tax on payments to non-resident taxpayers
Taxpayers who carry on business, including permanent establishments of non-resident individuals who make payments of Cambodia-sourced income as provided for in Article 33 of this Law, shall withhold and pay tax at the rate of 14 (fourteen) percent of the amount to be opened.

Article 27... Withholding tax as the final tax
Withholding tax on payments to retired individuals not subject to the automatic declaration regime under Article 25
of this Law and withholding tax on payments to non-immigrant taxpayers in accordance with Article 26 of this Law
shall be deemed to be the final tax for the recipient of the payment or allocation specified in the Articles.
of this law.

Article 28. Income Tax Relief
Enterprises that are subject to income tax under the automatic declaration regime, including qualified investment projects that have expired the income tax exemption period, are obliged to pay monthly income tax at the rate of 1 (one) percent of the turnover, inclusive of VAT, excluding VAT achieved in the previous month.

Article 29. Duties of medium and large taxpayers
Medium taxpayers and large taxpayers shall have the following obligations:
1. To carry out the obligation to register accounts as provided in paragraph 2 of Article 6 of this Law and to submit an annual income tax declaration to the Fiscal Administration in the form prescribed by the Fiscal Administration within three (three) months after the end of each taxable year, together with the balance of accounts, results and additional information.
2. For enterprises that suffer losses, they must also submit a fiscal declaration letter in the same form and within the same period.

Article 30. Duties of a petty taxpayer
Small taxpayers have the following obligations:
1. To submit a letter of declaration and payment of annual income tax to the Fiscal Administration every year within three (three) months after the end of each calendar year in the form determined by the Fiscal Administration.
2- In case of not keeping a record of the list of revenues and expenditures as determined by the Fiscal Administration, the amount of taxable income shall be determined by the Fiscal Administration after monitoring and calculating according to the rate of revenue according to the business occupation determined by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 31. Duties of a withholding agent
1. An individual or beneficiary who withholds tax under Articles 25 and 26 of this Law shall submit a letter of fiscal declaration and pay the withheld tax to the fiscal administration in the form prescribed by the fiscal no later than the 20th day of the month following the month in which the payment is made.
2- Enterprises must submit a prepayment tax declaration letter on dividend distribution as provided in Article
23 of this Law and pay taxes to the Fiscal Administration in the form prescribed by the Fiscal Administration.
No later than the 20th day of the month following the month in which the allocation is paid.

Article 32. Income tax payment obligation
Taxpayers are obliged to submit a fiscal declaration letter and pay income tax to the Fiscal Administration every month in the form determined by the Fiscal Administration no later than the 20th day of the month following the month in which the business transaction occurred.

Article 33. Cambodian Source Income
Without limitation to the following incomes, Cambodia's source income includes:
1- Interest paid by pension enterprises, pension co-ownership companies or government institutions of the Kingdom of Cambodia.
2- Dividends distributed by pension enterprises.
3- Revenue from services fulfilled in the Kingdom of Cambodia
4- Income from management and technical services paid by retired individuals.
5- Income derived from immovable property or immovable property in case the property is located in the Kingdom of Cambodia.
6- Bribes derived from the use or right to use immovable property paid by the expatriate taxpayer or the expatriate taxpayer through a permanent institution located in the Kingdom of Cambodia.
7. Profits from the sale of immovable or immovable property, including immovable property, located in the Kingdom of Cambodia, or profits from the transfer of any interest in immovable or immovable property, including immovable property, located in the Kingdom of Cambodia.
8- Premium or reinsurance against risks in the Kingdom of Cambodia.
9- Profits from the sale of real estate which is a share of the business assets of permanent establishments of foreign taxpayers in the Kingdom of Cambodia.
10- Income from business activities of the taxpayer through permanent establishments in the Kingdom of Cambodia.

Article 34. Foreign-sourced income
All income that is not Cambodian source income as provided for in Article 33 of this Law shall be treated as foreign source income.

Article 35 Determination of sources of income
In case there is not enough information to determine the source of income, or if the rules already in place cannot clearly reflect the income from any source, the tax administration determines the source of that income.

Article 36. Foreign Tax Credits
1. Taxpayers who have received income from foreign sources and have paid taxes under foreign tax laws are entitled to a tax credit for deduction from the income tax payable in the Kingdom of Cambodia, but must have a document certifying the payment of taxes abroad.
2- To calculate the tax payable in the Kingdom of Cambodia before deducting the tax credit, the total amount of income received from Cambodian and foreign sources must be taken into account.
3_ The tax credit is set separately for the tax paid by Cambodian expatriates in each overseas country, but the tax credit allowed to deduct for the tax year is the lowest amount out of:
a- Taxes actually paid in any foreign country.
b- The amount derived from the gross income tax proceeds from all sources for the same period calculated according to the tax rate in Article 20 of this Law shall be multiplied by the division between the income received abroad and the total income from all sources.
4. Foreign tax credit can be granted unless the taxpayer has completed the form as well as provided the documents required by the fiscal administration, especially the statement of the overseas tax payer by the foreign tax administration.
5- In case the amount of tax credit exceeds the tax debt, the excess amount may be referred to be used in subsequent years until the fifth (fifth) year from the year following the year in which the tax credit accrues.

Article 37. Calculation of income tax liabilities
The calculation of income tax liabilities is defined as follows:
1. Calculate the total tax liabilities in accordance with Article 20 of this Law.
2. To withdraw the tax credits paid under Article 23 and the foreign tax credits under Article 36 of this Law, but not to exceed the tax debts in paragraph 1 of this Article.

Article 38. Calculation of tax payable or tax credit for the taxable year
The calculation of the tax payable or tax credit for the taxable year is determined as follows:
1. In case the calculation result under Article 37 of this Law is greater than the sum of the amount of tax withheld on behalf of the taxpayer by the withholding agency under Article 25 of this Law and the amount of income tax withheld by the taxpayer annually under Article 28 of this Law, the taxpayer shall pay the wrong amount additionally to the Fiscal Administration.
2. If the calculation result under Article 37 of this Law is less than the sum of the amount of tax withheld on behalf of the taxpayer by the withholding agency under Article 25 of this Law and the amount of income tax withheld by the taxpayer for the tax year under Article 28 of this Law, after calculating the minimum tax liability, the taxpayer may apply for a refund of the incorrect amount or refer to it for use as an allowance for the following year.
3. Before making the payment of tax under paragraph 1 of this Article or applying for a refund or reference to use as a payment for the following year according to the second paragraph of this Article, the taxpayer must first determine the minimum tax liability according to the procedure as provided in Article 39 of this Law.

Article 39.. Calculation of minimum tax, tax payable or credit for the taxable year
The calculation of the minimum tax amount, tax payable or tax credit for the taxable year is determined as follows:
The minimum tax payable may be reduced by the income tax liability in the tax year together in accordance with Article 20 of this Law.
2- In case the income tax debt exceeds the minimum tax liability:
a- The taxpayer shall pay the tax payable in accordance with Article 37 of this Law upon filing the annual income tax declaration.
b- If the amount withheld under Articles 25 and 28 of this Law exceeds the minimum tax liability, the taxpayer may apply for a tax credit.
c- In the case as in paragraph 2 of this Article, the taxpayer is not subject to the minimum tax.
3- If the income tax debt is less than the minimum tax debt:
a. The tax credit of the taxpayer under paragraph 2 of Article 38 of this Law is reduced by the above amount.
b. Reduced tax credits in compliance with Paragraph A of this Paragraph shall be treated as the minimum tax payment for the taxable year.

Article 40_ Object of tax
Payroll tax is a monthly tax determined on salaries received within the framework of employment activities.

Article 41. Scope of Taxes
1. Physical retirees in the Kingdom of Cambodia are subject to salary tax on salaries of Cambodian origin and salaries of foreign origin.
2- Physical non-immigrant individuals are subject to salary tax on salaries of Cambodian origin.

Article 42. Definition
The main vocabulary used in this chapter is defined as follows:
1. Resident, in the case of an employee, taxpayer or physical individual, means a person who has a residence or place of residence in the Kingdom of Cambodia or who has been present in the Kingdom of Cambodia for more than 182 (one hundred and forty-two) days in any 12 (twelve) month ending in the current tax year.
2. Foreigner means any physical person who is not a citizen under paragraph 1 of this Article and receives a salary of Cambodian origin.
3- Unless otherwise provided for, the use of the terms employee, taxpayer and individual physical refers to both residents and non-residents as provided in this Article.
4- Employers, including state institutions, retired individuals, retirement co-ownership companies, permanent establishments in the Kingdom of Cambodia, organizations, associations, political parties or physical retired individuals engaged in business.
5- Employee refers to a physical individual who receives a salary from his or her service activities, including the person in charge or the governor of the enterprise, public servants and citizens who hold public office by election, except for members of the National Assembly and the Senate.
6- Cambodian source salary refers to the salary received within the framework of fulfilling service activities in the Kingdom of Cambodia.
7. Foreign:
a- When used with individual physical, meaning non-resident.
b- When used to determine the source of income, means outside the Kingdom of Cambodia.
8_Salary refers to salary, wages, resignations, allowances, premiums, overtime pay, allowances and additional benefits paid to the employee or paid for the direct or indirect benefit of the employee for the fulfillment of the service activity.

Article 43. Salaries of diplomatic and other foreign officials
The tax exemption on the salaries of diplomatic officials and other foreign officials is set out as follows:
1- Be exempt from payroll tax for:
A salary received by officials and employees of a diplomatic or consular mission of any foreign government holding a diplomatic or official passport of that country within the framework of fulfilling official functions in the Kingdom of Cambodia.
b- Salaries received by representatives, officers and foreign employees of international organizations and of technical cooperation agencies of other governments within the framework of fulfilling official functions in the Kingdom of Cambodia.
2. The tax exemption in this Article shall stand on the principle of rejection between the relevant governments.

Article 44 ... Employee's tax-exempt income
The tax-exempt income of employees is determined as follows:
1. Actual compensation for professional expenses paid by the employee in accordance with the directive and for the benefit of the employer and which has fulfilled the following three (3) conditions:
Distributed in the direct and absolute interests of enterprises
Do not exhibit exaggeration or excessive stockpiling
Presented as evidenced by a detailed invoice and paid in bulk and made on behalf of the person who received the actual cost of the reimbursement.
2. The remuneration in case of dissolution of the contract at the level prescribed in the Law on Labor and the type of remuneration entitled to tax exemption shall be determined by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.
3. The additional allowance for the establishment of a pension and ensuring social welfare or having a social character in the case stipulated in the Law on Labor and the Law on Social Security shall be determined by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.
4. Supply free of charge or at a lower cost than the cost of uniforms or equipment for special professions;
5. Contractor Allowance for Mission and Travel Expenses.

Article 45: Monthly Tax Base
Except for the additional benefits to be taxed under Article 48 of this Law, the basis for calculating the monthly tax of a pensioner is the taxable salary by allowing the deduction of:
1. Withholding which is an obligation to comply with the Law on Labor and the Law on Social Security.
2. Payments that are exempt from tax as provided in Article 44 of this Law.

Article 46.. Monthly taxable salary
The monthly taxable salary is set as follows:
1- The monthly taxable salary of a retired employee includes:
a- Salaries received from Cambodian sources.
b- Salary received from foreign sources.
c- Allowances, loans or allowances that the employer has opened to the employee shall be added in addition to the taxable salary of the month in which those funds were opened and shall be deducted from the salary in the month in which the employee has repaid.
2. Based on the presentation of evidence of family status, any retired employee who has a child in charge and/or a federal who is only a housewife at the time of tax payment is entitled to a reduction in the tax base by the amount to be determined by the Decree at the request of the Minister of Economy and Finance.
3. For non-immigrant taxpayers, the taxable salary is the Cambodian source salary that is taxable under the provisions of this Chapter.

Article 47. Monthly payroll tax rate
For retired employees, the tax payable shall be determined according to the growth rate of 0 (zero) percent, 5 (five) percent, 10 (ten) percent, 15 (fifteen) percent and 20 (twenty) percent on the monthly taxable salary and shall be deducted by the employer.

Article 48. Determination of payroll tax on supplementary benefits
1_ For each additional benefit, the employer shall withhold and pay tax at the rate of 20 (twenty) percent of the total value of the supplementary benefit provided to all employees.
2_The rules and procedures of payroll tax exemption for additional benefits shall be determined by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 49_ Determination of salary tax of non-immigrant taxpayers
Except for the additional benefits to be taxed under Article 48 of this Law, the tax amount shall be withheld by the taxpayer at the rate of 20 (twenty) percent on every taxable salary payment as provided in paragraph 3 of Article 46 of this Law.

Article 50: Foreign Tax Credits
Retired taxpayers who have received salaries from foreign sources and paid taxes in accordance with foreign tax laws are entitled to a tax credit for deduction from the payroll tax payable in the Kingdom of Cambodia, but must have a document certifying the payment of tax abroad.
1. To calculate the tax payable in the Kingdom of Cambodia before deducting the tax credit, the total amount of salary received from Cambodian and foreign sources must be taken into account.
2- The tax credit is determined separately for the tax paid by Cambodian expatriates abroad, but the tax credit provided for payroll tax paid abroad is the lowest amount out of:
a- Taxes actually paid in any foreign country.
b- The amount derived from the total salary tax from all sources in the same period calculated according to the class growth rate in Article 47 of this Law shall be multiplied by the division between the salary received abroad and the total salary from all sources.
3- Refund of foreign tax credit is possible unless the foreign taxpayer has completed the form as well as provided the documents required by the tax administration, especially the statement of the employer and the fiscal administration of the place of employment abroad.

Article 51. Tax withholding obligations
The tax withholding obligation is defined as follows:
1. This tax is an obligation of salaried individuals, including foreign individuals, unless otherwise provided for in international agreements.
2. On the salary, it shall be collected in a pre-deducted manner every month by the employer to open the salary.
3- If the employer resides abroad, the representative appointed by the employer in the Kingdom of Cambodia is the person responsible for withholding tax on payroll before payroll is paid to the employee and must declare the payment of such tax to the Fiscal Administration.
4- Employers representing foreigners in the Kingdom of Cambodia of foreign employers and employees shall be jointly responsible for paying payroll tax in the Kingdom of Cambodia, regardless of whether the payroll is made in the Kingdom of Cambodia or abroad.

Article 52. Tax withholding, accounting and reporting
An employer who pays a taxable salary must fulfill the following tasks:
1- Deduct tax before payroll.
2. Report to the Fiscal Administration and employees on the status of withheld taxes.
3- Possess and maintain a list of cards.

Article 53. Obligation to submit tax declaration and payment
1- Payroll tax is due and payable upon payroll.
2- The withholding agent is obliged to submit a letter of declaration and pay salary tax every month no later than the 20th day of the month following the month in which the salary accrues.

Article 54. Rules and procedures for managing tax collection
The rules and procedures of the management of payroll tax collection shall be determined by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 55: Subject of VAT
Value Added Tax shall be applied on the excised supply of goods or services.

Article 56 Scope of VAT
VAT applies to all VAT-liable supplies of goods or services in the Kingdom of Cambodia.

Article 57. Definition
The main vocabulary used in this chapter is defined as follows:
1. Goods refer to physical assets other than land and money.
2. Service refers to the provision of something of value other than goods, land and money.
3- Supply of goods refers to the transfer of the right of use or the right of assignment as the owner of the goods, with or without compensation.
4- Supply of services refers to a supply that is not the supply of goods, land or money made for compensation or without compensation.
The supply of services shall be treated as the supply of services.
5- Individual refers to an individual or group of individuals who do business and any other person who is associated with that person.
6- Attraction to any person means:
a- Any person who owns 20 (twenty) percent or more of the value or voting rights of the shares in the direct capital of the person taking into consideration.
b- Have joint management or have a joint director with individuals.
c- Being a family member or a federal or a family member of an individual's federation.
d- Purchased 30 (thirty) percent or more of the individual's total output in three (three) consecutive months.
7- VAT in this chapter refers to VAT on value-added.

Article 58 . . Taxable Persons
For the purposes of this Article, an alien who supplies digital goods or services into the Kingdom of Cambodia shall be deemed to be a taxable person.

Article 59: VAT-Charged Supplies
Except to the contrary in this Chapter, the term VATABLE supplies refers to:
1- Supply of goods or services by VAT persons in the Kingdom of Cambodia.
2- Deprivation of goods or services for personal use by taxable persons.
3- Giving as a gift or supply below the true value of goods or services by a taxable person.
4. The supply of digital goods or digital services to the Kingdom of Cambodia as provided in Article 58 of this Law.
5. Import of goods into the customs territory of the Kingdom of Cambodia.

Article 60. VATABLE Prices
The VAT value is set as follows:
1- The VAT value of supply is the cost of goods or services that the seller takes from the buyer.
2- In case the payment for the VAT supply is compensation for anything other than cash for the direct or indirect benefit to the seller, such compensation shall be included in the VAT price at the market price.
3- The VAT value of imported goods is the dutiable value, including customs duties and VAT at the time of importation.
4- If the VATABLE price of the goods or services supplied does not represent the true price, then the Fiscal Administration may determine a price for the goods or services and that price shall be considered as a valid price until there is other proof approved by the Fiscal Administration.
5. The VAT value of used goods purchased by a taxable person from a consumer for regular sale or on behalf of a consumer is the amount of difference between the sale price and the purchase price or the proceeds derived from the sale of such goods.

Article 61... Supply time
The supply time is set as follows:
1- VAT is due and payable upon supply.
2- The time of supply of goods or services is the time when the seller has to issue an invoice or the time when the seller has issued an invoice if the invoice is issued before the seller has to issue the invoice.
3. The VAT invoice shall be issued no later than 7 (seven) days after the delivery of the goods or the fulfillment of the service or after the payment in case the payment is made before the delivery of the goods or the fulfillment of the service.
4. For the supply of goods or services that are made continuously or for which there is multiple payments, the supply time shall be determined by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.
5- For the import of goods, the time of supply is the time when the importer submits a declaration letter to the Customs Administration in accordance with the law and the prevailing customs norms.

Article 62. Place of Supply
The supply locations are set as follows:
1. The supply of goods shall be deemed to have been made in the Kingdom of Cambodia if the goods are handed over even if they are in the Kingdom of Cambodia.
2- The supply of services shall be deemed to have been made in the Kingdom of Cambodia if the services have been fulfilled in the Kingdom of Cambodia, unless:
A supply of services in connection with a property shall be determined that the service is performed at the place where the property is located.
b. The supply of services in connection with transportation shall be determined that such services are performed at the place of transportation.
3- Goods shall be considered to have been imported into the Kingdom of Cambodia if they are imported into the customs territory of the Kingdom of Cambodia.

Article 63. Non-VAT Supplies
Non-VAT supplies are as follows:
1. Educational learning services.
2- Public Postal Service.
3- Hospital and clinic services, medical and dental services, and sales of medical and dental secondary goods related to the fulfillment of these services.
4- Passenger transportation services by public transport system, which is wholly owned by the State.
5- Insurance.
6- Electricity supply and clean water supply.
7. Domestically produced unprocessed agricultural products.
8. Garbage and solid or liquid waste collection services.
9. Basic financial services to be determined by the Proclamation of the Minister of Economy and Finance.
10- Import of personal use materials subject to customs duties at the price level to be determined by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.
11- Non-profit activities to serve the public interest, recognized by the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 64. Non-VAT Supplies to Diplomatic Missions and International Organizations
Non-VAT supplies to diplomatic missions and international organizations are defined as follows:
1. The import or domestic purchase of goods or services by foreign diplomatic missions and consulates, international organizations and other technical cooperation agencies of governments for use in the performance of their official functions shall be defined as non-VAT supplies.
2. The import or domestic purchase of goods or services for personal use of official staff of foreign diplomatic missions and consulates, international organizations and other technical cooperation agencies of the Government, as provided for in paragraph 1 of this Article, shall be defined as a non-VAT supply only for those goods included in the list of goods specified by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.
3- The non-VAT supply in this Article shall stand on the principle of conciliation between the relevant governments.

Article 66. VAT Setting
VAT is set as follows:
1. The VAT prescribed in Article 65 of this Law shall be treated as a debt to the State upon supply.
2. The VAT payable to the State is equal to the VAT on gross inputs at the rate specified in Article 65 of this Law minus the VAT credit on the total allowable inputs in the same month.

Article 67. Physical real estate that is no longer used in business
In case the physical immovable property of any business which has received VAT credit as provided for in Article 68 of this Law shall cease to be used in the business of a taxable person, the property shall be deemed to have been sold and shall be subject to VAT at market value upon cessation of use.

Article 68 ... VAT credit on non-VAT inputs and supplies
VAT credits on non-VAT inputs and supplies are defined as follows:
1. The VAT paid by a taxable person on goods or services for use in a business supplied by another taxable person or the VAT paid by a taxable person as an importer of imported goods or services for use in his or her business shall become a VAT credit on inputs for deduction from VAT on outputs.
2- In case the purchased goods or services are used in one part as a VAT supply and the other part as a non-VAT supply, VAT credit is allowed only for the part used as a VAT supply.
3. For the non-VAT supply of goods or services to foreign diplomatic missions and consulates, international organizations and other technical cooperation agencies of the Government, as provided for in Article 64 of this Law, suppliers are allowed to credit VAT on inputs without regard to the conditions as provided in paragraph 2 of this Article.

Article 69 . Documents required for applying for VAT credit on inputs
The application for VAT credit on inputs must be accompanied by:
1. VAT invoices made in accordance with Article 78 of this Law.
2. Import customs calendar made in accordance with the Law on Customs and Tax Payment Receipts or other payment receipts of the Customs Administration.

Article 70 . VAT on inputs that are not allowed to be used as credit
VAT on inputs that are not allowed to be used as credit includes the VAT paid by the taxable person on expenses, such as reception, entertainment or leisure, the purchase of a car or the purchase of certain telecommunications products.

Article 71 Obligation to file a declaration letter and pay VAT
The taxable person shall be obliged to submit a declaration letter and pay VAT every month no later than the 20th day of the month following the month of supply.

Article 72 . . Handling of excess credit
If the VAT on inputs paid by a taxable person under Article 65 of this Law is greater than the VAT on inputs collected by that person for any month:
1- The excess amount shall be used as a VAT credit for the VAT owed by the individual in the past month.
2. The remaining excess amount shall be considered as a VAT credit on the inputs of Article 68 of this Law for the following month.

Article 73. VAT refund to exporter
The Fiscal Administration may reimburse the following:
1 - VAT credit on monthly excess inputs at the request of a taxable person whose activities are mainly exported, if that person has presented clear documents proving the export and has duly executed the obligation to hold the inventory and other documents.
2- VAT paid by foreign tourists on the purchase of goods from VAT persons for use outside the Kingdom of Cambodia.

Article 74 ... VAT refund in case of excess VAT credit of 3 (three) months or more
To receive a VAT refund for any month, the application must be submitted within 20 (twenty) days after the end of those months.

Article 75 - Application of Value Added Tax on Qualified Investment Projects
The supply of domestic production inputs for the implementation of qualified investment projects as provided in the relevant provisions of the Law on Investment of the Kingdom of Cambodia shall be subject to VAT at the rate of 0 (zero) percent.

Article 76. Responsibility for collection and payment of VAT
Responsibilities for the collection and payment of VAT are set out as follows:
1. A taxable person or importer shall be obliged to pay VAT under Article 65 of this Law on every taxable supply carried out by a taxable person or importer.
2- Special conditions specifying the buyer's responsibility for VAT in case the supplier does not have a permanent establishment in the Kingdom of Cambodia or in case there are other obstacles to the collection of VAT from the supplier shall be determined by a decree at the request of the Minister of Economy and Finance.
3- Any person who has made a supply of goods or services, in the name of the owner and not in the capacity of an employee of any person and who has control over the supply, shall be deemed to be a taxable person for that supply.

Article 77. Registration
The registration is set as follows:
1. A taxable person as provided in Article 58 of this Law shall register for VAT within 15 (fifteen) days after the date on which such person becomes a taxable person.
2. For a person who is required to register and does not make a registration, the Fiscal Administration may register that person from the time that person is required to register.
3. For a group of two or more taxable individuals, in which one or more individuals are not taxable individuals, the fiscal administration may consider any taxable individual to be registered for the whole or any part of the attraction.
4- For the purpose of registration and with the consent of the Fiscal Administration, with respect to a group of taxable individuals who are attached to each other as provided for in Article 57 of this Law, the activities of the members of the group may be considered as the activities of only one elected member.

Article 78 .. VAT Invoice
The VAT invoice is set as follows:
1. A VAT-liable person who supplies a VAT invoice with the title VAT invoice and with the correct number to the buyer who is a taxpayer under the auto-declaration regime will be issued a regular invoice to the buyer who is not under the auto-declaration regime.
2. No person may issue an invoice or other document certifying any amount as VAT on the supply of goods or services, unless the person is a registered VAT person in accordance with Article 77 of this Law and the goods or services supplied are goods or services subject to VAT.
3- Apart from other charges, if any invoice is found to be fraudulent as a VAT invoice and the invoice shows that there is a certain amount of VAT payable, the person issuing the invoice must pay to the Fiscal Administration within seven (7) days after the date of invoicing the amount posted on the invoice, even if the VAT amount is to be paid or not.
4. In the case of retail sales, in which most of the sales are not made with the VAT payable persons required by paragraph 1 of this Article, it shall be deemed to have been sufficiently satisfied if the seller has provided a receipt of the details recorded in the Bela list or other documents.
5- For imports, a duly filled customs declaration stating the payment of VAT shall be used as a control document to determine the eligibility for VAT credit.

Article 79 . . Non-issuance of VAT invoices
Failure to issue VAT invoices is subject to the following penalties:
1. Apart from other sanctions, if the Fiscal Administration finds for the second (two) time that any business establishment of a taxable person fails to issue invoices as required, the Fiscal Administration may close that business institution for a limited period of not more than seven (seven) days.
2- If any business establishment that has been closed as provided in paragraph 1 of this Article continues to commit such offenses again, the business establishment may be closed again for a limited period of not more than seven (seven) days.

Article 80. Lists, Records & Information
The list, records and information for VAT are set out as follows:
1- The VAT payer shall use the cash recording system set by the Fiscal Administration and shall keep copies of all invoices issued and all invoices received.
2. A taxable person shall properly record and keep a record of all business transactions carried out and shall have an account to keep track of the VAT collected on sales and the VAT paid on his or her purchases, as well as various adjustments to the selling price or VAT amount in the form prescribed by the Fiscal Administration.
3. The tasks as provided in paragraph 2 of this Article shall be carried out on a daily basis and shall be summed up and the balance shall be calculated at the end of each month.
4. Invoices, records and other documents related to this VAT shall be kept in chronological order, in the form and place designated by the Fiscal Administration, within 10 (ten) years after the completion of the latest business transactions related to these documents.
5. The cash recording system, all documents and records to be kept in accordance with this Article as well as other documents and records related to the business of the individual shall be provided to the Fiscal Administration for supervision upon request.

Article 81 . SPECIAL RULES FOR IMPORT
The provisions of this Chapter relating to imports shall be governed by the Customs Administration in accordance with the Law on Customs.

Article 82. Business Termination and Business Transfer
The rules of business cessation and business transfer are set out as follows:
1 - Within 15 (fifteen) days after the cessation of business, the taxable person shall submit a declaration letter to the Fiscal Administration in the form prescribed by the Fiscal Administration, enclosed with details of sales and purchases after the latest fiscal declaration and details of all goods in stock for which VAT has not been paid or for which VAT credit has already been received as well as VAT payment to those limits.
2- The transfer of business from one individual to another shall not be subject to value-added tax.
3- The rules and procedures for the cessation and transfer of business shall be determined by the Decree at the request of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 83 . VAT credit for stocked goods to newly registered persons
VAT credits on stocked goods are defined as follows:
1- For a newly registered person and on the date of registration there are already stocks of goods for which VAT has been paid, that person may apply to the Fiscal Administration to authorize VAT credit on the VAT paid on those stocks after the Fiscal Administration has inspected that the invoices or copies of the customs declarations of those goods are valid.
2- If there is agreement on the validity of those documents, the Fiscal Administration may authorize the VAT credit for the supply made during the 60 (sixty) days prior to the date of registration.

Article 84... Rules and procedures of VAT collection management
The rules and procedures of the management of VAT collection shall be determined by sub-decree upon request.
Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 85. Subject of VAT
Special VAT shall apply on certain goods or services that are of a luxury nature or are not essential to daily life or affect health, society or the environment.

Article 86. Scope of VAT
Special VAT applies to the import, manufacture or distribution of goods or the supply of services subject to special VAT for use in the Kingdom of Cambodia.

Article 87. Definition
The main vocabulary used in this chapter is defined as follows:
1- Special VAT Persons refer to importers or manufacturers of goods or suppliers of services subject to special VAT
2. Import refers to the act of importing goods into the customs territory of the Kingdom of Cambodia by any individual.
For the purposes of this paragraph, the consignee, the person who owns the goods, the person who will become the owner of the goods, or the person who has the right to take possession of the goods before the goods cease to be subject to customs control, is also considered to be the importer.
4- Production refers to the activity of converting raw materials, gathering, assembling, packaging, filling ports into semi-finished products or finished products.
5- Producer refers to any person who manufactures goods or any person who hires another person to produce goods for himself.
6- Distributor refers to a person who supplies goods imported or manufactured by himself or repurchased from importers or from producers.
7- Supply refers to the sale or expropriation for personal use or the gifted or actual provision of goods or services by a special VAT person.
8- VAT stamp refers to a stamp sheet for stamping on special VAT goods to certify that special VAT has been paid.
9- VAT in this chapter refers to special VAT.

Without limitation to the following:

d. Electronics.

3- The Royal Government may issue a decree to additionally impose or suspend special taxable goods or services at the request of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 89. Special VAT Rate
1. The special VAT rate shall be determined as a percentage rate on the price of goods or services on which special VAT is charged or as a value determined on weight, weight, size or quantity.
2. The special VAT rate shall be determined by a decree at the request of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 90... Special VAT basis
The special VAT basis shall be determined by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 91 ... Rules and procedures for VAT collection management
The rules and procedures of the management of special VAT collection shall be determined by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 92. Subject of VAT
VAT for public lighting shall apply on the supply of liquor, mercy or tobacco products.

Article 93. Scope of VAT
VAT for public lighting applies to the supply of alcohol, marijuana or tobacco products in the Kingdom of Cambodia.

Article 94. Definition
The main vocabulary used in this chapter is defined as follows:
1. Alcohol refers to all types of products that contain alcohol.
2- Merit refers to alcoholic water made by soaking various ingredients, which are mainly beer or alcoholic beverages.
3- Tobacco refers to a whole or part of a product made of tobacco leaves as a raw material and which is produced for use in tobacco.
4- VAT in this chapter refers to VAT for public enlightenment.

Article 95. VAT Rate
The VAT rate for public lighting shall be determined by a decree at the request of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 96 . . VAT Basis
The basis for calculating VAT for public lighting shall be determined by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 97 Supply Time
1. VAT for public lighting shall be determined and payable upon initial supply.
2. The rules of supply shall comply with the rules of supply for VAT as any;
Paragraphs 1 to 4 of Article 61 of this Law.

Article 98.. Duty to submit a declaration letter and pay VAT
A VAT person shall be obliged to submit a declaration letter and pay VAT for public lighting every month by the 20th day of the month following the month in which the product is supplied.

Article 99 ... Rules and procedures for VAT collection management
The rules and procedures of VAT collection management for public lighting shall be determined by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 100.. Subject of VAT
Accommodation VAT shall be applied on the supply of accommodation services in the Kingdom of Cambodia.

Article 101 Scope of the building
Accommodation VAT applies on the supply of hotel accommodation services in the Kingdom of Cambodia.

Article 102.. Definition
The main vocabulary used in this chapter is defined as follows:
1- Hotel refers to a place that provides accommodation services in the form of rooms, beds and provides other facilities and services according to each type of accommodation service provider, such as hotels, hotels, apartments, suite hotels, resort hotels, motels, lodges, bungalows, guesthouses or guest houses, tourist resorts and other accommodation service providers of similar characteristics, even if named as whatever they are.
2- VAT in this chapter refers to VAT on accommodation.

Article 103. VAT Rate
VAT on accommodation shall be determined at the rate of two (two) percent.

Article 104. VAT Basis
The basis of VAT on accommodation is the accommodation fee, including various charges as well as VAT.
Except for VAT on value-added and VAT on self-proposition.

Article 105 Supply Time
The rules of supply of accommodation services shall comply with the rules of supply of services for VAT on
value added as provided in Article 61 of this Law.

Article 106. Duty to submit a declaration letter and pay VAT
The taxable person shall be obliged to submit a declaration letter and pay VAT on accommodation every month no later than the 20th day of the month following the month in which the accommodation services are supplied.

Article 107. Rules and procedures for VAT collection management
The rules and procedures of the management of VAT collection on accommodation shall be determined by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 108. Subjects of Taxes
Patent tax is an annual tax that is levied on each business activity of a taxpayer based on the type of taxpayer and the level of income.

Article 109. Scope of Taxes
Patent tax applies to taxpayers doing business in the Kingdom of Cambodia.

Article 110. Tax Exemption
Patent taxes are exempted as follows:
1- State institutions, diplomatic missions or foreign consulates, international organizations and other government technical cooperation agencies.
2- The activities of any organization that are organized and carried out for purely religious, charitable, scientific, literary or educational purposes and no share of the property or income is used for private gain.
3. All business activities with annual turnover below the level of taxpayer turnover under the automatic declaration regime as prescribed in Article 6 of this Law.

Article 111. Tax rate
The patent tax rate shall be determined by a decree at the request of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 112. Obligation to submit tax declaration and payment
1. Patent tax payable during the period from January 1 to March 31 annually.
2. Taxpayers who commence business within the first six (six) months of the year shall pay patent tax for the whole year, but if commencing business within the last six (six) months of the year, the taxpayer shall pay half of the patent tax.

Article 113. Activities and places of taxable business activities
The activities and places of taxable business activities shall be determined as follows:
1- Taxpayers with multiple business activities are required to pay different patent taxes according to each business activity.
2- Activities as appendices of business activities are considered as a single business activity.
3- Taxpayers who have branches, warehouses, factories, factories for the same business in the same capital or province shall have to pay the same patent tax.
4- Taxpayers who have business activities in different capitals or provinces shall have to pay patent tax according to the capital or province in which the business is located.
5- Taxpayers who have branches, warehouses, factories, factories for the same business activity located in different capitals or provinces shall pay the minimum patent tax for each type of taxpayer according to the capital or province in which the business is located.
6. In case of relocation to another capital or province or change of business activities, the new patent tax shall be paid again.

Article 114. Patent Tax Card
1. The Fiscal Administration shall issue a patent tax card to the taxpayer after the patent tax has been paid.
2- The taxpayer is obliged to display a valid patent tax card at his/her place of business.

Article 115... Rules and procedures for managing tax collection
The rules and procedures governing the collection of patent taxes shall be determined by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 116. Subjects of Taxes
Tariff on billboards shall be applied to all types of billboards.

Article 117. Scope of Taxes
The billboard tax applies to all forms of advertising, both mobile and immovable, in the Kingdom of Cambodia.

Article 118. Definition
For the purposes of the Billboard Tax Regulation, the term Billboard refers to:
1- Advertising flyers made of rubber, plain paper, rods or other objects.
2- Business labels for marking names, locations, head offices, offices or places of business.
3- Wallpapers or posters for commercial purposes.

Article 119 . Tax Exemption
Billboard tax is exempt for billboards for non-profit-seeking purposes as follows:
1- Labels of state institutions.
2- Labels of foreign embassies or consulates, national and international organizations and other government technical cooperation agencies, non-governmental organizations and associations.
3- Posters with the goal of social education in the public interest, such as preserving and protecting the environment, stopping domestic violence, protecting natural resources, traffic education, and health education.

Article 120. Tax rate and tax basis
The tax rate and tax base on the billboards shall be determined by a decree at the request of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 121. Obligation to submit tax declaration and payment
Billboard tax payable during the period from January 1 to March 31 annually.

Article 122. Failure to file a tax declaration and payment
If the taxpayer has not paid the billboard tax as provided in this chapter, the competent authority shall not issue a permit for the billboard or billboard that has not yet paid the billboard tax.

Article 123 Rules and Procedures for Tax Collection Administration
The rules and procedures of the management of tax collection on billboards shall be determined by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 124. Subjects of Taxes
The tax on the operation of kerosene and mineral resources applies to the operation of kerosene and mineral resources of the Kingdom of Cambodia.

Article 125.. Scope of Taxes
The Regulation on Taxation of Kerosene and Mineral Resources Operations applies to kerosene and mineral resources operations within the territorial integrity and sovereignty of the Kingdom of Cambodia, including the seabed and subsea layers of the Exclusive Economic Zone and the Seabed Plateau, as well as other areas sovereign by the Kingdom of Cambodia.

"Article 126 Definitions
The main terms used in this Chapter are defined as follows:
1. For the purpose of petroleum operations:
A- Petroleum refers to crude oil, natural gas and other hydrocarbons, whether in solid, liquid, gaseous, natural state and any other substance that is a component of hydrocarbons.
B- Petroleum agreement refers to a petroleum production sharing contract or any form of contract provided for under the Law on the Management of Petroleum and Petroleum Products and related regulations between the Royal Government of Cambodia and the relevant taxpayers to conduct petroleum operations.
C- Petroleum operations refers to all activities of exploration, development and production of petroleum carried out in the petroleum agreement area in accordance with the petroleum agreement.
D- Agreement area refers to the area subject to the petroleum agreement that was initially granted, including any part of that area that was returned in accordance with the petroleum agreement.
E. Development project refers to the development plan, development work program and development work activities to develop and produce petroleum in the agreement area approved by the institution.
F The closure and environmental restoration plan refers to the closure and environmental restoration plan of the taxpayer approved by the institution under the petroleum agreement in accordance with the Law on the Management of Petroleum and Petroleum Products.
G. Pre-exploration costs refer to the costs of exploration to determine the initial petroleum geological potential without the right to develop and produce.
C. Exploration costs refer to the costs of geological, petrological, geophysical, geochemical, topographic surveys, data analysis costs, site visits, pre-development engineering costs, exploration drilling costs, feasibility studies, environmental impact studies, general administrative costs and other costs incurred in petroleum operations to determine the presence, location, quantity and quality of petroleum resource habitats.
C. Development costs refer to the costs incurred after the institution has approved the development project to build production facilities for petroleum operations, including site preparation, well drilling, construction of production wells and construction of petroleum pipelines as production facilities, purchase costs Tangible and intangible assets, as well as activities related to the development of the petroleum agreement holder, in accordance with the conditions stipulated in the production permit issued by the institution.
Nh - Reserve for site closure and environmental restoration costs refers to the reserve that is allowed to be deducted in advance for site closure and environmental restoration costs in accordance with the plan and conditions set by the institution.
D Total costs for site closure and environmental restoration refers to the total costs for site closure and environmental restoration in the agreement area approved by the institution according to the taxpayer's site closure and environmental restoration plan in accordance with the petroleum agreement.
T Time of commencement of commercial production refers to the time when the taxpayer begins commercial production in accordance with the provisions of the petroleum agreement or the provisions of the institution.
2. For the purpose of mineral resource operations:
A Mineral resource refers to any substance, whether in solid, liquid, or gaseous form, that occurs naturally through geological processes or as a result of extraction from the ground, on land, in the sea, or under the seabed, such as gemstones, coal, non-metallic minerals, metallic minerals, mineral water, and rock. Gravel, sand and clay. The term mineral resources does not include petroleum as stated in Article a of paragraph 1 of this article.
B- Mineral resources license refers to a permit that authorizes the taxpayer by the institution to operate mineral resources.
C- Mineral resources operation refers to all activities authorized under a permit or mineral resources license. Mineral resources operation is divided into the pre-exploration phase, the exploration phase and the mineral resources exploitation phase.
D License area refers to the area authorized to operate mineral resources and is the subject of the license, including any part of the area that has been abandoned in accordance with the mineral resources license.
E- Site closure and environmental restoration plan refers to the taxpayer's environmental restoration plan approved by the institution under the mineral resources license. Site restoration includes mine clearance, reforestation, and clean-up within the license area.
F Pre-exploration expenses refers to expenses related to the initial exploration phase in The surface layer of the earth using simple tools that have minimal impact on the surface to determine the presence of mineral resources.
G- Exploration costs refer to the costs of research studies with the aim of discovering, testing mineral indices to determine the potential, size, quality, quantity and economic feasibility of the business through surveys, geological, geophysical and geochemical research, excavation, drilling, transportation and analysis of soil, sediment, water, rock and other mineral samples, as well as general administrative costs and other costs incurred in the operation of mineral resources to determine the presence, location, quantity and quality of mineral resource habitats.
G Development costs refer to the costs incurred to develop mineral resource habitats to start commercial production, including design, construction, installation of production facilities, drilling of production wells, drilling of production wells and all related activities.

Article 127. Income Tax Rate
1. Taxpayers engaged in kerosene operations and taxpayers engaged in mineral resources operations, as provided in Article 126 of this Law, shall be subject to income tax at the rate of 30 (thirty) percent of the taxable income in a taxable year.
2- In addition to the tax rate as provided in Paragraph 1 of this Article, the taxpayer shall be taxed on excess income at the rate of growth by class as provided in Paragraph 3 of this Article based on the proportion of excess income.
3- The excess income tax rate is as shown in the table below:
4. Taxpayers are exempt from paying the minimum tax as provided in Article 24 of this Law.

Article 128. Policies and Restrictions of Expense Deduction
1. Taxpayers are allowed to calculate taxable income by deducting expenses as provided in Articles 129 to 133 of this Law at the end of the taxable year in which the activities, production, trade occurred, including other related current expenses in each taxable year.
2- Expenses related to the operation of kerosene or mineral resources in any of the contracted areas or any licensing territory for any taxable year are allowed to be deducted only from the gross revenue from the operation of kerosene or mineral resources in the contracting area or licensing domain of that taxable year.
3- If, in any taxable year, the total expenditure related to the operation of petroleum or mineral resources in the contracted area or licensing domain exceeds the total gross revenue resulting in a loss, the loss shall be considered as a burden for deduction from the taxable income achieved in the next taxable year. In the event of a loss of more than 1 (one) year, the reference to the loss shall be in accordance with the order of the year in which such loss occurred.
4- Losses incurred in any of the contracted areas or licensed domains shall not be subject to deductions in other contracted areas or licensed domains.

Article 129. Interest expense
Taxpayers are allowed to deduct interest expenses according to the debt-to-capital ratio ratio of 3 (three) to capital1 (one).

Article 130. Reserve for site closure and environmental restoration costs or site restoration costs
The reserve for site closure and environmental restoration costs or site restoration costs is determined as follows:
1- For petroleum operations:
a- If the taxpayer has a site closure and environmental restoration plan approved by the institution, the amount required by the taxpayer to pay into the fund for site closure and environmental restoration costs is considered a reserve for site closure and environmental restoration costs. This reserve is allowed as a provision and is allowed to be deducted in the taxable year for the purpose of calculating taxable income. In the case where the taxpayer does not have a site closure and environmental restoration plan approved by the institution, the reserve under this paragraph is not allowed.
b- The reserve for site closure and environmental restoration costs is calculated based on the total costs approved by the institution for site closure and environmental restoration. The reserve for site closure and environmental restoration costs in each year and the year in which the reserve is allowed to be deducted shall be determined according to the site closure and environmental restoration plan.
C- If the total actual costs of the mine closure and environmental restoration exceed the total amount of the provision for mine closure and environmental restoration, the excess amount shall be allowed to be deducted from the taxable income for the year.
D- If, at the end of the mine closure and environmental restoration, the total actual costs of the mine closure and environmental restoration are less than the total amount of the provision for mine closure and environmental restoration, the excess amount shall be included in the taxable income for the taxable year in which the mine closure and environmental restoration is completed.
2- For mineral resource operations:
A- If the taxpayer has a mine closure and environmental restoration plan approved by the institution, the amount required by the taxpayer to pay into the fund for mine closure and environmental restoration is considered a provision for mine closure and environmental restoration. This provision shall be allowed as a provision and shall be allowed to be deducted in the taxable year for the purpose of calculating taxable income. In the case where the taxpayer does not have a mine closure and environmental restoration plan approved by the institution, the provision under this paragraph shall not be allowed.
B- The reserve for site restoration costs is calculated based on the total costs approved by the institution for mine closure and environmental restoration. The reserve for site restoration costs in each year and the year in which the reserve is allowed to start deducting shall be determined in accordance with the mine closure and environmental restoration plan.
C- If the total actual costs of mine closure and environmental restoration exceed the total amount of the reserve for site restoration costs, the excess amount shall be allowed to be deducted from the annual taxable income.
D- If, at the end of the mine closure and environmental restoration, the total actual costs of mine closure and environmental restoration are less than the total amount of the reserve for site restoration costs, the excess amount shall be included in taxable income for the taxable year in which the mine closure and environmental restoration is completed.
3. The rules and procedures for managing the reserve for site closure and environmental restoration costs shall be determined by a joint declaration between the Ministry of Economy and Finance and the institution.

Article 131. How to save
The method of revocation is determined as follows:
1. The taxpayer shall amortize the expenditure on the expenditure on exploration and development in an equal manner in accordance with Article 132 of this Law.
2. For physical and intangible property other than precursors, exploration and development expenses purchased or created after the commencement of commercial production in the area where the agreement is signed or the licensing domain, the taxpayer shall dispose of the physical property in accordance with Articles A to D of Paragraph 1 of Article 13 of this Law and dispose of the intangible property in accordance with Article 14 of this Law.

Article 132. Equal
Equal rates for petroleum and mineral resources operations are determined as follows:
1. For kerosene operations:
a- The taxpayer shall amortize the man's expenditure and exploratory expenditure in an equal manner according to the expected life expectancy of the commercial production under the development project or 5 (five) years, choosing whichever option is less.
b- The taxpayer shall amortize the development expenditure in a manner equal to the expected life expectancy of the commercial production of each means of production under the development project or 10 (ten) years for the operation of kerosene by choosing whichever option is less.
c- In case the expected life expectancy of the commercial production of any means of production under the development project is modified, the taxpayer shall make adjustments to make adjustments to the remaining expenses, precursors, exploration expenses and development expenses according to the revised expected life period, not exceeding the life expectancy specified in Paragraph A and Article B of this paragraph.
2- For mineral resources operations:
a. The taxpayer shall amortize the pre-expenditure and exploratory expenditure in an equal manner according to the expected life expectancy of the commercial production under the development project or 5 (five) years, choosing whichever option is less.
b. The taxpayer shall amortize the development expenditure in a manner equal to the expected lifetime of the commercial production under the development project or seven (seven) years, choosing whichever is less.
c- In case the expected life expectancy of commercial production under the development project is modified, the taxpayer shall make adjustments to the amortization of the experiential expenditure, exploration expenditure and the remaining development expenditure according to the revised expected life period, not exceeding the expiry life under Paragraph A and Paragraph B of this paragraph.
d- In case the taxpayer has a development project with a duration of less than 1 (one) year, the development cost may be included in the amortization and exploration expenses.

Article 133. Ukuhlaziywa kwe-Abortion
The time limit is as follows:
1- The taxpayer shall repay the precurement, exploration and development expenses incurred before the commencement of the first commercial production at the end of the taxable year in which the taxpayer commences the first commercial production in the area where the agreement or license is signed.
2. After commencing the first commercial production in the area where the agreement is signed or the license domain is signed, if the taxpayer conducts pre-construction or explores or continues to construct other means of production under the development project in the area where the agreement is signed or the license domain, the taxpayer shall pay the pre-tax expenses, exploration expenses and development expenses at the following times:
a- At the end of each taxable year for pre-tax expenses or exploration expenses according to the order of the year in which the expenditure was incurred.
b- At the end of the taxable year in which each means of production is used for development expenses.
Each means of production under the development project shall be made separately in accordance with Article 132 of this Law and shall be aggregated for deduction in the taxable year.
3. For physical and intangible assets other than precursors, exploration and development expenses purchased or created after the commencement of commercial production in the area of the agreement or license domain, the taxpayer shall dispose of them at the end of the taxable year in which those assets are put into use.

Article 134. Transfer of benefits and development and co-production
1 - In the event of a partial or wholly transfer of a benefit that is a right or share in the kerosene agreement or mineral resources license in the form of sale, purchase, exchange or gift, the taxpayer, who is the transferor and the individual as the beneficiary shall comply with the following:
a. The taxpayer who is the transferor shall record the income derived from the transfer of benefits in the kerosene agreement or mineral resources license as income from the operation of kerosene or mineral resources subject to income tax as provided for in Chapter II of this Law.
b- The person who is the beneficiary shall:
Continue to implement fiscal obligations from taxpayers who are transferors to benefits that are rights or shares received.
Continue to dispose of physical property, supernatural property, precursive expenses, exploration expenses, and development expenses in accordance with the rules and procedures and bases that the taxpayer who is the transferor has done in the past.
In the event that the transfer of benefits in a kerosene agreement or mineral resources license is valued in excess of the actual accounting value, the offset value shall be treated as a commercial fund.
The individual as a continuing recipient shall record as revenues for subsequent years by dividing these revenues in proportion to the expected life of the remaining commercial production or 10 (ten) years for kerosene operations and 7 (seven) years for mineral resources operations, choosing whichever option is less.
2- For two or more taxpayers who are allowed to enter into joint development and production agreements to carry out joint operations in the development and production of one or more kerosene reserves located in different kerosene agreement areas, the rules and procedures to be applied shall be determined by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 135. Duties of a taxpayer
1. A non-resident taxpayer who has entered into a kerosene agreement or mineral resources license with the Royal Government of Cambodia as provided for in Article 126 of this Law shall form a local company for the Contracting Area in accordance with the prevailing laws of the Kingdom of Cambodia at least 15 (fifteen) days prior to the commencement of economic activities.
2. The taxpayer shall submit a letter of fiscal declaration and payment of monthly and annual VAT to the Fiscal Administration in accordance with the provisions of the law and the letter of customs norms on taxation.
3. The operator, who is the representative of all taxpayers in the contracting area or licensing domain, shall provide reports and documents of business transactions in the contracting area or licensing domain as required by the Fiscal Administration.

Article 136. Fiscal incentives
The provision of fiscal incentives to any kerosene agreement or mineral resources license made prior to the entry into force of the provisions of this Chapter shall be determined by a decree at the request of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 137. Implementation of tax regulations
Taxpayers engaged in kerosene transactions and taxpayers engaged in mineral resources transactions as provided in Article 126 of this Law shall comply with the provisions of this Chapter and other provisions on taxation.

Article 138. Rules and procedures for managing tax collection
The rules and procedures for the management of tax collection on petroleum operations or mineral resources operations shall be determined by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 139. Subjects of Taxes
Property rental tax is applicable on the rental of property in the Kingdom of Cambodia.

Article 140. Scope of Taxes
The property rent tax applies to the owner or the right of the owner of the property who is not a taxpayer under the automatic declaration regime.

Article 141. Definition
The main vocabulary used in this chapter is defined as follows:
1- Real estate refers to:
a- Buildings and other structures such as houses, factories, hotels, offices as well as their appendices.
b- Adjacent to industrial establishments.
c- Commercial property, on-site industry, large buildings or warehouses.0
d- Mobile residence for accommodation or other business activities.
d. Land without construction.
2. Inheritance refers to the person who has the right to the property through the grant by the owner of the property.
3. Real estate rent refers to the gross wage contracted or agreed with the tenant based on the market price.

Article 142. Tax rate
Property rent tax is set at the rate of 10 (ten) percent of the property rent.

Article 143. Tax Exemption
Property rental tax is exempted as follows:
1- Royalties from the rental of real estate of the Royal Government or ministries or government institutions.
2- Royalties from the rental of real estate of foreign diplomatic missions or consulates, international organizations and other government technical cooperation agencies.
3- Royalties from the rental of the property of any organization or association that:
A is organized and operated for purely religious, charitable, scientific, literary or educational purposes.
b- No share of the fee is used for private benefit.
4- The money deposited by the tenant as a security deposit and upon the end of the contract, the owner of the tenant must return the full amount to the tenant.
5. Wages that have already been withheld by the enterprise as a taxpayer under the automatic declaration regime under Articles 25 and 26 of this Law.
6- The rent from the rental of the property of the enterprise as a taxpayer according to the automatic declaration regime which has already been included in the taxable income of the enterprise.

Article 144. Obligations of the property owner or rights
The owner of the employee or the owner's rights shall have the following obligations:
