1- Be registered with the Fiscal Administration in the geographical area where the real estate is located within 15 (fifteen) days from the date of signing the lease contract or from the date of change in the contract according to the form determined by the Fiscal Administration.
2. To notify in writing to the Fiscal Administration within 15 (fifteen) days after the cessation of the lease with the date and valid signature of the owner or representative of the owner.
3- A receipt must be issued to the tenant at the time of receipt of wages.
4. Submit a declaration letter of payment of property rent tax to the Fiscal Administration according to the following deadline:
a. every month no later than the 20th day of the following month if the contract requires monthly payment.
b. No later than the 20th day of the month following the month in which the payment is to be made according to the total amount if the contract requires the total payment for several months.

Article 145. Tenant's duties
The tenant shall be obliged to present the receipt of the payment provided by the owner and shall provide other information related to the lease to the Fiscal Administration.

Article 146. Rules and procedures for managing tax collection
The rules and procedures of managing the collection of property rent tax shall be determined by the Announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 147. Subjects of Taxes
Property tax is applied to properties located in the Kingdom of Cambodia.

Article 148. Scope of Taxes
Property tax applies to real estate located in the provincial capital administration of the Kingdom of Cambodia.

Article 149.Definitions
For the purposes of the regulation on property tax, the term real estate refers to land, houses, buildings and other constructions.

Article 150. Tax rate
Property tax is collected annually at the rate of 0.1 (zero comma) percent.

Article 151. Basis of tax
The property tax basis and the Property Valuation Commission for property tax shall be determined and established by the Proclamation of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 152. Tax Exemption
Property tax is exempted as follows:
1- Real estate which is agricultural land.
2- Real estate belonging to the Royal Government or Ministries, Royal Government Institutions.
3. Property belonging to any community or individual who:
A is organized and operated for purely religious and charitable goals.
b. No share of the property or income is used for private benefit.
4- Real estate belonging to diplomatic missions or foreign consulates, international organizations and other government technical cooperation agencies.
5- Real estate, which is infrastructure, consisting of roads, bridges, clean water production or production systems, electricity, airports, ports, motor terminals, including buildings and offices that directly serve the activities of those infrastructures.

Article 153 Obligation to file a tax declaration and payment
The owner or occupier or ultimate beneficiary of the property shall be obliged to file a declaration and pay the annual tax.

Article 154 Rules and Procedures for Managing Tax Collection
The rules and procedures of the management of property tax collection shall be determined by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 155 Objects of Taxation
Stamp tax applies to the transfer of ownership or right of occupancy or the placement of shares as real estate and immovable property, the transfer of shares, contracts for the supply of goods or services using the state budget and letters of character.

Article 156 Scope of Taxation
Stamp tax applies to:
1- Transfer of ownership or right to occupy real estate and immovable property or placing shares as real estate and immovable property in the company.
2- Transfer of any or all shares of the Company's shares.
3- Contract for the supply of goods or services using the state budget.
4. Letters of merit, including letters on the dissolution of the combined company and letters on the closure of the company.

Article 157 Definitions
The main vocabulary used in this chapter is defined as follows:
1. Circle of petition refers to:
Between the birth parent and the birth child
Between husband and wife
Between the grandmother and the grandchild
Between the Founding Brothers and the Founding Brothers
Between parents and son
between the grandmother and the granddaughter.
2- Inheritance refers to the transfer of ownership or right to occupy real estate from a living person to a petition without taking a fee.
3- Execution refers to the transfer of ownership or right to occupy real estate from the deceased person to the petitioner.
4. Contract price refers to the price specified in the contract for the supply of goods or services using the state budget.
5- Share price refers to the value of the transfer of shares based on the market price.
6- Shares refer to any or all shares or interests or sales of business of individual companies, co-ownership companies and sole proprietorships registered or unregistered with the Ministry or competent body.
7- Real estate refers to land, houses, buildings and other constructions, whether registered or not registered by the Land Integrity Administration.
8- Real estate company refers to any company that directly or indirectly occupies real estate valued at more than 50 (fifty) percent of the company's total asset value.
9- Property refers to all kinds of means of transport or vehicles, such as ships, ferries, boats, canoes, oars, automobiles, tractors, tractors, and similar vehicles.
10. Letter of Qualification refers to a Letter of Qualification on the dissolution of a consolidated company and the closure of a company registered at the Ministry or competent institution.

Article 158 Tax Rates
Stamp tax shall be determined at the following rates:
1-4 (four) percent of the value of the property for the transfer of ownership or right to occupy construction property and/or land or the placement of shares as real estate in the company or the transfer of shares or similar interests of the real estate company.
2- 4 (four) percent of the value of the property on the transfer of ownership or right to occupy the property or the placement of shares as real estate in the company.
3- 0.1 (one comma) percentage of the share value for the transfer of any or all shares of the Company's shares.
4.0.1 (zero comma) percent of the contracted value for a contract for the supply of goods or services using the state budget.
5. KHR 1000,000 (one million) for a letter of merit, including a letter on the dissolution of the combined company and a letter on the closure of the company.

Article 159 Tax basis
The stamp duty basis is determined as follows:
The Ministry of Economy and Finance may determine the value of real estate and immovable property for the purpose of calculating this tax.
2- The price of shares or similar interests shall be calculated according to the market price at the time of the transaction, the transfer of shares or similar interests occurs.
3. The contract price shall be calculated according to the price in the contract for the supply of goods or services using the state budget.
4. Letters of customs shall be set at 1,000,000 (one million) riels for each letter of customs.

Article 160 Taxpayers
Stamp duty shall apply to:
1- The receiver of ownership or right to occupy real estate and immovable property.
2- The inheritor of ownership or the right to hold shares.
3- You receive a contract for the supply of goods or services using the state budget.
4- The beneficiary of the letter of customary characteristic.

Article 161 Tax Exemption and Preferences
Stamp duty is exempted and preferential as follows:
1. Receipt of ownership or right to occupy land in concession from the Royal Government.
2- Acquisition of ownership or right to occupy real estate in the circle of petition.
3. Acquisition of ownership of motor vehicles, motor vehicles of all kinds, tractors and rickshaws of all types with a power of up to 150 (one hundred and fifty) horses.
4. Acquisition of ownership or right to occupy real estate and immovable property to be recorded in the inventory of various state institutions of the Kingdom of Cambodia.
5- Acquisition of ownership or right to occupy real estate and movable property of diplomatic missions or consulates, foreign organizations, international organizations and technical cooperation agencies of other governments.
6- Purchase of real estate of various enterprises as goods for resale.

Article 162 Obligation to file a tax declaration and payment
Taxpayers are obliged to submit a tax declaration letter and pay the tax in full within three (3) months for:
1. Transfer of ownership of real estate and immovable property or placement of shares as real estate and immovable property in the Company.
2. Transfer of any or all shares of the Company's shares.
3- Contract for the supply of goods or services using the state budget.
4. Letters of merit, including letters on the dissolution of the combined company and letters on the closure of the company.

Article 163 Failure to file a tax declaration and payment
If any new owner or occupier has not paid stamp duty:
1. The Land Administration shall not issue or transfer a new property owner identification certificate or a new real estate title or similar permit.
2. Subnational administrative authorities, including capitals, provinces, municipalities, districts, districts, communes, sangkat villages, shall not specify the transfer of real estate occupancy rights.
3. Public and transport bodies or competent authorities shall not issue new identification cards for the transfer of ownership of all types of means of transport and vehicles, except for motor vehicles, motor vehicles of all kinds, tractors and rickshaws of vehicles with a power of up to 150 (one hundred and fifty) horses.

Article 164 Rules and Procedures for Managing Tax Collection
The rules and procedures of the stamp tax collection management shall be determined by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 165 Objects of Taxation
Capital gains tax shall apply to capital gains made from the sale or transfer of capital in the Kingdom of Cambodia and abroad by individual physical taxpayers and from the sale or transfer of capital in the Kingdom of Cambodia by foreign taxpayers.

Article 166 Scope of tax
Capital gains tax applies to taxpayers who earn capital gains.

Article 167 Definitions
The main vocabulary used in this chapter is defined as follows:
1. Taxpayer refers to a retired taxpayer or a retired taxpayer who has sold or transferred capital to another person.
2. Retired taxpayer means a physical person who has a residence or place of residence in the Kingdom of Cambodia or who has been present in the Kingdom of Cambodia for more than 182 (one hundred and fifty-two) days in any 12 (twelve) month ending in the current tax year.
3- Alien taxpayer refers to a physical individual or entity who is not a taxpayer.
4- Capital refers to real estate, contracts, investment assets, business reputation, intellectual property and foreign currency.
5. Capital gains refer to taxable income derived from the acquisition of income from the sale or transfer of capital minus deductions for permissible expenses.

Article 168 Tax Rates
The capital gains tax rate is determined at the rate of 20 (twenty) percent.

Article 169 Tax Exemption
Capital gains tax is exempt for sales or transfers:
1- Property belonging to state institutions.
2- Assets belonging to foreign diplomatic missions or consulates, international organizations and technical cooperation agencies of other governments.
3- Pension as the principal of the taxpayer.
4- Real estate in the circle of petitions.
5- Property for serving the public interest in accordance with the Law on Infrastructure.
6- Agricultural land belonging to or the right of occupation of the citizen who is a farmer is fertile, real and has a residential address in the commune/district where the agricultural farm is located.

Article 170 Rules of Deduction of Expenses
The rules of deduction of expenses for capital gains are as follows:
1 How to cut expenses as scheduled.
2 Ways to Cut Expenses Practically.

Article 171 Obligation to file tax declaration and payment
The taxpayer or withholding agent must submit a tax declaration letter in the form prescribed by the Fiscal Administration and pay capital gains tax to the Fiscal Administration within a period not exceeding three (three) months after achieving capital gains.

Article 172 Rules and Procedures for Tax Collection Administration
The rules and procedures of the management of capital gains tax collection shall be determined by the announcement of the Minister, Ministry of Economy and Finance.

Article 173 Objects of Taxation
The tax on unused land shall be applied on unused constructed land and unused unconstructed land.

Article 174 Scope of Taxation
The unused land tax applies to unused land located in the Kingdom of Cambodia.

Article 175 Definitions
For the purposes of the regulation on tax on unused land, the term unused land refers to land with or without unused construction.

Article 176 Tax Rates
Tax on unused land shall be collected annually at the rate of 2 (two) percent.

Article 177 Basis of Taxation
The basis for calculating the tax on unused land shall be based on the land value determined by the Land Assessment Commission for the tax on unused land.

Article 178 Tax Exemption
Tax exemption on unused land is determined by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 179 Obligation to file a tax declaration and payment
The owner or occupier or ultimate beneficiary of unused land shall be obliged to submit a declaration and pay annual tax.

Article 180 Rules and Procedures for Tax Collection Administration
The rules and procedures of the management of tax collection on unused land shall be determined by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 181 Objects of tax
The transport tax shall apply to all types of transport.

Article 182 Scope of tax
Transport tax applies to means of transport in the Kingdom of Cambodia.

Article 183 Definitions
For the purposes of the Regulation on Means of Transport Tax, the term means of transport refers to any type of means of transport or vehicle, such as ships, ferries, boats, canoes, oars, automobiles, tractors, tractors, and similar vehicles.

Article 184 Tax Rates
1. The tax on means of transport shall be determined according to the following types of means of transport:
A truck.
B- Peanut truck head, peanut mine, peanut semi.
c. Passenger cars.
d. Vehicle or vehicle vehicle.
Touring cars.
e. Vehicles or recycling vehicles.
2- The tax rate on means of transport shall be determined by a decree at the request of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 185 Taxpayers
The tax on the means of transport shall apply to the owner of the means of transport.

Article 186 Tax Exemption
Transport tax is exempt for:
1- Ambulances, fire trucks belonging to the State.
2- Vehicles belonging to the Cambodian Armed Forces Unit, the Royal Thai Armed Forces and the National Guard.
3. Vehicles belonging to foreign embassies or consulates, international organizations or other government technical cooperation agencies.
4. Motor vehicles and motor vehicles of all kinds, tractors and similar machinery and vehicles of all kinds with a power of 150 (one hundred and fifty) horsepower or less.

Article 187 Obligation to file a tax declaration and payment
The owner is obliged to submit a declaration letter and pay the annual tax.

Article 188 Rules and Procedures for Managing Tax Collection
The rules and procedures of the management of tax collection on means of transport shall be determined by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 189 Objects
1- The provisions of this Chapter define the rights and obligations of the taxpayer, the powers and obligations of the fiscal administration and the procedure of reviewing the tax paid.
2. All provisions of this Chapter shall apply to all types of taxes, except for any separate taxes that otherwise provide.

Article 190 Definitions
The main vocabulary used in Chapters 17 and 18 is defined as follows:
1-Taxes refer to taxes and VAT.
2- Individual refers to the physical individual or individual.
3- Taxpayer refers to a person who is obliged to pay taxes.
4. Fiscal Administration refers to the organization assigned by the General Department of Taxation.
5. Tax Officer refers to a tax officer of all ranks who is serving within the framework of the General Department of Taxation.
6- Investigation refers to all types of tax audits, including investigation of offences on tax regulations.
7- Fiscal declaration letter means a document in which the tax regulations require the taxpayer or withholding agent to meet the conditions provided for in this Act.
8. Withholding agent refers to a person whose tax regulations require the withholding and payment of tax into the state budget on behalf of the debtor.
9. Economic activity refers to the activity of an individual who does it continuously or once in a while to earn or not make a profit in supplying or intends to supply goods or services to other individuals in order to obtain some benefit.
10. Additional tax refers to a cash penalty for an offense against tax regulations, which is calculated at a fixed rate on the basis of underpaid or late paid tax.
11- Interest refers to the interest arising from the underpayment or late payment of tax, which is calculated at a determined rate on the basis of underpaid or late payment.

Article 191 International Agreements
1. The provisions of international agreements concerning tax matters to which the Kingdom of Cambodia, as a State Party, shall have the scope to cover the provisions of this Act.
2. The rules and procedures for implementing the provisions of international agreements on tax issues shall be determined by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 192 Language used in proclamation letters and fiscal documents
All tax declaration letters, as well as other documents and correspondence necessary for tax determination, tax collection and compulsory compliance with tax laws and customs norms or other forms of tax determination, shall be in Khmer.

Article 193 Rights and obligations of taxpayers
The rights and obligations of taxpayers are defined as follows:
1- Taxpayers have the following rights [cite: 240]
a- To be kept confidential and used only for the purposes specified in the tax regulations of information relating to its business affairs provided to the Fiscal Administration as provided in Article 197 of this Law. [CITE: 240]
b- Receive regular information on the progress of the tax system and the procedures for determining taxes as provided in Articles 199 and 211 of this Law. [CITE: 240]
c- Receive information about its rights, including the right to lodge a complaint as provided in Articles 211 and 238 of this Law. [Cite: 241]
d- Lodge a complaint as provided in this Law against all decisions of the Fiscal Administration as provided in Articles 211 and 238 of this Law. [CITE: 241]
d. Pay taxes not exceeding the provisions on taxation as provided in Article 213 of this Law.
2- Taxpayers have the following obligations [CITE: 242]
a- Register with the Fiscal Administration as provided in Article 203 of this Law. [CITE: 242]
b- Submit a fiscal declaration and provide information as required by the tax regulations as provided in Articles 201 and 206 of this Law. [CITE: 242]
c. Pay taxes on the due date as provided in the regulations on taxation. [CITE: 242]
d. Maintain, maintain and disclose the list, letters of justice and other documents to the Fiscal Administration as provided in the provisions on taxation and Article 201 of this Law.
d- Appear to the Fiscal Administration on the date stated in the notification letter of the Fiscal Administration as provided in Article 202 of this Law. [CITE: 242]
(f) Pay taxes, additional taxes and other interest as determined by the Fiscal Administration on the date as provided in the Regulations on Taxation or for which the Fiscal Administration has notified in writing as provided in the Regulations on Taxation and Articles 213, 232 and 233 of this Law. [CITE: 243]

Article 194 Powers and Obligations of the Fiscal Administration [CITE: 243]
The powers and obligations of the fiscal administration are defined as follows: [CITE: 243]
1- The Fiscal Administration has the following powers: [CITE: 243]
a- Determine the basis of taxation on taxpayers or withholding agents as provided in Articles 209 and 210 of this Law. [CITE: 243]
b. Requiring the taxpayer or withholding agent to appear as provided in Article 202 of this Law. [CITE: 243]
c- Determine the list of necessary documents and letters of justice that the taxpayer or withholding agent shall keep, keep and provide to the fiscal administration as provided in Articles 201 and 230 of this Law. [CITE: 244]
d- Requiring the taxpayer or the taxpayer to provide information relating to the taxpayer or the withholding agent as provided in Article 202 of this Law. [CITE: 244]
d- Entering the residence or business establishment of the taxpayer, withholding agent or the beneficiary in order to obtain information relating to the taxpayer or withholding agent as provided in Article 230 of this Law. [CITE: 244]
(cite: 244] Obtain from any State institution information relating to or relating to the taxpayer or withholding agent as provided in Article 209 of this Law. [CITE: 244]
e- Implement strict measures against the taxpayer or withholding agent when the person fails to pay taxes, additional taxes and other interest as required in Articles 217, 218, 220, 221 and 222 of this Law. [CITE: 245]
[CITE: 245]
(c) Reject and/or re-determine the true nature of any transaction in case of review, finding that the taxpayer has prepared or engaged in any transaction that shows a false or unrealistic intention in order to reduce or eliminate the amount of tax payable, which is contrary to the spirit of the tax regulations.
2- The Fiscal Administration has the following obligations: [CITE: 246]
a- Collect taxes, additional taxes and other interest as provided in Article 195 of this Law;
b. Maintain the confidentiality of the information provided by the taxpayer or the taxpayer and provide such information only to any person specified in the tax regulations as provided in Articles 197 and 244 of this Law.
c- Provide information to the taxpayer or withholding agent to ensure the appropriate implementation in accordance with the provisions on taxation as provided in Article 199 of this Law. [CITE: 247]
d- Refund or credit the overpaid tax as provided in the tax regulations.
d- Giving a notice of tax determination to the taxpayer or withholding agent as provided in Articles 209 to 211 of this Law;

Article 195 Competent Bodies [CITE: 247]
1- The bodies responsible for managing the implementation of tax regulations are as follows: [CITE: 247]
A Directorate General of Taxation of the Ministry of Economy and Finance.
b- Other institutions of the Royal Government to which the tax regulations have been empowered.
2- The Fiscal Administration is obliged to collect taxes, enforce the provisions of the Regulations on Taxation and appeal to the courts in case of violation of the law.
[cite: 248] The decision of part or all of the administrative acts is the authority of the Minister of Economy and Finance. [Cite: 248] The Fiscal Administration may decide to partially or wholly decide on this administrative act in case of obtaining a delegation of authority from the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 196 Authority in times of national emergency [CITE: 249]
1- In case the nation faces an economic, financial crisis or emergency or any urgent need to ensure the livelihood and well-being of the people and ensure the normalcy of the economic and social process, the Royal Government may decide to grant or exempt or suspend any type of tax immediately, partly or in whole at the request of the Minister of Economy and Finance. [CITE: 249]
2. The granting of any preferential treatment or exemption or suspension of any type of tax as provided in the above paragraph shall be subject to subsequent regulatory action by the Finance Act.

Article 197 Confidentiality of Tax Information
1. The Fiscal Administration and all persons who are or have been officers and agents of the Fiscal Administration shall maintain the confidentiality of information concerning taxpayers received in the course of fulfilling official duties and may provide information only to persons authorized by this Article.
2. Officers and agents of the Fiscal Administration may provide information of interest to taxpayers to:
a. Officers and other agencies of the Fiscal Administration in time and in order to fulfil their duties in accordance with the provisions on taxation.
b. Criminal authorities for the target of prosecution of tax offences.
c. The court is in the trial stage to determine the taxpayer's tax payable or liability for the violation of tax regulations.
d. The competent authority has the jurisdiction to relate to the taxation of any other country in accordance with international agreements.
3. A person who has received information from another person who has been authorized to provide information as provided in paragraph 2 of this Article shall maintain the confidentiality of such information in accordance with the provisions of this Article, except to any minimum level that is necessary to allow the provision of such information.
4. Information relating to the taxpayer may be provided to another person with the written consent of the taxpayer.

Article 198 Provision of information to taxpayers
1. A letter or notification letter provided by the fiscal administration to the taxpayer shall be deemed to be obligated to the taxpayer unless the letter or notice is in writing and handed over to the taxpayer.
2- In case the regulations on taxation require the fiscal administration to provide a letter or letter of notice to an individual, the letter or letter of notification is considered to have been duly delivered, unless it has been delivered to that person or has also been sent by post as a letter of intent to the legal address of that person. The taxpayer gave it to the fiscal administration.
In the case of a certified letter or notification sent by a certified letter, the date of notification is the date of stamping on the certified letter of the post office.
4. The letter or letter of notification shall be deemed to have been duly handed over if the conditions in paragraph 2 of this Article have already been fulfilled even if the person who is notified refuses to hand over or receive the letter of recommendation.
5- In case the address of the person has been changed and the individual has not notified the Fiscal Administration of the change, the affidavit or notification letter sent to the most recently known address shall be deemed to have been duly delivered.
6. In case for any reason the affidavit or notification letter cannot be provided to the taxpayer as provided in paragraphs 1 to 5 of this Article, the affidavit or notification letter is considered to have been duly handed over if the Fiscal Administration:
a- Seal the letter or notification letter attached to the door of the taxpayer's residence or place of business, or
b- Advertise in the press, radio, television or website of the Fiscal Administration by requiring the taxpayer to appear at the Fiscal Administration not later than 15 (fifteen) days after the date of publication.

Article 199. Dissemination and Explanation of Tax Regulations
1. The Fiscal Administration shall prepare a brief explanatory book on the main contents of each type of tax.
2- For any type of tax that the fiscal administration determines should be explained, the local tax officer shall educate the taxpayer to understand the duties and rights of those taxpayers.

Article 200. Incentives for tax collection
1- The Ministry of Economy and Finance shall build an incentive system for fiscal administration.
2- The rules and procedures for the operation of the incentive system shall be determined by the announcement of the Minister, Ministry of Economy and Finance.

Article 201. Holding, recording and keeping lists, letters of justice and financial documents
1. Taxpayers shall hold, record and keep lists, letters of justice and other financial documents as prescribed by the tax regulations and shall file such lists and documents as required by the Fiscal Administration.
2. Taxpayers who are not obliged to hold accounting lists in accordance with the International Financial Reporting Standards of Cambodia as prescribed by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance shall keep a journal recording in order of day and month all other revenues and expenses related to business as determined by the Fiscal Administration.
3. In case the taxpayer fails to hold, record or record incorrectly the accounting list or records in accordance with the prescribed conditions, the Fiscal Administration shall determine the other income and expenses.
4. A person who is required to hold, record or keep lists, documents or journals prescribed by tax regulations or other regulations shall keep such lists or documents for a period of 10 (ten) years for medium and large taxpayers and 3 (three) years for small taxpayers from the end of the tax year.
5- Taxpayers are required to issue invoices on every business transaction.
6- The taxpayer must properly record the details of the invoice in the journal.

Article 202... Right to Information
1- For the purpose of determining the tax payable by any individual, or to collect taxes or to fulfill obligations in accordance with international agreements, the Fiscal Administration may send a notice to taxpayers or creditors, including banks, insurance enterprises and financial institutions, to:
a. Provide information of interest to the taxpayer or related persons as provided in the notice, such as information on suppliers, customers or bank accounts.
b- Appear at the time and place specified in the notification letter to provide information and to display or provide documents or data in the possession of that person, which are clearly stated in the notification letter.
2. In addition to the information required as provided in Paragraph 1 of this Article, the notification letter must be registered and the identification number of the taxpayer individual (if any) and the signature of the fiscal administration that issued the notification.
3. Taxpayers or their creditors, including banks, sub-guarantee enterprises and financial institutions, shall submit a report or a letter of reply to the Fiscal Administration within 30 (thirty) days after receiving the notification letter on the provision of information concerning the taxpayer.
4- All individuals may report to the Fiscal Administration information related to taxation.
5. Professional secrecy shall not impede the implementation of this Article and other articles of this Law.

Article 203.Registration and Renewal Obligations
1. Any person shall be registered with the Fiscal Administration within 15 (fifteen) days after such person commences economic activities or other activities, including activities of institutions or organizations as provided in Paragraph 3 of Article 5 of this Law.
2. All persons shall notify the Fiscal Administration within 15 (fifteen) days after the change of address, format, name, business object, transfer, termination of business, composition, manager, person in charge of tax affairs of the enterprise.
3. The rules and procedures of registration and renewal shall be determined by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 204. Registration certificate and fiscal identification number
1- Upon completion of the registration, the Fiscal Administration shall issue a certificate of registration bearing the individual's fiscal identification number.
2- All entities under the Ministry of Economy and Finance must use the identification number in this Article.

Article 205. The right of the fiscal administration to register taxpayers
The Fiscal Administration has the right to register all persons who are required to be registered by law and who have come to register, in which case the Fiscal Administration may determine the effective date of registration.

Article 206.. Filing of Fiscal Declaration Letter
The filing of the Fiscal Declaration Letter is determined as follows:
1. The taxpayer or withholding agent shall submit the tax declaration letter to the Fiscal Administration in the form, time and place specified by the Fiscal Administration.
2- The tax declaration letter must be signed by the taxpayer or the taxpayer's legal representative.
3- All investors shall submit a monthly tax declaration letter for each month and an annual fiscal declaration letter for that taxable year and pay all VAT taxes in accordance with the provisions of each tax.
4- All investors must attach a certificate of the Council for the Development of Cambodia confirming compliance with the Annual Fiscal Declaration for the tax year.
5. All taxpayers or withholding agents or investors may submit a fiscal declaration letter as provided in paragraphs 1 and 3 of this Article through the electronic declaration receipt system of the Fiscal Administration and have the same value as the original written fiscal declaration letter.

Article 207. Filing of press releases and other documents
Any person who has opened money to another person shall submit to the Fiscal Administration a letter, press release and other documents on the disclosure of such money in accordance with the form prescribed by the Fiscal Administration.

Article 208. Taxpayer Representative
The taxpayer shall be directly responsible for all actions of the person who is his/her legal representative or the person who received the transfer of rights from him or herself until the Fiscal Administration receives a written certification from the taxpayer on the revocation of the Assignment of that right.
2- An individual who is the taxpayer's representative must have the right on behalf of the taxpayer to:
Filing a Fiscal Declaration Letter
Present reports or other affidavits
Pay all VAT taxes imposed by tax regulations
Lodge a complaint
Fulfill all obligations that taxpayers must be responsible for in terms of laws and customs norms on taxation.
3- The person who is the taxpayer's representative within 15 (fifteen) days shall provide information to the Fiscal Administration by attaching written proof of valid transfer of rights.
4- A person licensed as a tax service agent may act as a taxpayer's representative and be able to provide tax-related services to taxpayers.

Article 209.Determination of tax
The amount of tax is determined as follows:
1- In case the taxpayer's tax amount is paid by withholding and the taxpayer is not obliged to make a fiscal declaration, the taxpayer's tax determination is the determination of the amount of tax withheld in the calendar year.
2- In case the taxpayer or withholding agent is obliged to file a fiscal declaration, the tax determination of the taxpayer or withholding agent is the tax determination calculated by the taxpayer or withholding agent on the fiscal declaration letter submitted to the fiscal administration.
3- In case the taxpayer or withholding agent is obliged to file a fiscal declaration letter, has not properly kept the accounting list or other documents as required or has not provided the necessary information to the fiscal administration to properly determine the tax, the determination of tax of the taxpayer or withholding agent is a unilateral tax determination made by the fiscal administration and handed over to that person.
a- Information contained in various fiscal declarations or other documents submitted by the taxpayer to the Fiscal Administration.
b- Information contained in the press release letter.
c- Other information received by the Fiscal Administration.
4- If there are grounds to state that there may be obstacles to tax collection, the fiscal administration may impose taxes on taxpayers at any time.

Article 210. Tax reassignment and tax reset period
The re-determination and re-determination period shall be carried out as follows:
1. For the determination of tax as provided in paragraph 1 of Article 209 of this Law, the Fiscal Administration may re-determine the tax within three (three) calendar years after the calendar year in which the withholding occurred.
2. With regard to the determination of taxes as provided in Paragraph 2 and Paragraph 3 of Article 209 of this Law, the Fiscal Administration may re-determine the tax within any period as follows:
a- Within three (3) years after the date of submission of the Fiscal Declaration Letter.
b- Within 10 (ten) years after the required date of filing a tax declaration, if there is evidence that there is an obstacle to the implementation of tax regulations.
c- In any period, with the written consent of the taxpayer.
3. The taxpayer or the withholding agent may request to make an adjustment to the tax declaration letter within 3 (three) years after the date of filing the tax declaration letter in accordance with paragraph 2 of Article 209 of this Law, based on the basis of confusion or omission made by the taxpayer in the previous declaration letter.
4- The taxpayer or withholding agent may request the Fiscal Administration to make adjustments to the tax redetermination within three (3) years after the date of the tax redetermination based on the additional information that the taxpayer or the Fiscal Administration did not receive at the time of the tax redetermination.
5. In case the taxpayer or the withholding agent makes adjustments to its tax determination or requests the Fiscal Administration to adjust the tax redetermination requirements, the statute of limitations for tax redetermination in paragraphs 1 and 2 of this Article shall start from the date of submission of the corrective fiscal declaration letter or the date on which the fiscal administration makes the adjustment of tax redetermination.
6. The rules and procedures of re-taxation and the re-taxation period shall be determined by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 211 . Procedures for resetting taxes
The redetermination of taxes is carried out according to the following procedure:
1. The Fiscal Administration shall send a notice of tax redetermination to the taxpayer.
2- The taxpayer has 30 (thirty) days to respond to the redetermination of the tax to the entity in charge of the redetermination.
3. If there is any objection to the re-determination of the tax, the taxpayer shall lodge a complaint with the Director General of the General Department of Taxation in accordance with the procedure as provided in Article 236 of this Law.
4. The unit in charge of tax redetermination of the General Department of Taxation shall send the result of tax redetermination to the tax collection unit within 30 (thirty) days after the issuance of the notice on tax redetermination.

Article 212.. Burden of evidence
1- In case the taxpayer does not keep enough documents or does not provide enough information, the Fiscal Administration has the right to determine the tax on the taxpayer based on the basis of the specific information that the Fiscal Administration has.
2- In case the taxable income or declared income by the taxpayer is very different from the purchase of assets or objects that make the taxpayer's expenses stand out, the fiscal administration has the right to determine the tax on the basis of the estimated income, appropriate to the size of the expenditure to purchase the prominent assets or objects.
3. The search for evidence to prove that the tax amount determined by the Fiscal Administration as in Paragraph 1 and Paragraph 2 of this Article is incorrect is the burden of the taxpayer.

Article 213. Paying taxes
The tax payment is set as follows:
1. The tax is due and payable within the period required by the tax regulations to file a fiscal declaration.
2. The tax debt is due and payable within 30 (thirty) days after the delivery of the notice of tax debt.
3. The tax amount shall be due and payable within three (3) days after the delivery of the notice of tax debt as provided in paragraph 4 of Article 209 of this Law.
4. The Minister of Economy and Finance shall promulgate rules and procedures to:
Setting a tax collection date to avoid losses due to tax debt
Ukuhlaziywa kwezinhlobo ezingaphezulu ezingaphezulu.
The rules and procedures for suspension or suspension of the statute of limitations shall be determined by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 214. Responsibilities of the Governor or the Registrar or Proprietors
If the Governor or the librarian or the owner of any enterprise knows or intends to cause the enterprise not to report or report tax in violation of tax regulations or not to pay withholding tax to the Fiscal Administration, the Governor or the librarian or owner of such enterprise shall be directly responsible for the tax payable.

Article 215. Business transfer or stock transfer and enterprise merger
1- In case of business transfer or transfer of shares, the new owner shall be responsible for all tax liabilities of the business or enterprise.
2- In case of dissolution of two (two) or more enterprises, the enterprises that continue or arise from the dissolution of two (two) or more enterprises shall be responsible for all tax liabilities.

Article 216 . Tax Debt Reminder Letter and Tax Debt Reminder Letter
1. As provided in paragraph 4 of Article 211 of this Law, the Fiscal Administration shall send a notice of tax debt to the taxpayer stating the amount of tax, additional tax, interest and monetary penalty.
2. In case the taxpayer fails to pay the tax debt as provided in Paragraph 1 of this Article, the Fiscal Administration shall send a letter of reminder of the tax debt to the taxpayer.
3. The Fiscal Administration may take strict measures as provided in Articles 217, 218, 220, 221 and 222 of this Law at least 15 (fifteen) days after the delivery of the Notice of Reminder of Tax Debt as provided in Paragraph 2 of this Article.

Article 217. Right to detain, seize and seize assets of taxpayers
The right to detain, seize and seize the assets of the taxpayer is defined as follows:
1- If an individual who is obliged to pay taxes as required by the provisions of the tax regulations is negligent or refuses to pay taxes after the notice of tax collection is duly handed over, the Fiscal Administration has the right to detain, seize and seize the individual's assets at an appropriate value level with respect to the tax debt.
The Fiscal Administration shall send a notice of tax debt reminder to the taxpayer at least 15 (fifteen) days before implementing the strict measures as provided in Articles 218, 220, 221 and 222 of this Law.
2. The right to detain, seize and seize the property of the taxpayer arises on the date on which the notice of reminder of tax debt is handed over to the taxpayer as provided in Article 198 of this Law.
3. Provided that all the conditions of this Article have been duly fulfilled, the right to detain, seize and seize assets as provided for in paragraph 1 of this Article shall prevail and take precedence over all other rights that existed before or which arose after the right to detain, seize and seize the assets of the taxpayer, unless otherwise provided for in the Bankruptcy Law and the regulations relating to the right to property. All rights established on the assets of the taxpayer that are detained, seized and detained by the fiscal administration after the date of the public announcement of the fiscal administration cannot be brought against the priority rights of the fiscal administration over the assets. Forms and procedures for public announcement of assets of taxpayers to be detained, seized and seized and the fiscal administration shall be determined by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.
4-The key to custody, supervision and maintenance of this property is the burden of the taxpayer.
5. Any person may lodge a complaint with the Fiscal Administration to request for the lifting of the right to detain, seize and seize his/her property as provided in paragraph 1 of this Article, citing the mistake in granting that right.
If the Fiscal Administration finds that the imposition of the right to detain, seize and detain the property is erroneous, the Fiscal Administration shall issue a certificate of the right to detain, seize and detain the property within 10 (ten) days after the inspection as well as sign in the letter of intent that the right to detain, seize and detain the property is erroneous.

Article 218. Right of use and dependency, right of temporary assignment and forfeiture
The right of use and dependency, the right of temporary disposal and confiscation of assets, the taxpayer is defined as follows:
1- In case of necessity and in order to ensure the payment of tax debts, the fiscal administration has the right to use and depend on the assets of the detained taxpayers.
2- Apart from the right of use and dependency as provided in Paragraph 1 of this Article, the Fiscal Administration may appeal to the court to confiscate the taxpayer's assets for the purpose of ensuring the payment of tax debts. And the money derived from the temporary allocation is to be stored in a temporary account of the fiscal administration.
3. A person who has the task of possessing and managing the property of a taxpayer who is confiscated by the Fiscal Administration as provided in Paragraph 2 of this Article may not return such property to the taxpayer or take such property to make other payments, except for the payment authorized by the Fiscal Administration.
4. For cash assets, the Fiscal Administration may confiscate the cash of the taxpayer or the cash that the taxpayer will receive without having to follow the procedures as provided in the second paragraph of this Article.

Article 219 . Assignment of confiscated property
In case of sale of assets after the seizure of the taxpayer's assets, the amount sold in excess of the taxpayer's tax liabilities under this Act shall be returned to the taxpayer, unless otherwise disposed of by a court in accordance with applicable law.

Article 220.. Bank Account Hold
1. The Fiscal Administration may detain the account of the taxpayer at the Bank in accordance with the notification letter of the Fiscal Administration and which shall take effect immediately after the handing over of the letter to the Bank.
2- Through the notice of withholding of the bank account, the Bank cannot open a new account for the same taxpayer nor can make any other payments from that account, except for the deduction of money determined by the Fiscal Administration to pay the tax payable, additional tax, interest and other monetary fines.
3. The detained bank account can be reopened unless there is a notification letter from the Fiscal Administration.
4. Banks that fail to comply with the notification letter in paragraph 1 of this Article shall be responsible to the Fiscal Administration for the amount available in the taxpayer's account when the notification letter is handed over.

Article 221.. Suspension of import and export operations
1. The Fiscal Administration may suspend export-import operations.
2. The Fiscal Administration may confiscate, use, depend on and temporarily dispose of the goods of the taxpayer detained by the Customs Administration in accordance with the conditions as provided in Article 218 of this Law.
3. The permission for import and export operations to cease and desist shall comply with the notification letter of the Fiscal Administration.
4. Goods detained by the Customs Administration that do not belong to the taxpayer shall be released from detention with the consent of the Fiscal Administration.

Article 222 . . Invalidation of Permits and Licenses
The Fiscal Administration may issue a notice to the competent authority requesting the annulment of the taxpayer's various permits and licenses to carry out any activity.

Article 223. Negligence
A taxpayer or withholding agent is considered negligent if the amount of tax paid is less than the amount of tax prescribed by the tax regulations not exceeding 10 (ten) percent or has not paid the tax by the date specified by the law or other customs norms.

Article 224 Gross negligence
A taxpayer or withholding agent is considered to be seriously negligent if the amount of tax paid is less than the amount of tax prescribed by the tax regulations by more than 10 (ten) percent.

Article 225. Obstruction of the implementation of tax regulations
is considered as an offense to obstruct the implementation of tax regulations for offenses committed contrary to the provisions of this Law and other relevant customs norms as follows:
1. Failure to register at the Fiscal Administration in accordance with the provisions of this Law and other relevant customs norms.
2- Failure to notify the Fiscal Administration of the change in registration information.
3- Failure to submit a fiscal declaration letter.
4- Failure to use the recording system set by the Fiscal Administration.
5- Non-invoicing.
6- Failure to provide information or submit reports as requested.
7- Refusal to allow the Fiscal Administration to conduct an audit of accounting books or other documents.
8- Failure to keep a list of accounts and other documents.
9- Attempting to obstruct the determination and collection of taxes.
10- Creating or providing false records, documents, reports or information.
11- Concealment or intentional destruction of accounting records, records, documents, reports or other information.
12- Fraudulent invoicing.
13- Not allowing the fiscal administration to enter business establishments to determine and collect taxes.

Article 226.. Tax evasion
1- Tax evasion is any crime committed intentionally and premeditatedly leading to the loss of the tax amount required by the tax regulations.
2- It is also considered as tax evasion in any of the following cases:
a. Gross negligence as provided in Article 224 of this Law, which is committed twice separately within three (three) calendar years.
b- Gross negligence as provided for in Article 224 of this Law, which is committed three or more separate times within 10 (ten) years of a calendar year.

Article 227. Causes of Dismissal of Prosecution
1- Coordination with the Fiscal Administration through the payment of taxes, additional taxes and interest leading to prosecution for criminal offences on the provisions on taxation.
2. The provisions of paragraph 1 of this Article shall not apply to criminal offences punishable by other criminal laws.

Article 228.. Ability to build a criminal case
1. The Fiscal Administration is the only institution competent to investigate and build cases related to criminal offences under the provisions on taxation, in accordance with this Law and the Code of Criminal Procedure of the Kingdom of Cambodia.
2- The Fiscal Administration may also have the capacity to investigate and build cases involving other criminal offences involving criminal offences on tax regulations, if authorized by the Public Prosecutor.

Article 229. Judicial Officer Rehabilitation of Tax Officers
1. The tax officer in charge of the judicial administration and the judicial administration agent shall examine the offenses on the tax regulations.
2. The form and procedure of granting rehabilitation to tax officials shall be determined by the inter-ministerial announcement of the Minister of Justice and the Minister of Economy and Finance.
3- All transactions of tax officials involving criminal offenses on tax regulations shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of the Criminal Procedure Code.

Article 230 . The power to investigate
The tax officer has the following powers to investigate:
1- The tax officer shall have the authority to enter a business establishment or a place which is deemed to be a business institution to examine the accounting lists, fiscal declarations of all kinds and other relevant documents for the purpose of determining taxes.
2- A tax officer who has lawfully entered a business establishment or place which is considered a business institution as provided for in paragraph 1 of this Article has the right to:
a. Make quotations or copies of any documents, including electronic documents located in that place;
b. Capture documents or other evidence that may become information or evidence for determining the tax payable of any person by making a record of the seizure.
c. Put up various inspection devices or stamp and detain goods if there is any involvement in the implementation of any tax.
d. Inventory assets, raw materials, products in production, finished products, and other stocks/agreements.
d- Seize, detain or seize the taxpayer's assets to secure tax debts.
Detain taxpayers who commit criminal offences against tax regulations in accordance with the Code of Criminal Procedure of the Kingdom of Cambodia.
3. In all cases, when a criminal offence under the provisions on taxation is detected within the framework of the investigation of the tax officer, the operation of the tax officer involving the collection of evidence, the making of records and the execution of all other necessary criminal procedures, including the detention of suspects, shall be conducted by a tax officer who is qualified as an officer or an agent of justice and shall be carried out in accordance with the Code of Criminal Procedure of the Kingdom of Cambodia.
4. The Fiscal Administration may require banking institutions located in the Kingdom of Cambodia to provide information about the accounts of taxpayers or related persons at the Bank or detain the accounts of such taxpayers or related persons in case there is evidence of tax evasion.
5- During the investigation, the tax officer must behave appropriately to avoid harming the honor and business of the taxpayer.

Article 231. Types of Administrative Actions
1- The administrative acts prescribed in this Law include additional taxes, interest, monetary fines, suspension or revocation of licenses, temporary closure of businesses and other administrative acts prescribed by the Proclamation of the Minister of Economy and Finance.
2- Decision on the imposition of administrative sanctions as the competence of the Fiscal Administration.

Article 232. Application of additional taxes
1. Additional tax shall apply to offenses related to tax regulations.
2- Additional tax for underpayment or late payment of taxes shall be calculated separately from monetary fines for committing acts of obstruction of the implementation of tax regulations.
3. In case of underpayment, additional tax and interest are due and payable in the same manner as the underpaid tax is applied.
4. In any case, the imposition of additional taxes does not affect the implementation of the tariffs.

Article 233. Additional taxes and interest
Additional taxes and interest are set as follows:
1. For a person who commits a negligent offense as provided in Article 223 of this Law, the additional tax amount shall be equal to 10 (ten) percent of the amount of tax paid in arrears or late payment, plus an additional interest of 1.5 (one and five) percent of the amount of tax paid in arrears for each month or the portion of the month in which the amount of tax is not yet paid.
2. For a person who commits serious negligence as provided for in Article 224 of this Law, the additional tax amount shall be equal to 25 (twenty-five) percent of the amount of tax paid in shortfall, plus an additional interest of 1.5 (one comma five) percent of the amount of tax paid in arrears for each month or the portion of the month in which the tax amount is not yet paid.
3. In case of unilateral taxation, the additional tax shall be equal to 40 (forty) percent of the amount of tax underpaid, plus an additional interest of 1.5 (one comma five) percent of the amount of tax underpaid for each month or the portion of the month in which the tax is unpaid.
4. In case of unilateral determination of tax for non-filing of a declaration, the additional tax amount shall be equal to 40 (forty) percent of the determined tax amount, plus an additional interest of 1.5 (one comma five) percent of the determined tax amount for each month or the portion of the month in which the tax amount has not yet been paid.
5. If an individual fails to pay tax within 15 (fifteen) days after receiving the notice of reminder of tax liability, the additional tax shall be determined at the rate of 25 (twenty-five) percent of the late tax amount plus 1.5 (one comma five) percent of the late tax amount for each month or the portion of the month in which the tax amount has not yet been paid.
6. Additional tax on late payment of tax on means of transport and stamp duty shall be equal to 100 (one hundred) percent of the tax payable.
Interest shall not be applied during the re-determination period under Article 211 of this Law or within 30 (thirty) days after the delivery of the notice of tax debt under Article 213 of this Law.

Article 234- Written warning
shall give a written warning by the Fiscal Administration to any person who commits an offense obstructing the implementation of any tax regulations as provided in Paragraph 1, Paragraph 2 and Paragraph 3 of Article 225 of this Law.

Article 235 . . Monetary fines for obstructing the implementation of tax regulations
Monetary fines for obstructing the implementation of tax regulations are set as follows:
1. To impose a fine of KHR 5,000,000 (five million) by the Fiscal Administration, in addition to other administrative acts, against any person who has received a written warning from the Fiscal Administration more than two (2) times and still commits an act of obstructing the implementation of any tax regulations as provided in Paragraph 1, Paragraph 2 and Paragraph 3 of Article 225 of this Law.
2. To impose a fine of 10,000,000 (ten million) riels by the Fiscal Administration, in addition to other administrative acts, against any person who commits an offense obstructing the implementation of any tax regulation as provided in Paragraph 4, Paragraph 5, Paragraph 6, Paragraph 7 and Paragraph 8 of Article 225 of this Law.
3. In case a person who has already been ordered to pay a fine as provided in Paragraph 1 or Paragraph 2 of this Article and that person has committed an offence of obstructing the implementation of any tax regulation as provided in Paragraph 1, Paragraph 2, Paragraph 3, Paragraph 4, Paragraph 5, Paragraph 6, Paragraph 7 and Paragraph 8 of Article 225 of this Law, that person shall be subject to criminal offenses as provided in Article 225 of this Law.

Article 236 ... Rules of Administrative Complaint
The rules for resolving taxpayers' complaints about fiscal issues are set out as follows:
1 - Taxpayers who do not agree with the resetting, monetary fines or other decisions made by competent entities of the Fiscal Administration may lodge a complaint with the Director General of the General Department of Taxation.
2. Administrative complaints shall be made in writing in the form as provided in Article 237 of this Law and shall be submitted to the Fiscal Administration within 30 (thirty) days after the date on which the taxpayer receives the notice of tax liability, monetary fine or other decision made by the competent entity of the Fiscal Administration.
3. Administrative complaints do not exempt the taxpayer from the obligation to pay taxes, additional taxes, interest and other monetary fines specified in the tax debt notice, monetary fines and other rulings made by the competent entities of the fiscal administration.

Article 237. Contents of the taxpayer's administrative complaint
1- An administrative complaint may be acceptable if the complaint contains the following contents:
A identification number of the taxpayer making the complaint.
b- References to the determination of the ruling or outcome that is the subject of the complaint.
c- The cause or sin that is the subject of the complaint.
d- Reasons for the protest.
d- Date and signature of the taxpayer and signature of the taxpayer's legal representative.
2 - The rules and procedures for handling complaints shall be determined by the announcement of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 238. Decision of the Fiscal Administration
1. The Fiscal Administration shall re-issue a decision within 60 (sixty) days after the date of receipt of the complaint to confirm the accuracy or inaccuracy in whole or in any part of the tax determination or other decisions complained by the taxpayer.
2- If the taxpayer disagrees with the new decision of the Fiscal Administration, the taxpayer may lodge a complaint with the Fiscal Dispute Settlement Committee within 30 (thirty) days after the date of receipt of the decision.

Article 239. Fiscal Dispute Settlement Committee
1. To establish a Fiscal Dispute Settlement Committee, tasked with examining and resolving complaints of taxpayers who are dissatisfied with the decisions or final measures of the General Department of Taxation related to tax disputes.
2 - The organization and conduct of the Fiscal Dispute Settlement Committee shall be determined by a decree at the request of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 240. Complaint to the Court
1. The taxpayer has the right to appeal to the competent court to object to the decision of the Fiscal Dispute Settlement Committee within 30 (thirty) days at the latest after receiving the notice of the decision.
2. The taxpayer shall deposit in the National Treasury money or assets of at least equivalent value equal to the amount of tax involved in the dispute before filing a complaint with the court.

Article 241. Implementation of the ruling on monetary fines
1. The Fiscal Administration may exercise its authority as prescribed in this Law to ensure the efficiency of the implementation of the ruling on monetary fines when the decision becomes official.
2. In case of necessity and in order to ensure the effectiveness of the implementation of the ruling on monetary fines, the provisions of Chapter 1 (General Provisions) of Contents 1 (General Provisions) and Chapter 3 (Physical Coercion) of Article 3 (Physical Coercion) of Article 8 of the Criminal Procedure Code shall be applied in cases where the decision on monetary fines has been enforced.

Article 242.. Tax evasion offenses
Without regard to other criminal offences, the governor, secretary, employee owner of any enterprise or the person responsible for any enterprise who commits tax evasion as provided for in Article 226 of this Law shall be sentenced to imprisonment from 1 (one) year to 5 (five) years and a fine of between 100,000,000 (one hundred million) and 200,000,000 (two hundred million) KHR.

Article 243. Offences obstructing the implementation of tax regulations
Excluding other criminal offences, the offender shall be sentenced to imprisonment from 1 (one) month to 1 (one) year and a fine of between KHR 50,000,000 (fifty million) and KHR 100,000,000 (one hundred million) to any person who commits an offence obstructing the implementation of any tax regulation as follows:
1- Trying to block the setting and collection of taxes.
2- Create or provide false records, documents, reports, or information.
3- Concealing or deliberately destroying accounting lists, records, documents, reports or other information.
4- Issue fraudulent invoices.
5- Do not allow the tax administration to enter business establishments to determine and collect taxes.

Article 244.Leakage of secrets
Regardless of other criminal offences, any person who leaks the confidentiality of tax information in violation of Article 197 of this Law shall be punished with imprisonment from 1 (one) month to (one) year and a fine of between 50 000 000 (fifty million) and 100 000 000 (one hundred million) riels.

Article 245.. Practicing as a tax service agent without a license
Not to mention other criminal offences, a person who practices as a tax service agent without a license shall be sentenced to imprisonment from 1 (one) month to 1 (one) year and a fine of between 10,000,000 (ten million) and 20,000,000 (twenty million) KHR.

Article 246. Failure to pay collected taxes
Excluding other criminal offences, a person who fails to pay the collected tax shall be sentenced to imprisonment from 1 (one) year to 3 (three) years and a fine of between 50 000 000 (fifty million) and 100 000 000 (one hundred million) KHR.

Article 247. Collection of tax money that is not eligible to be collected
Without regard to other criminal offences, a person who collects tax money without obtaining the right from the State or permission in accordance with the provisions of this Law or other competent customs norms shall be sentenced to imprisonment from one (one) year to three (three) years and a fine of between 50 000 000 (fifty million) and 100 000 000 (one hundred million) rials.

Article 248. Administrative Responsibilities of Tax Officers
Any tax officer who violates the provisions of this Act and other relevant regulations in the performance of his or her functions and duties shall be subject to administrative sanctions in accordance with the law and other applicable customs norms.

Article 249. Individual Responsibilities
1. An individual may be declared criminally responsible as provided for in Article 42 (Criminal Liability of an individual) of the Criminal Code for the offences provided for in Articles 242, 243, 245, 246, 247 and 250 of this Law.
2. Individuals who commit the offenses as prescribed in Article 242 of this Law shall be punished with a fine of between 100,000,000 (one hundred million) and 200,000,000 (two hundred million) riels.
3. Individuals who commit the offenses as provided in Article 243, Article 246 and Article 257 of this Law shall be punished with a fine of between 50 000 000 000 (fifty million riels to 100 000 000 000 (one hundred million) riels.
4. Individuals who commit the offenses as provided for in Article 245 of this Law shall be punished with a fine of between 10,000,000 (ten million) and 20,000,000 (twenty million) riels.
5. Individuals who commit the offenses as provided for in Article 250 of this Law shall be punished with a fine of between 50,000,000 (fifty million) and 200,000,000 (two hundred million) riels.
6. An individual may be sentenced to any or more additional penalties as provided in Article 168 (Additional Penalties Applicable to Individuals) of the Criminal Code of the Kingdom of Cambodia.

Article 250. Responsibilities of Initiators and Conspirators
An initiator or conspirator who has the intent of aiding, inducing, inducing or inciting another person to commit a criminal offence under the provisions of this Law and other relevant customs norms shall be punished in the same manner as a chari.

Article 251.. Corruption offences
1. Offences as provided for in paragraph 3 of Article 243, Article 246 and Article 247 of this Law and committed by public prosecutors or citizens who hold public office by election shall be designated as corrupt offences punishable under the Anti-Corruption Act and shall be subject to the sole exclusive competence of the Anti-Corruption Unit in investigating and building corruption cases to the courts.
2- Investigation of corruption offences in the field of taxation and building cases of corruption in this field to the courts are the exclusive competence of the Anti-Corruption Unit, in accordance with the Law on Anti-Corruption.

Article 252. Enforcement of other criminal laws
The application of the provisions of Chapter 18 of this Law does not preclude the enforcement of other criminal laws in cases of offences defined as offences as provided for in this Law as offences prescribed in other criminal laws.

Article 253.Interregulatory
All Customs Norms promulgated on the basis of the Law on Taxation promulgated by Royal Decree No. Nos/Krom/0297/03 dated 24 February 1997 and the Law on Amendments to the Law on Taxation promulgated by Royal Decree No. 033/010 dated 31 March 2003 and subsequent amendments shall have the effect of continuing to apply until replaced by a new Letter of Customs Regulation in accordance with the provisions of this Act.

Article 254. Nirvana
The Law on Taxation promulgated by Royal Decree No. NS/KROM/0297/03 dated 24 February 1997 and the Law on Amendments to the Law on Taxation promulgated by Royal Decree No. NS/KROM/0303/010 dated 31 March 2003 and any provisions contrary to this Law shall be set aside.
