Article 1 
The decree aims to set out the rules and procedures of administering VAT collection on value-added.

Article 2 
The Decree has the scope to apply to the VAT supply of goods or services within the Kingdom of Cambodia.

Article 3 
For the purposes of this decree:
1- Commodity refers to physical assets other than land and money.
2-Service refers to the provision of something of value other than goods, land, and money.
3- Supply of goods refers to the transfer of a right of use or assignment in the status of ownership of goods with or without compensation.
4- Supply of services refers to a supply that is not a supply of goods, land or money made for the receipt of compensation or no compensation.
5- Individual refers to an individual or group of individuals who conducts business and any other person who is associated with that person.
6- VAT-liable persons refer to persons who are subject to VAT taxation and make VAT-liable supplies as provided in Article 59 of the Law on Fiscal Affairs. For the purposes of this Decree, a non-profit person who supplies digital goods or digital services into the Kingdom of Cambodia shall be considered a VAT-liable person.
7- VAT Yield refers to the profit derived from the VAT supply of goods or services. 
8- As an individual, it means:
a- Any person owning 20 (twenty) percent or more of the value or voting rights of the shares in the direct capital of the person under consideration.
b- Have joint management or have a joint director with the individual.
c- As a family member or as a federation or as a family member of the individual's federation. 
D-Purchased 30 (thirty) percent or more of the individual's total output items in the 3B period.
9- Digital goods refer to supernatural goods that are ordered, supplied and transmitted entirely electronically.
10-Digital services refer to services that are transacted electronically.
11-Electronic commerce refers to the activity of buying, selling, renting, exchanging goods or services, including commercial and civil activities, as well as various activities and transactions of the State electronically.
12-Alternative VAT method refers to the method by which an individual receiving a supply of goods or services is subject to VAT on behalf of the person making the VAT supply.
13-VAT in the two chapters of this Decree refers to VAT on value-added.

Article 4 
1. An automated taxpayer who has made the supply of VAT as provided in Article 59 of the Law on Fiscal Affairs shall submit an application to the General Department of Taxation for the proper registration of VAT within 15 days after the date on which such person becomes a VAT person as provided in Article 77 of the Law on Fiscal Taxation.
2-Every non-permanent taxpayer in the Kingdom of Cambodia who conducts trade electronically is obliged to register VAT on simple value-added based on the taxpayer rank as determined by the proclamation of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 5 
1- Persons who have registered VAT on value-added shall be required to obtain a VAT registration certificate on value-added containing a fiscal identification number and the effective date of registration. 
2- The registered VAT assessee shall furnish or hang the registration certificate issued at his principal place of business.

Article 6
Individuals who owe tax must request in writing to the General Department of Taxation to cancel its registration of taxation.
If that person ceases to supply goods or services with value, which is a portion of its business activities.

Article 7 
The Directorate General of Taxation has the right to cancel the registration of:
1- The person requested the deletion pursuant to Article 6 of this Decree.
2. An individual who has not requested the deregistration of the Inspector General of Taxation is of the opinion that such person has no requirement or right to register under Article 4 of this Decree.
3-Individuals who have not applied for cancellation of registration but have not declared VAT supply within three consecutive calendar months.

Article 8
The General Department of Taxation shall notify in writing the taxpayer of the decision to approve or disagree to the cancellation of registration pursuant to Article 6 of this Decree within 30 days after receipt of the application for cancellation of registration or within 30 days after the decision to cancel the registration pursuant to paragraphs 2 and 3 of Article 7 of this Decree.

Article 9 
When a VAT-taxed individual is removed from the list pursuant to this chapter, the VAT-taxed individual is deemed to have made a VAT supply of all goods on hand, including assets, and is responsible for paying VAT on all goods for which VAT credit has already been received on the entry.

Article 10 
The cancellation of the individual's registration has an impact on the debt obligations and the individual's debt obligations as stipulated in the Law and the Letter of Incorporation on Taxation, including the requirement to file a declaration letter in accordance with Article 71 of the Fiscal Law, which the individual did or did not do when he or she was a tax-bearing individual.

Article 11 
The VAT credit on inputs when an individual is registered as a VAT lien is defined as follows:
 1- A VAT person is allowed a VAT credit on inputs, paid or payable on the supply, VAT on all goods, including capital assets, which the individual received prior to registration.
 2. The conditions of credit authorization are defined as follows:
A- Goods are purchased for VAT sales or for use to make VAT-taxed supplies of VAT-taxed persons.
b- Goods listed on the inventory list shall be in hand on the effective date of listing. c- Those supplies or imports are made no later than 60 days prior to the effective date of listing.
d-Credit applications are made in accordance with the format prescribed by the General Department of Taxation.
d- There shall be a clear and accurate document of proof to the Directorate of Taxation stating that the person has paid the actual VAT that may be credited.

Article 12 
1. When a VAT-indebted individual calculates the VAT payable in a month, the VAT-indebted individual is allowed to credit only the VAT paid on:
a- Any VAT supplies received by the VAT individual within a month or at least 60 days after receipt of the supplies.
b- Any importation of goods by an individual subject to VAT within a month or at the latest 60 days after importation.
2. VAT credit on inputs shall occur at the following times:
a- When goods or services are supplied to a VAT debtor or imported by a VAT-debted person. b- When a VAT-taxed person is registered, in the case of VAT credit as provided in Article 11 of this Decree.
VAT credits are permitted only to VAT supplies or imports for use to make
VAT supplies only.

Article 13 
VAT taxpayers are not allowed to credit VAT on inputs to VAT paid on: 
1- Hospitality, entertainment, or leisure expenses, unless the person engages in business as a supplier of reception, entertainment, or leisure.
2- Purchase or importation of vehicles, except for persons engaged in VAT as sellers or leasers of vehicles.
3-Purchase or importation of certain tella products, except for persons engaged in business as suppliers of those telco products.
4. For the purposes of this Article:
A- Reception refers to the supply of food, drink, tobacco, shelter, or hospitality.
B- Vehicle refers to a person-only vehicle with no more than 10 seats.
C- Polyester products refer to regular gasoline, soup gasoline, diesel fuel, and lubricants.

Article 14 
In case the goods or services purchased are used one share as a VAT-taxable supply and the other share as a non-VAT-liable supply, VAT credit on inputs is allowed only to the portion used as a VAT-liable supply.  VAT on inputs used for non-VAT supplies is not allowed as VAT on inputs.

Article 15 
1. In case the VAT on inputs in the VAT period cannot be divided between the VAT and non-VAT-liable supplies, the amount of VAT credit on the inputs that can be given shall be calculated according to the formula A x B/C.
A = Total amount of VAT on inputs during the VAT period.
B = The total untaxed value of the VAT supplies made by the VAT debted persons during the VAT period.
c = Total VAT-free value of VAT and non-VAT supplies made by individuals
Subject to VAT for the VAT period, except for the value of the non-VAT-liable supply of the transfer of the business.
2- In case the fraction B/C is worth less than 0.05, the VAT debtor is not allowed VAT credit on the entries in the VAT period.
3-In case the fraction B/C is worth more than 0.95, the VAT debtor is allowed VAT credit on all entries in the VAT period.
4- In case the fraction B/C has a value ranging from 0.05 to 0.95, the person subject to VAT is allowed to credit VAT on inputs in proportion to the formula as provided in paragraph 1 of this article.
The value of the fraction b/c is set to two digits after the middle with no upward alignment.

Article 16 
In the event that a VAT debtor makes a VAT-taxed supply and a non-VAT-taxed supply, there are consequences due to the compliance with paragraph 1 of Article 15 of this Decree, the VAT debtor may take the following other way to calculate VAT on deductible inputs:
1- Allocate VAT on inputs of VAT supplies and VAT on inputs of non-VAT supplies, where possible.
 2- For VAT on the remaining non-divisible inputs, VAT credits shall be calculated in accordance with paragraph 1 of Article 15 of this Decree.

Article 17 
In the first month of the next calendar year, the VAT-paying person who has calculated VAT on the entries pursuant to paragraph 1, Article 15 and paragraph 2 of Article 16 of this Decree shall make the calculation of the deductible VAT credit for the past calendar year according to the formula in paragraph 1 of Article 15 of this Decree, based on the annual total amount of:
1- VAT on non-divisible items.
2- Supply subject to VAT.
3- VAT-liable supplies and non-VAT-liable supplies, except for non-VAT-liable supplies of business transfers.

Article 18 
1. In case the calendar year VAT credit amounts to:
a- More than the VAT credit in the declaration letter, the balance shall be treated as a VAT credit for the first month of the next calendar year.
b- Less than the VAT credit in the declaration letter, the balance shall be treated as a VAT debit payable through the VAT declaration letter for the first month of the next calendar year.
2- For the purposes of this Article:
A- Calendar Annual VAT Credit refers to the VAT on the total deductible inputs for the calendar year, based on the annual total calculation.
b- VAT credit in the declaration letter refers to the VAT on the total input requested as a credit in each month of the calendar year.
c-VAT debit refers to the calendar year VAT credit less than the VAT credit in the declaration letter. d-Balance refers to the proportional amount of calendar annual VAT credit and VAT credit in the declaration letter.

Article 19 
In order to apply for VAT credit on deductible entries pursuant to the provisions of this Decree, a VAT holder must:
1. The original copy of the VAT invoice issued by the person employed as the supplier.
2- Import customs receipts and tax payment receipts as proof of VAT paid on imports of goods.

Article 20 
VAT refund on excess inputs is determined as follows:
1- A VAT-paying person who makes an export as provided in Article 73 and Article 74 of the Law on Fiscal Affairs, such person may request a refund of VAT credit on excess inputs every month.
2. For a VAT debtor who has already requested a VAT credit refund on excess inputs but has not declared a VAT supply, the Directorate General of Taxation is not required to make a refund.
3. VAT refund on excess inputs shall be determined by the proclamation of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 21 
The use of VAT invoices shall be carried out as follows:
1- A VAT-taxed person who supplies goods or services is required to invoice VAT to a buyer who is a taxpayer, as per the automatic declarant regime, and shall issue regular invoicing to a buyer who is not subject to the autonomous regime.
 2- The person receiving the supply shall require the VAT person who supplies the goods or services to provide an invoice of that supply.
3-A VAT-debted person engaged in the supply of goods or services shall maintain the original copy of the VAT invoice or regular invoice and other documents issued to the customer.
4. VAT invoices or ordinary invoices must be in accordance with the invoice rules prescribed by the proclamation of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 22 
Supplies are not subject to foreign diplomatic and consular missions, international organizations, or cooperative agencies
Other government techniques are defined as follows:
1. Importation or domestic purchase of goods or services by foreign diplomatic and consular missions, international organizations, and
Technical cooperation agencies of other governments, for use in the fulfilment of their official functions, shall be defined as VAT-free supplies. Non-VAT-liable supplies shall be provided only in cases where there is a specification, from the Head of Mission to the Fiscal Administration, that the importation or domestic purchase of such goods or services for the purpose of the above use only.
2. The importation or purchase of domestic goods or services for the personal use of official personnel of foreign missions, diplomats and consulates, international organizations and other governmental technical cooperation agencies as provided in paragraph 1 of this article, shall be defined as the non-taxable supply of goods or services listed in the list of goods or services prescribed by the proclamation of the Minister of Economy and Finance.
 3. The supply not subject to VAT in this Article shall stand on the exclusion policy between the concerned Governments.

Article 23 -
The place of supply is defined as follows:
1- The supply of goods shall be deemed to have been made in the Kingdom of Cambodia if the goods are delivered to the Kingdom of Cambodia if the goods are in the Kingdom of Cambodia when the shipment is commenced.
2- The supply of services is considered to have been made in the Kingdom of Cambodia if the service has been fulfilled in the Kingdom of Cambodia unless:
a- The provision of services in connection with the property shall be determined that the service took place at the place where the property is located.
b- The supply of the service in connection with the delivery shall be determined that the service took place at the place of the delivery.
3. For services supplied in the Kingdom of Cambodia by immigrant individuals, the VAT-debted person who is the recipient of the supply shall charge VAT on behalf of the supplier and pay VAT to the Fiscal Administration if the supplier does not have a permanent establishment in the Kingdom of Cambodia.
4. Goods are considered to have been brought into the Kingdom of Cambodia if the goods are imported into the Kingdom of Cambodia.
Customs of the Kingdom of Cambodia

Article 24 
In the event that a VAT individual mixes supplies between goods and services, those supplies are limited
As follows:
1- The supply of secondary services, which, together with the supply of goods, is a share of the supply of goods.
2- The supply of secondary goods which, together with the supply of services, is a share of the supply of services. 
3- The supply of secondary services which, together with imports, are a share of imports.

Article 25 
The time of supply is determined as follows to calculate the VAT for each VAT period that the VAT holder must declare to be paid to the General Department of Taxation:
1. The time of supply of goods or services is defined as follows:
a- When a supplier supplies goods or services is when a supplier is billed or when a supplier has
The supplier shall invoice no later than 7 days after the delivery of the goods or the fulfillment of the service or after the payment in case the payment is made prior to the delivery of the goods or the fulfillment of the service.
b- In case the goods are taken for personal use, the time of supply is when the goods are disposed of.
Taken to early use.
c- In case the goods or services are supplied in the form of a gift, the time of supply is when the goods are delivered in such a manner as a transfer of use or assignment rights or when the services supplied are completed.
2- When supplying goods under a lease contract with a detached purchase clause or financial obligation, is when
The goods are delivered to the property as a transfer of use or assignment rights.
3- Goods or services shall be deemed to have been ready supplied to the ready supplied share within the period prescribed by law or the period prescribed by law and the time of supply of each ready supplied share is the earlier date on which the payment is due and the date on which the payment is received.
When supplied, as provided in this paragraph, applies to goods being supplied under a lease contract or goods or services being supplied under a contract or rule providing for overpayment, or services being supplied continuously.
4. For the import of goods, the time of supply is when the importer submits a declaration to the Customs Administration in accordance with applicable laws and customs regulations.

Article 26 
The VAT value of the supply is determined as follows:
1- VAT value of a supply is the cost of goods or services charged by a VAT debtor from a customer who is the purchaser.
2- In case the payment to the VAT supplies is compensation for anything other than the tariff to benefit, directly or indirectly, to the seller, that compensation shall be charged at the VAT value at the market price.
3. The VAT value of imported goods is the value subject to customs duties, including customs duties and VAT at the time of importation.
4- If the VAT value of the goods or services supplied does not represent the true value, the General Department of Taxation may determine a price for the goods or services and that price shall be treated as valid until such other confirmatory evidence as the Fiscal Administration has agreed.
5- The VAT value of used goods, which a VAT debtor has purchased from a consumer to be sold on behalf of a consumer or sold on behalf of a consumer, is the amount between the selling price and the purchase price, or as a royalty derived from the sale of such goods.

Article 27
The VAT rate on value-added is determined as follows:
1. VAT on value-added shall be determined at the rate of 10 (ten) percent on the VAT value of each VAT supplied in the Kingdom of Cambodia.
2. VAT on value-added shall be determined at the rate of 0 (zero) percent on the VAT value of each VAT-taxed supply for goods exported from the Kingdom of Cambodia or the supply of VAT services fulfilled outside the Kingdom of Cambodia.

Article 28 
The rules and procedures for adjusting VAT after supply or at the time of billing are defined as follows:
1- A VAT-indebted person who has already invoiced or filed a monthly fiscal declaration letter may make a VAT adjustment if any of the following events occur:
  a- The supply has been canceled, or 
  b- The character of the supply has been varied or fundamentally altered, or
  c- The benefit for a previously agreed supply is modified by a new agreement with the supply recipient, by reason of a discount or by other reasons, or 
  d-The goods or any portion of the goods or packaging shells are sent back to the supplier or the service is not completed.
2. In case of any adjustment as provided for in paragraph 1 of this article, the person owed VAT shall make the adjustment of his VAT amount as follows:
  a- If the VAT on the adjusted exit item exceeds the VAT on the exit item recorded by the VAT-debted person, the excess amount is considered as the VAT collected by the VAT individual in the month in which the facts as specified in paragraph 1 of this article occurred.
  b- If the VAT on the adjusted issuance item is less than the VAT on the exit item to which the person owes the VAT recorded, the amount is treated as VAT credit for the month in which such facts as specified in paragraph 1 of this article occurred.
3. With respect to the supply to a person who is not a VAT debtor, excess VAT as provided for in Clause B of the second paragraph of this Article shall not be allowed as VAT credit unless the VAT debtor has proof of payment of the excess VAT to the recipient of the supply.
4- If the person owed VAT has already been invoiced, there is an adjustment of the VAT by fact, as provided in paragraph 1 of this article:
a- The amount of the adjusted VAT is less than the amount of VAT recorded in the invoice The person who owes VAT who supplies goods or services shall provide the recipient of the supply with a VAT credit letter as provided in Article 21 of this Decree.
b- The amount of adjusted VAT is more than the amount of VAT recorded in the invoice The person owed to VAT who supplies goods or services shall provide the recipient of the supply with a VAT debit letter as provided in Article 21 of this Decree.
5- A person employed by VAT as a supplier or a recipient of a supply who has issued or received a debit letter or VAT credit letter shall record in the journal the amount specified in the debit letter or VAT credit letter the same as recorded in the journal the amount of the VAT invoice.

Article 29 
1- The VAT debtor shall hold a record of the accounting list of all supplies made and received in the course of business, including VAT-taxed supplies at the rate of 0 (zero) per cent and non-VAT-liable supplies.
a- Monthly value-added VAT account stating VAT on gross output items, VAT on gross inputs, interest, VAT payable, or VAT credits on forward-looking or due to be refunded.
b- Purchase records detailing VAT-paid purchases and all VAT-free purchases
The original of the VAT invoice for the local purchase for which VAT has been paid, the import customs clerk certified by the Customs Administration showing the VAT paid and the VAT-free purchase invoice.
c- All sales records that include sales at the rate of 10 (ten) percent, rate 0 (zero) percent, and sales not subject to VAT.
d-Debit and letters of credit issued and received.
d- Records on every export of goods or services at a rate of 0 (zero) percent, as well as export customs records, original copies of invoices issued to foreign buyers, shipping documents for the export of goods, letters of purchase or contract with foreign buyers, and proof of payment by way of wire transfer through a bank registered in the Kingdom of Cambodia or by letter of credit.
- A record of the retailer's cash movements, which includes a bank statement and a list of money at banks, bills, bills, and other accounting records, including the original copy of the receipt or a detailed list of the amount of daily transactions.
C- Records in digital format if the taxpayer uses accounting lists by information technology systems.
- Details on the calculation of VAT on inputs in cases where VAT persons make VAT supplies
and non-VAT supply.

The Annual Accounting Report includes the Results Account, Balance Sheet, and Supplementary Information.
2. All records shall be made in accordance with the form prescribed or recognized by the General Department of Taxation and shall be kept in order of date and number respectively and prepared for inspection within 10 years.

Article 30 
1- A taxpayer who supplies goods or services to a taxpayer who is not a taxpayer under the decree shall hold a list of accounts and records as provided for in Article 29 of this Decree and shall follow the following procedures:
a- In the case of a regular invoice, if the VAT amount is specified on the invoice, the VAT due in the month shall be calculated from the sales record.
b- If on the invoice there is no separate VAT amount specified or the VAT person makes the sale.
In calculating VAT, the VAT gross value of the sales shall be multiplied by the VAT fraction.
The 2-fraction VAT for a rate of 10 (ten) percent is 1/11. 
3-To calculate the VAT value, take the total value of the sale, subtract the VAT.

Article 31 
The conditions of the supply of goods or services by an enterprise as an agent are defined as follows:
1- The supply of goods or services made by the enterprise as an agent for the benefit of the enterprise, the other being the original enterprise, is treated as the supply of that original enterprise.
2. An enterprise as an agent shall charge VAT on the revenues derived from the supply of goods or services to the original enterprise, and this VAT is VAT on the inputs of the original enterprise.
3-The rules and procedures for the implementation of this Article shall be determined by the proclamation of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 32 
The collection of VAT upon import is defined as follows:
1. VAT is due upon import and is collected by the Customs Administration and is treated in the same manner as customs duties.
2. The VAT value of the import of goods is the total amount of:
a- The value of goods for tax calculation in accordance with the Customs Act and the customs letter.
b- The amount of customs duties and VAT when imported other than VAT on value-added.
3. The Customs Administration shall provide the importer with an import customs declaration in which there shall be: 
A- Fiscal identification number if the importer is a VAT-taxed individual.
B- Write "None" in the box for the fiscal identification number if the importer is not a VAT-taxed person.
c- Customs tax receipt stating the amount of VAT paid.
d-Confirm the validity of the VAT refund if the importer is an individual subject to VAT.
d- Clarify the invalidity of the VAT refund if the importer is not a VAT-paying person.

Article 33 
The applicable domain of the 0 (zero) percent rate on the export of goods or services is defined as follows:
1. VAT on value-added shall be determined at the rate of 0 (zero) percent on the VAT value of each supply of goods exported from the Kingdom of Cambodia or the VAT supply of services fulfilled outside the Kingdom of Cambodia.
a- Supply of goods to anywhere outside the Kingdom of Cambodia.
b- Provision of services for use outside the Kingdom of Cambodia. 
c- Supply of international passenger and cargo transportation services.
d-Supply of services as it pertains to the international transportation of passengers and goods.
2- For the purposes of syntax C of paragraph 1 of this article, the transportation of passengers and goods by road, land, waterway or air is international transport if such transportation is made:
a- From one place in the Kingdom of Cambodia to another place outside the Kingdom of Cambodia.
b- From a place outside the Kingdom of Cambodia to a place in the Kingdom of Cambodia.
c- From a place outside the Kingdom of Cambodia to another place outside the Kingdom of Cambodia in case
Transportation or any share of transportation through the territory of the Kingdom of Cambodia.
3. The supply of goods or services as provided for in this article shall have sufficient documentary evidence that can be inspected.

Article 34 
A VAT-indebted person who ceases business shall submit an application to the Fiscal Administration in the form prescribed by the Fiscal Administration within 15 days following the cessation of business.

Article 35 
The transfer of business from one VAT-taxed individual to another person is not subject to VAT on value-added in the case of a transfer.
That is met under the following conditions:
1- The business is transferred from one taxpayer to another person in order to continue doing business under the new ownership.
2. A VAT debtor who transfers a business shall notify the General Department of Taxation of the business transfer within 15 days after the date of the transfer.
3-The person receiving the business is required to update the taxpayer's information when receiving the business and shall continue to apply VAT on value added to the goods and assets received at the time of supplying those goods and assets.
4. The person receiving the business shall retain the VAT documents associated with the transferred business for a period of 10 years.

Article 36
VAT on value added to electronic businesses, the terms of supply of digital goods or digital services are defined as follows:
1-Supply of goods or services from business to consumer is the supply of goods or services from a taxed person to a consumer.
2- Supply of goods or services from business to business is the supply of goods or services from an immigrant person or VAT debted person to a VAT-debted individual.

Article 37
Persons as specified in the second paragraph of Article 4 of this Decree, who have already registered additional VAT, shall have the following duties:
1. To collect VAT on the supply of digital goods or digital services to consumers as provided for in paragraph 1 of Article 36 of this Decree and to declare and pay VAT on the added value each month to the Fiscal Administration in accordance with applicable tax laws and customs, without allowing VAT credit on inputs.
2. The collection of VAT on the supply of digital goods or digital services to taxpayers shall not be made as provided for in the second paragraph of Article 36 of this Decree, but shall be made annually to the Fiscal Administration in accordance with the applicable tax rules and regulations.

Article 38 
Taxpayers who receive the supply of digital goods or digital services, or any electronic commerce activity from non-citizens, shall collect VAT in the manner of VAT in lieu of VAT and declare and pay VAT on the added value to the Fiscal Administration in accordance with applicable tax rules and customs.

Article 39 
The supply time is determined as follows:
1- For immigrant persons, as provided in Article 37 of this Decree, the time of supply is the time when the invoice is issued or when the digital goods are delivered or the digital services are fulfilled or the payment is received.
2-For taxpayers on the provisions of Article 38 of this Decree, the time of supply is the time when the digital goods are delivered or the digital services are fulfilled or the payment is due or paid.

Article 40 
The VAT paid by the taxpayer in the manner of alternate VAT as provided in Article 38 of this Decree is allowed as VAT credit on inputs.

Article 41 
The rules and procedures for the administration of VAT collection on the supply of digital goods or digital services or all electronic commercial activities into the Kingdom of Cambodia shall be determined by the proclamation of the Minister of Economy and Finance.

Article 42 
Any provisions contrary to this decree shall be set aside.

Article 43 
The Minister in charge of the Cabinet, the Minister of Economy and Finance, all Ministers and the Heads of all relevant institutions shall be in charge of implementing this Decree according to their respective duties from the signing date onwards 11 March 2024.
